question: Who among the following is known as the ‘Father of the Green Revolution’ in the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __Norman Borlaug.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Norman Borlaug:-

 
 
• The "Father of the Green Revolution" is typically attributed to an American agronomist named Norman Borlaug.
 
• Borlaug was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 in recognition of his contributions to world peace through increasing food supply.
 
• His pioneering work introducing high-yielding and disease-resistant wheat varieties combined with modern agricultural production techniques to Mexico, Pakistan, and India led these countries to greatly increase their food production and to serve as examples for the global Green Revolution.
 
• His work is estimated to have saved a billion people from starvation worldwide.
 
 
 
• Green Revolution:-
 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a series of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives, occurring between the 1950s and the late 1960s, that increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in the developing world.
 
• The term "Green Revolution" was first used in 1968 by former United States Agency for International Development (USAID) director William Gaud, who noted the spread of the new technologies and said, "These and other developments in the field of agriculture contain the makings of a new revolution.
 
• It is not a violent Red Revolution like that of the Soviets, nor is it a White Revolution like that of the Shah of Iran. I call it the Green Revolution."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Ralph Bunche:-

 
 
• He was an American political scientist, diplomat, and leading U.S. civil rights activist.
 
• He received the 1950 Nobel Peace Prize for his late 1940s mediation in Palestine.
 
• He was the first African American and person of color to be so honored in the history of the prize.
 
 
 
• Linus Carl Pauling:-
 
 
• He was an American chemist, biochemist, peace activist, author, and educator.
 
• He was one of the most influential chemists in history and is considered one of the greatest scientists of the 20th century.
 
• His work contributed significantly to the understanding of the nature of the chemical bond and the structure of molecules and crystals.
 
 
 
• Dr. M.S. Swaminathan:-
 
 
• He is an Indian geneticist and international administrator, renowned for his leading role in India's "Green Revolution," a program under which high-yield varieties of wheat and rice seedlings were planted in the fields of poor farmers.

question: The __________ is an Indian treatise on politics, economics, military strategy, the function of the state, and social organisation, attributed to Kautilya.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthashastra.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arthashastra** is an Indian treatise on politics, economics, military strategy, the function of the state, and social organization attributed to the philosopher and Prime Minister Kautilya (also known as Chanakya).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Chanakya also known as Vishnugupta, l. c. 350-275 BCE) was instrumental in establishing the reign of the great king Chandragupta Maurya (r. c. 321-c.297 BCE), founder of the Mauryan Empire (322-185 BCE). Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.
 
• The name of the work comes from the Sanskrit words *Artha* (“aim” or “goal”) and *Shastra* (“treatise” or “book”) and the goal of the work is a comprehensive understanding of statecraft which will enable a monarch to rule effectively.
 
• The title has therefore been translated as The Science of Politics, The Science of Political Economy, and The Science of Material Gain; this last because Artha is understood in Hinduism as one of the fundamental aims of human beings in pursuing wealth and social status.
 
• The Arthashastra is thought to have been written by Kautilya as a kind of handbook for Chandragupta instructing him on how to reign over a kingdom and encouraging direct action in addressing political concerns without regard for ethical considerations. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Arthashastra is informed both by Hinduism and the practicality of the philosophical school of Charvaka which rejected the supernatural elements of the faith in favor of a completely materialistic view of the universe and human existence. 
 
• The Arthashastra has since enjoyed international fame as one of the greatest political treatises ever written and is frequently compared to The Prince (published 1532 CE) by the Italian political philosopher Niccolò Machiavelli (l. 1469-1527 CE) of Renaissance fame.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Ayas** described in the Rigveda is** Metal**.
 
• The Rigveda or Rig Veda is an archaic Indian collection of Vedic Sanskrit hymns.
 
• It is one of the four holy canonical texts (śruti) of Hinduism known as the Vedas.
 
• The Rigveda is the oldest known Vedic Sanskrit text present till now.
 
• Its early layers are one of the matured extant texts in any Indo-European language.
 
• The sounds and texts of Rigveda have been orally communicated since the 2nd millennium BCE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The philological and linguistic evidence signals that the bulk of the Rigveda Samhita was composed in the northwestern region of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is most likely between 1500 and 1000 BC although a wider approximation of 1700–1000 BCE has also been given.
 
• The text is layered comprises of the Samhita, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, and Upanishads.

__
 
• The Rigveda is one of the oldest and most important texts in the Vedic literature.
 
• It is primarily a collection of hymns dedicated to various deities.
 
• The Rigveda mentions various functionaries such as 'Senani' (military commander), 'Kulapa' (head of a family or clan), and 'Gramani' (village headman).

solution:

• **Kuttakaganita or "computation using kuttaka"** is the word used by **Brahmagupta for algebra**. Kuttaka (often translated as "pulverizer") is an algorithm for reducing the terms of an indeterminate equation, which is basically a recast of the Euclidean algorithm to obtain the largest common divisor of two natural numbers.
 
• Interestingly, puzzles called kuttaka are still found in folklore even now. After Brahmagupta, mathematicians referred to algebra as avyakta ganita or unknown quantity arithmetic, as opposed to vyakta ganita ganita (arithmetic of known quantities).
 
• Others also used the term bijaganita for algebra, beginning around the 9th century.
 
• Bija means "seed" or "element," and bijaganita has been translated as the known quantity of "computation with the seed or unknown quantity that produces the fruit or phala."

subject: GK
question:
Which of the following statements is NOT correct about Gupta emperor, Samudragupta?

a) He was the successor of Chandragupta I.

b) His court poet Bhimsena composed a prashasti of praise for him which was known as Gwalior Prashasti.

c) On his gold coins he was depicted playing the harp which shows his passion for music.

d) He held the title of Ashvamedha Parakram.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Statement b only__.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Samudragupta:**

__
 
• The **first prominent king** of the Gupta Dynasty was **Samudragupta.**
 
• He is Known as the **Napoleon of India for his conquests.**
 
• **Samudragupta's court poet and minister 'Harisena' composed the Allahabad pillar Inscription or Prayag Prasasti.**
 
• The **Pillar was an Ashokan Pillar erected by Ashoka **six centuries before him.
 
• This** inscription serves as a praise for Samudragupta and mentions both his conquests and the boundaries of the Gupta Empire.**
 
• As per this inscription,** Samudragupta defeated 9 kings in the North, 12 Kings in the South, reduced all the Atavika states to vassalage.**
 
• **Samudragupta was defeated, captured, and later released by the kings of Palakkad, Kottura, and Avamukta.**
 
• Samudragupta used a **variety of tactics, including violent devastation.**
 
• **He made the kings of the forest states in central India his servants.**
 
• The **Shaka-Murundas are included among the monarchs **who made an effort to appease **Chandragupta in his father Samudragupta's Allahabad Pillar inscription.**
 
• The Allahabad Pillar inscription mentions that the **Kushana rulers of North-West India and the Saka satraps of western India** also submitted to him.
 
• **The Kushan ruler by name of Shahanushahi** is said to have **personally appeared before Samudra Gupta and tendered voluntary submission** and **agreed to accept and circulate the imperial coins as currency** in his territories and **offered his daughter in marriage to the emperor.**
 
• The **empire of Samudra Gupta probably extended from Afghanistan in the west to Assam in the east and from Nepal in the north to Kanchi in the south**.
 
• To commemorate his victories he performed** Ashvamedha Yaga and donated liberally to Brahmins, the poor, and the needy.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Gupta dynasty was established by Shrigupta.** He hailed from either Magadha (Bihar) or Prayag (eastern U.P.).
 
• His son **Ghatotkacha, who carried the title of maharaja**, appears to be some small king about whom nothing much is known.

 
 

 **Chandragupta-I**
 
 
 
• The **real founder of the Gupta empire was Chandragupta I (AD 319–334).**
 
• The year of his accession in A.D. **319 marks the beginning of the Gupta era.**
 
• He took the title of **maharajadhiraja (king of kings)**.
 
• He **married a Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi.**
 
 
• This **event is recorded** in a **series of gold coins issued by Chandragupta.**
 
 
 
• Chandragupta, was ruling over Magadha (Bihar) Saket (modern Ayodhya) and Prayaga (modern Allahabad) with his capital at Pataliputra (Modern Patna).
 
 
 
 

 **Samudragupta**
 
 
 
• Chandragupta was succeeded by his **son Samudragupta (A.D. 335-375).**
 
 
 
 

 **Chandragupta II**
 
 
 
• Samudragupta was succeeded by his** son Chandragupta II (AD 375–414)** also known as **Chandragupta Vikramaditya**, he not only extended his father’s empire but also consolidated his position through matrimonial alliances with other royal dynasties of the period.
 
• **He married Kuvernaga, the Naga princess and had a daughter Prabhavati from her.**
 
• **Prabhavati was given in marriage to Rudrasena II of the Vakataka dynasty ruling in Deccan.**
 
 
• After the death of her husband, **Prabhavati ruled the territory as regent to her minor son with the help of her father.**
 
 
 
• The control of Vakataka territory proved very beneficial to Chandragupta II, as he was now able to target his other enemies better.
 
• His **greatest military achievement was his victory over the Shaka kings** and assumed the **tilte of Sakari (Destroyer of Sakas).**
 
• This conquest made Gupta empire reach up to the western coast.
 
• An **iron pillar inscription at Mehrauli in Delhi indicates that his empire included even north-western India and Bengal.**
 
• He took the **title of Vikramaditya** i.e. the **one who is as powerful as the sun.**
 
• Chandragupta II is remembered for his **patronage of art and literature.**
 
• He is credited with maintaining **nine luminaries (navaratna)** in his court.
 
 
• The great **Sanskrit poet **and **playwright Kalidasa was the most notable of them all.**
 
 
 
• The **Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa Hien (AD 404–411)** visited India during his reign.
 
• He has left an account of the life of people in India in the fifth century AD.
 
 
 
 

 **Kumaragupta**
 
 
 
• He reigned from **AD 415 to AD 455.**
 
• He inherited the vast empire of his father Chandragupta II.
 
• He was a powerful ruler who ruled for 40 years defending his kingdom.
 
• He adopted the title of **Mahendraditya.**
 
• He** founded the Nalanda University** (a renowned university of ancient India).
 
• **Kalidas (the Shakespeare of India) flourished during the reign of both Chandragupta II and Kumaragupta I.**
 
• He was the** worshipper of Lord Kartikeya (son of Lord Shiva, his vehicle is peacock).**
 
• He **died during the war with the Hunas.**
 
 
 
 

 **Skandagupta**
 
 
 
• **Skandagupta is known as ''Vikramaditya'' Saviour of India as he successfully fought the battle against the invading Huns.**
 
• He ascended the throne in **455 AD and ruled till 467 AD.**
 
• Skandagupta **issued five types of gold coins:**
 
 
• **Archer type, King and queen type, Chhatra type, Lion-slayer type and Horseman type.**
 
 
 
• His **silver coins are of four types**:
 
 
• **Garuda type, Bull type, Altar type and Madhyadesha type**.

 The Pallavas, ruling parts of southern India, were contemporaries and often adversaries of the Chalukyas, known for their rock-cut architecture and patronage of art.

question:
Select the correct alternative on the basis of the given statements on the cities of Harappan civilisation.

**Statement I:** Most of the Harappan cities were divided into two parts: Higher Town and Lower Town.

**Statement II: **The archaeologists describe the lower part of the towns as Citadel.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Neither Statement I nor Statement II is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement I is true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Many of the Harappan or Indus Valley Civilization cities were indeed divided into two major parts.
 
• The "Higher Town" was often a fortified area, which typically housed the public buildings, administrative buildings, and the higher social classes.
 
• The "Lower Town" was where the majority of the populace lived, and it was well-planned with residential areas, markets, streets laid out in a grid pattern, and sophisticated drainage systems. **Hence, statement I is correct.**
 
• In the context of Harappan cities, it is the "Higher Town" or the raised platform part that is often referred to as the Citadel or Acropolis, not the lower part.
 
• The Citadel was usually the area that contained the major public buildings, administrative centers, and possibly religious buildings. Hence, statement II is incorrect.
 
• It was fortified and separated from the lower residential areas, indicating a distinction in social or functional use.

question: Which of the following is considered the oldest known civilization of the Indian subcontinent?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus Valley Civilization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as Harappan Civilization, is considered the oldest known civilization of the Indian subcontinent, dating back to approximately 3300 BCE.
 
• It was primarily located along the Indus River and its tributaries in present-day Pakistan and northwest India.
 
• Major urban centers of the civilization included Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, and Dholavira, which displayed advanced town planning, drainage systems, and architecture.
 
• The people of the Indus Valley were skilled in metallurgy, pottery, and trade, with evidence of extensive trade networks connecting Mesopotamia and other regions.
 
• The civilization is notable for its undeciphered script and seals, which provide insights into its social, economic, and religious practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Town Planning:** Indus cities were well-planned with grid-like layouts, advanced drainage systems, and organized residential and public spaces.
 
• **Seals and Script:** Thousands of seals with animal motifs and inscriptions in the undeciphered script have been discovered, indicating administrative and trade practices.
 
• **Trade Networks:** Archaeological evidence suggests long-distance trade with Mesopotamia, Central Asia, and other civilizations, with goods like cotton, beads, and pottery being exchanged.
 
• **Decline:** The civilization began to decline around 1900 BCE, possibly due to environmental changes, tectonic activity, or the drying of the Saraswati River.
 
• **Legacy:** The Indus Valley Civilization laid the foundation for subsequent cultures and civilizations in the Indian subcontinent, influencing agricultural, architectural, and societal practices.

question:
In the following questions, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Select the correct option from the following:

Assertion (A): Rows of circular brick platforms at Harappa were used for religious ceremonies.

Reason (R): These platforms were found to contain wheat and barley grains.

options.text: Both A and R are false
Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is false, but R is true

solution:
The correct answer is __**A is false, but R is true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** is incorrect as there is no evidence to suggest that rows of circular brick platforms at Harappa were used for religious ceremonies.
 
• **Reason (R)** is true because these platforms were indeed found to contain traces of wheat and barley grains, indicating their association with storage or processing activities rather than religious purposes.
 
• Harappan civilization was primarily urban, and its structures often had practical purposes such as granaries, workshops, or drainage systems rather than religious use.
 
• The presence of grains like wheat and barley aligns with the agricultural economy of the Harappans, which was a key aspect of their livelihood.
 
• Thus, the correct conclusion is that A is false, but R is true, as the Reason (R) does not support the Assertion (A).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harappan Civilization:**

 
 
• It is also known as the Indus Valley Civilization, flourishing between 2500 BCE and 1900 BCE.
 
• Prominent sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Kalibangan, and Lothal.
 
• The civilization was known for advanced urban planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures.
 
 
 
• **Granaries in Harappa:**
 
 
• Large granaries were discovered at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro, indicating surplus food production and storage.
 
• These granaries were often located near river banks for easy transport of goods.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture in Harappan Society:**
 
 
• Major crops included wheat, barley, sesame, and peas.
 
• Irrigation systems were used to support agriculture, although evidence of large-scale canals is limited.
 
 
 
• **Religious Practices:**
 
 
• No specific religious structures like temples have been identified in Harappan sites.
 
• Seals and figurines suggest the worship of natural elements, animals, and fertility symbols.

The correct answer is __**Vardhamana Mahavira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Vardhamana Mahavira

 
 
• Vardhamana Mahavira was born at Kundgrama near Vaishali in Bihar.
 
• His father, Siddharth was the head of the "Jantrika clan" of Kshatriyas.
 
• His mother, Trishala belonged to the Lichchhavi tribe.
 
• After getting true knowledge, he came to be known as the master of "Kevalajana".
 
• He was the 24th Tirthankara of the Jain religion.
 
• He died at Pawapuri in Bihar.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagarjuna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hiuen Tsang, the Chinese traveler and Buddhist scholar, referred to Nagarjuna as "one of the four lights of the world" for his exceptional contributions to Buddhist philosophy.
 
• Nagarjuna was a renowned Indian philosopher, often regarded as the founder of the Madhyamaka school of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• His philosophical concepts, particularly the doctrine of "Shunyata" (emptiness), are considered revolutionary in Buddhist thought.
 
• Due to his profound intellect and transformative contributions to philosophy and metaphysics, Nagarjuna is often referred to as the "Indian Einstein."
 
• He lived during the 2nd–3rd century CE and his works significantly influenced Buddhist traditions and Indian intellectual history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shunyata (Emptiness):** Nagarjuna's doctrine that nothing possesses inherent existence and all phenomena arise due to dependent origination.
 
• **Madhyamaka Philosophy:** Nagarjuna's school of thought emphasized the "Middle Way," avoiding extremes of eternalism and nihilism.
 
• **Scientific Analogies:** Nagarjuna's philosophical inquiries into causality and interdependence are compared to modern scientific principles, earning him the title "Indian Einstein."
 
• **Contributions to Medicine and Alchemy:** Nagarjuna is also credited with advancements in Ayurveda and early Indian alchemical traditions.
 
• **Works:** His major treatises include "Mula-Madhyamaka-Karika" (Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way) and other texts exploring Buddhist metaphysics.

• Magadha’s capital was **Rajagriha (modern-day Rajgir)**, which was a significant hub for political and religious activities during the Mahajanapada period.
 
• The Kuru Mahajanapada had its capital at **Indraprastha**, which is associated with the modern-day Delhi region.
 
• The capital of Avanti Mahajanapada was **Ujjayini**, known for its cultural and religious importance in ancient times.
 
• These capitals were significant centers of administration, trade, and culture during the time of the Mahajanapadas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahajanapadas:**

 
 
• The term "Mahajanapada" refers to the sixteen large states or kingdoms that existed in ancient India during the 6th century BCE.
 
• These states were spread across the Indo-Gangetic plains and were the precursors to later empires such as the Maurya and Gupta dynasties.
 
• The Mahajanapadas were classified into monarchies and republics, with governance structures varying between them.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Capitals:**
 
 
• Capitals like Rajagriha, Kaushambi, Ujjayini, and Indraprastha were strategic centers for trade, culture, and governance.
 
• These cities were often fortified and served as seats of power for their respective rulers.
 
• Capitals also played a key role in the spread of religion, especially Buddhism and Jainism during this period.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Spread:**
 
 
• The Mahajanapadas were located in modern-day regions of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and parts of Pakistan.
 
• This geographical distribution highlights the diversity and cultural richness of ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Religious and Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Many of the Mahajanapadas, such as Magadha, played a vital role in the development and spread of Buddhism and Jainism.
 
• These regions were home to several important religious councils and gatherings.

question:
Select the correct alternative on the given statements based on Ashoka’s Lion capital and India’s State Emblem.

Statement I: In the original Ashoka’s Lion Capital, there are four lions mounted backto-back on a circular abacus that itself rests on a bell-shaped lotus.

Statement II: The State Emblem is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Asoka at Sarnath in which the bell-shaped lotus was omitted.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Neither Statement I nor Statement II is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Statement I and Statement II are true.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The original Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath features four lions standing back-to-back.
 
• The lions are mounted on a circular abacus, which in turn rests on a bell-shaped lotus.
 
• The State Emblem of India is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka.
 
• In the State Emblem, the bell-shaped lotus was omitted, and only the abacus and the four lions were retained.
 
• The adaptation of the Lion Capital as the State Emblem signifies the Republic of India's commitment to peace and goodwill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lion Capital of Ashoka:**

 
 
• The Lion Capital was originally erected around 250 BCE by Emperor Ashoka to commemorate his conversion to Buddhism.
 
• It was discovered by archaeologists in 1905-1906 at Sarnath, near Varanasi.
 
 
 
• **Symbolism:**
 
 
• The four lions represent power, courage, confidence, and pride.
 
• The wheel (Dharma Chakra) depicted on the abacus symbolizes the eternal wheel of law.
 
 
 
• **State Emblem of India:**
 
 
• Adopted on 26th January 1950, the day India became a republic.
 
• The State Emblem also includes the motto "Satyameva Jayate" (Truth Alone Triumphs) inscribed below the abacus in Devanagari script.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Significance:**
 
 
• The bell-shaped lotus is a common feature in Mauryan architecture and represents purity and beauty.
 
• The adaptation of the Lion Capital without the lotus signifies a focus on the symbolic values of the lions and the wheel.

• The city administration **was documented by Megasthenes and Kautilya. **

• **City administration was well planned.**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** established the Mauryan Empire by overthrowing the Nanda Dynasty in the late 4th century BCE.
 
• The Nanda Dynasty was known for its wealth and powerful military and was the ruling dynasty in the region of Magadha before the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was supported by his mentor and advisor, **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, in his efforts to overthrow the Nandas.
 
• The final ruler of the Nanda Dynasty, Dhana Nanda, was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya, leading to the establishment of the Mauryan rule.
 
• The Mauryan Empire, under Chandragupta Maurya, marked the beginning of a significant period in Indian history, characterized by political unity and the spread of Buddhism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nanda Dynasty**

 
 
• The Nanda Dynasty was founded by Mahapadma Nanda, who is often considered the first historical emperor of India.
 
• The Nandas are known for their centralized administration and large army, which included a significant number of war elephants.
 
• The dynasty ruled from approximately 345 to 322 BCE and was known for its immense wealth and extensive control over the Ganges plain.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya (Kautilya)**
 
 
• Chanakya was an ancient Indian teacher, philosopher, economist, jurist, and royal advisor.
 
• He is traditionally identified as the author of the Arthashastra, an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
 
• Chanakya played a crucial role in the establishment of the Mauryan Empire and was the chief advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya, lasted from 322 to 185 BCE and was one of the largest empires in Indian history.
 
• Under the rule of Ashoka, the empire saw the widespread adoption of Buddhism and the spread of Buddhist principles throughout Asia.
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly organized and included a vast network of spies and a standing army.
 
 
 
• **Magadha**
 
 
• Magadha was an ancient Indian kingdom located in the eastern part of India, in what is now Bihar.
 
• It played a central role in the rise of several significant Indian empires, including the Maurya and Gupta Empires.
 
• The region was known for its strategic location, fertile land, and rich mineral resources, which contributed to its power and influence.

• Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Mauryan Empire, is credited with establishing an extensive **spy system** to ensure efficient governance and internal security.
 
• This spy network was a part of the administrative framework suggested by his advisor **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, as outlined in the Arthashastra.
 
• The system comprised secret agents who worked undercover to gather intelligence on both internal and external matters.
 
• Spies were categorized based on their roles, such as **‘Sanstha’** (stationary informants) and **‘Sanchari’** (roving informants), to monitor various aspects of administration and society.

• The text is divided into 15 books, covering topics like diplomacy, law, taxation, and intelligence gathering.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya (Kautilya):**
 
 
• A renowned ancient Indian philosopher, economist, and political advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Mauryan Empire and the formulation of its governance policies.
 
• Known for his strategic acumen and the compilation of the Arthashastra.
 
 
 
• **Spy System in Ancient India:**
 
 
• Ancient Indian rulers, including those of the Mauryan dynasty, used spies to gather intelligence on political, military, and economic matters.
 
• Spies often disguised themselves as ascetics, merchants, or commoners to blend into society and collect information.
 
• The system helped prevent rebellions, monitor officials, and manage foreign relations.

• The Mauryan Empire (322–185 BCE) was the first large-scale empire in Indian history, founded by Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• It was marked by centralized administration, a well-organized bureaucracy, and military strength.
 
• Under rulers like Chandragupta and Ashoka, it became one of the most powerful empires in the ancient world.

question: In 1957 - 58 Dr. Vishnu Wakankar accidentally discovered which prehistoric archaeological site?
solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Bhimbetka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 1957 - 58, Dr Vishnu Wakankar** accidentally discovered prehistoric** archaeological site Bhimbetka.**
 
• **The Bhimbetka rock shelters **are an archaeological site spanning both the prehistoric Paleolithic and Mesolithic periods and the historical era in central India.
 
• This shows the earliest signs of human life in India and proof of the Stone Age beginning in Acheulian times at the site.
 
• It is situated about 45 kilometres southeast of Bhopal in the Raisen District in the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, consisting of seven hills spread over 10 km and over 750 rock shelters. More than 100,000 years ago, at least some shelters were inhabited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **V. S. Wakankar,** who saw these rock formations and thought these were similar to those he had seen in Spain and France, was the first archaeologist to visit a few caves at the site and discover its prehistoric significance.
 
• With a team of archaeologists, he visited the region and documented many **prehistoric rock shelters in 1957.**
 
• The evidence indicates that there was a continuous human settlement here from the Stone Age through the late Acheulian to the late Mesolithic until the 2nd century BCE in these caves, **according to the Archaeological Survey of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Caves of Udayagiri** are twenty rock-cut caves from the early years of the 5th century CE near Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh. The caves of Udayagiri include Vaishnavism (Vishnu), Shaktism (Durga and Matrikas) and Shaivism iconography (Shiva).

• The hymns are dedicated to various deities, primarily the Rigvedic deities like Agni (Fire), Indra (the king of gods), and Soma (a sacred potion or plant).

 Option

 3) Yajurveda
 Comprises the liturgy (mantras) needed to perform the sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas, containing both prose and verse forms.

question: Which of the following Vedas is found in two recensions, black and white, and is full of rituals to be performed publicly or individually?

The correct answer is __**Yajurveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yajurveda:-**

 
 
• **The Yajurveda is the Veda primarily of prose mantras for worship rituals. **
 
• It is one of the four Vedas, the Hindu scriptures that are considered to be the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism.
 
• **The Yajurveda is compiled with ritual-offering formulas that were said by a priest while an individual performed ritual actions such as those before the Yajna fire.**
 
• The Yajurveda is also one of the scriptures of Hinduism.
 
• **The Veda that is found in two recensions, black and white, and is full of rituals to be performed publicly or individually is the Yajurveda.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Rigveda**:-

 
 
• **It is the oldest and most important of the four Vedas. **
 
• It is a collection of over 1,000 hymns that were composed over a period of centuries, most likely between 1500 and 1200 BCE.
 
• The hymns are dedicated to a variety of deities, including Indra, Agni, and Soma.
 
• The Rigveda is considered to be one of the most important texts in Hindu literature. It is a source of information about early Indian culture and religion.
 
 
 
• **Atharvaveda:-**
 
 
• **It is the fourth and youngest of the four Vedas. **
 
• It is a collection of hymns and spells that are used for a variety of purposes, including healing, protection, and cursing.
 
• The Atharvaveda is considered to be a practical Veda, as it deals with the everyday concerns of life.
 
• It is also a source of information about Indian folk medicine and magic.
 
 
 
• **Samaveda:-**
 
 
• **It is the third of the four Vedas. **
 
• It is a collection of hymns that are set to music.
 
• The hymns are derived from the Rigveda, but they are set to a different melody.
 
• The Samaveda is considered to be the Veda of music, and it is used in Hindu rituals. It is also a source of information about Indian music theory and practice.

question: The Aryans are considered to represent a linguistic group speaking which of the following groups of languages?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-European**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Aryans are traditionally associated with the Indo-European group of languages.
 
• This linguistic group includes languages such as Sanskrit, Greek, Latin, and their modern descendants.
 
• The Indo-European languages are one of the most widely spoken language families in the world.
 
• Historically, the migration and spread of Aryans contributed to the dissemination of these languages across Europe and South Asia.
 
• The earliest known speakers of Indo-European languages are believed to have lived in the steppes of Central Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-European Language Family:**

 
 
• It is divided into several branches, including Germanic, Romance, Slavic, and Indo-Iranian.
 
• Languages like English, Spanish, Russian, Hindi, and Bengali are part of this family.
 
• The Proto-Indo-European language is the hypothetical common ancestor of all Indo-European languages.
 
• Scholars use linguistic reconstruction techniques to study and understand Proto-Indo-European.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit:**
 
 
• An ancient language of India, which has a significant role in Hindu scripture and classical Indian literature.
 
• It is one of the earliest attested Indo-European languages.
 
• Sanskrit has influenced many modern South Asian languages.
 
 
 
• **Historical Spread:**
 
 
• The Indo-European languages spread through migrations and conquests.
 
• The Aryans are believed to have entered the Indian subcontinent around 1500 BCE.
 
• They brought with them their language and cultural practices, which significantly influenced the region.
 
 
 
• **Modern Relevance:**
 
 
• Indo-European languages are spoken by nearly half of the world's population.
 
• They play a crucial role in global communication, trade, and diplomacy.
 
• Understanding the roots of these languages helps in studying historical human migration patterns.

question: Which of the following dances evolved from ‘Ekaharya Lasyanga’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to sculptural and historical evidence available, the Bharatnatyam dance evolved from** ‘Ekaharya Lasyanga’.**
 
• This is the **classical dance form of Tamil Nadu**.
 
• This dance form is nearly 2000 years old and is viewed as the** mother of many Indian classical dance forms**.
 
• Bharatnatyam dance is referred to as** Ekaharya**, where one performer pulls on several roles in a single performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ekaharya Lasyanga is one of the forms and styles in the **Natyasastra**.
 
• In this form, there is **one actor playing many roles**.
 
• Instead of many actors presenting a dramatic story, the solo actor presents, through abhinaya, the particular dominant state - **Sthayi Bhava**.

**Kuchipudi**

 
• Kuchipudi is the **classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is a dance cum drama performance that emerged from the** Krishna district** of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• This dance form is a mixture of **Tandava **(masculine) and **Lasya** (graceful feminine).
 
• The dancers in Kuchipudi dance **occasionally speak dialogues**, but the dancers in Bharatanatyam don't.

**Kathakali**

 
• Kathakali is the **classical dance form of Kerala**.
 
• It communicates the story through **footwork and gestures of face and hands**.
 
• The features of this dance form can be traced back to Natya Shastra.
 
• The art form consists of** angika, acharya, vichika, **and** satvika, **the four aspects of abhinaya along with the Nritya and Natya aspects.

**Odissi**

 
• Odissi is the** classical dance form of Odisha.**
 
• **Gotipua** is the** precursor** to the Odissi dance.
 
• Examples of this dance can be seen in the **Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves **in Odisha.
 
• Odissi dance form represents **water**.

subject: GK
question: Varnam is one of the stages in ________, a classical dance of India.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

** Varnam **is the Nritya component of **Bharatanatyam**. It is a combination of dance and emotions and is the most important part of the whole performance which is synchronized with** tala and Raag, **to express the story.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** In the early nineteenth century, four dance teachers of Thanjavur defined the elements of a Bharatnatyam recital.

They are:

__
 
• **Alarippu** – It is an invocatory piece of performance that includes basic dance postures and is accompanied by rhythmic syllables. It is meant to seek the blessings of God.
 
• **Jatiswaram** – It is the Nritta component and is devoid of expressions, it includes the different poses and movements.
 
• **Shabdam** – It is the dramatic element with expressed words, which includes the abhinaya in the song. It is generally in praise of the glory of God.
 
• **Varnam** – It is the Nritya component. It is a combination of dance and emotions and is the most important part of the whole performance. It is synchronized with tala and Raag, to express the story. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• **Padam** – It refers to a mastery over the abhinaya (expression) of the spiritual message, by the artist. Music becomes light, dance becomes emotional.
 
• **Jawali **– These are short love-lyrics performed at a faster tempo.
 
• **Thillana **– It is the concluding stage of the performance, and comprises pure dance (Nritta) with exuberant movement and intricate rhythmic variations.

**The four Thanjavur teachers:**

 
• Known as the ‘Tanjore quartet’, are Chiniah, Ponniah, Vadivelu, and Shivanandam. Under them, Bharatnatyam also came to be known as Tanjore Natyam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Oldest among all classical dance forms, Bharatnatyam derives its name from **Bharata Muni** and ‘Natyam which means **dance in Tamil**.
 
• However, other scholars have ascribed the name ‘**Bharata’ to ‘Bhava’, ‘Raga’ and ‘Taal’.**
 
• The origins of this dance form can be traced back to ‘**Sadir’ **– the solo dance performance of the temple dancers or **‘devadasis’ **in Tamil Nadu, hence it was also referred to as ‘**Dashiattam’.**
 
• With the decline of the Devadasi system, art too became nearly extinct. However, the efforts of **E. Krishna Iyer**, a prominent freedom fighter, revived this dance form.
 
• Previously, this dance form was performed by solo female dancers; it has since become increasingly popular among male and group artists as well.
 
• Bharatnatyam is often referred to as the fire dance, as it is the manifestation of fire in the human body. Most of the movements in Bharatnatyam resemble that of a **dancing flame.**
 
• In this dance form, equal emphasis is given on both the **Tandava and Lasya aspects** of dance, with major emphasis on **‘mudras’.**

question: Sattriya dance form is famous in which of these states?
solution:
The correct answer is __Assam.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form originating in Assam.
 
• It was introduced in the 15th century by the great Assamese Vaishnav saint and reformer, **Srimanta Sankardeva**.
 
• This dance was initially performed in **Satras** or monasteries as a part of the daily rituals or to mark special festivals.
 
• **Sattriya** combines elements of dance, drama, and music to narrate mythological stories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect
 Detail
 
 
 
 

 **Recognition**
 Sattriya was recognized as a classical dance form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi of India in 2000.
 
 

 **Elements**
 It incorporates elements such as **Nritta** (pure dance), **Nritya** (expressive dance), and **Natya** (dramatic storytelling).
 
 

 **Music and Instruments**
 The dance is performed with traditional Assamese music and instruments like **Khol** (drum), **Taal** (cymbals), **Flute**, and **Violin**.

The correct answer is __**1910**__.

__
 
• 1910 is the year when Bharatanatyam was banned by the British colonial government.
 
• The ban was part of the British policy to suppress Indian traditions and cultures.
 
• Bharatanatyam was seen as a vital expression of South Indian culture and spirituality.
 
• The ban led to the decline of temple dances and adversely affected the livelihoods of dancers.
 
• Efforts by Indian nationalists and revivalists in the 20th century helped to lift the ban and restore the dance form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
Aspect

 
 
 
Details

 
 
 

 
 
Origin

 
 
 
Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, India.

 
 
 

 
 
Elements

 
 
 
It includes nritta (pure dance), nritya (expressive dance), and natya (dramatic storytelling).

 
 
 

 
 
Significance

 
 
 
It is not just an art form but a way to express devotion and spirituality.

 
 
 

 
 
Revival

 
 
 
The dance form saw a significant revival and restructuring in the 20th century, making it popular worldwide.

 
 
 

 
 
Cultural Impact

 
 
 
Bharatanatyam has played a crucial role in promoting Indian culture and heritage globally.

• T Balasaraswati was a celebrated exponent of Bharatanatyam, an Indian classical dance form.

• Balasaraswati's performances and teaching significantly contributed to the popularization of Bharatanatyam globally.
 
• She received numerous awards, including the Padma Bhushan and the Padma Vibhushan, for her contributions to Indian classical dance.

• Bharatanatyam is a major form of Indian classical dance that originated in the Tamil Nadu region of South India. Here are some key aspects:
 
 
• It is known for its grace, purity, tenderness, and sculpturesque poses.
 
• Bharatanatyam is often performed as a narrative dance, which includes nrita (pure dance), nritya (solo expressive dance), and natya (group dramatic dance).
 
• The dance form was traditionally passed down through the 'Devadasi' system, where young women were 'married' to deities and performed in temples.
 
• In the 20th century, Bharatanatyam transitioned from temples to the stage, becoming a popular and respected art form worldwide.

question: The origin of most of the classical dance forms of India is _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Natya Shastra.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Natya Shastra:-**

 
 
• **Natya Shastra is a treatise on the art of theatre, dance, and music. It is considered to be one of the oldest and most comprehensive texts on these subjects. **
 
• **The text is attributed to Bharata Muni, a sage who is said to have lived in the 2ⁿd century BCE.**
 
• Natya Shastra is divided into 36 chapters and covers a wide range of topics, including the history of theatre, the different types of plays, the roles of the actors, the costumes, the music, and the dance.
 
• The text also provides detailed instructions on how to perform a play.
 
• Natya Shastra has had a profound influence on the development of theatre, dance, and music in India.
 
• It is still studied and performed today, and it is considered to be a classic work of Indian literature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yajur Veda:-**

 
 
• **It is one of the four Vedas, the sacred scriptures of Hinduism. **
 
• It is a collection of mantras, or sacred utterances, that are used in religious rituals. Yajur Veda is divided into two main parts: the Black Yajur Veda and the White Yajur Veda.
 
 
 
• **Artha Shastra:-**
 
 
• **It is a treatise on economics, politics, and statecraft. **
 
• It is considered to be one of the oldest and most important works on these subjects.
 
• The text is attributed to Kautilya, a minister to the Mauryan emperor Chandragupta Maurya.
 
 
 
• **Atharva Veda:-**
 
 
• **It is one of the four Vedas, the sacred scriptures of Hinduism. **
 
• It is a collection of mantras, or sacred utterances, that are used in a variety of rituals.
 
• Atharva Veda is divided into 20 books and contains over 7000 mantras.

__
 
• Jatin Goswami

 
 
• A well-known veteran classical dancer from Assam is Jatin Goswami.
 
• In 1933, Jatin Goswami was born in Dergaon, Upper Assam.
 
• Jatin Goswami began his first lesson of Satriya dance at home with the help of his father.
 
• Later, he received expert gurus' instruction in dance and music on the Vaishnava Satras.
 
• In order to advance and expand the Satriya dancing style, he also founded a dance group.

• Sangeet Natak Akademi

 
 
• Sangeet Natak Akademi, the apex body in the field of performing arts in the country, was formed in 1953.
 
• It was set up for the preservation and promotion of the vast intangible heritage of India's diverse culture expressed in forms of music, dance, and drama.
 
• The management of the Akademi vests in its General Council.
 
• Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar Karaikudi was the first to receive the Sahitya Natak Akademi award.
 
• Sangeet Natak Akademi Puraskar is an award given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Academy was established on 31 May 1952 by a resolution of the Ministry of Human Resource development.
 
• The Akademi was officially inaugurated on 28 January 1953 by the first President of India Rajendra Prasad and PV Rajmannar was appointed as its first Chairman.

question: Nahid Siddiqui is a famous classical dancer in _______ genre.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Nahid Siddiqui is a renowned classical dancer specializing in the **Kathak** genre.
 
• She has significantly contributed to the promotion and revival of Kathak dance both in India and internationally.
 
• Nahid Siddiqui is acclaimed for her innovative choreography and mastery over the intricate techniques of Kathak.
 
• She has received multiple awards and recognitions for her outstanding contributions to the field of classical dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance**

 
 
• Originated in northern India and is one of the eight classical dance forms in India.
 
• Known for its intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.
 
• Historically, Kathak dancers traveled and performed across the subcontinent, evolving the dance form into a storytelling medium.
 
• Kathak has influences from Mughal culture and incorporates both Hindu and Persian elements.
 
 
 
• **Gharanas in Kathak**
 
 
• There are three primary gharanas (schools) of Kathak: Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras.
 
• Each gharana has its unique style, emphasis on techniques, and traditional compositions.
 
 
 
• **Prominent Kathak Dancers**
 
 
• Birju Maharaj: A leading exponent of the Lucknow gharana.
 
• Shovana Narayan: Known for her innovative approach and contributions to the modern Kathak.
 
• Kumudini Lakhia: A celebrated Kathak dancer and choreographer.
 
 
 
• **Costumes in Kathak**
 
 
• Female dancers usually wear anarkali suits, lehengas, and dupattas.
 
• Male dancers typically wear dhotis or churidars with kurtas and angarakhas.
 
• Jewelry and ghungroos (ankle bells) are integral to the costume, enhancing the visual and auditory experience.

question: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma is renowned for her contribution to **Mohiniyattam**, a classical dance form from Kerala.
 
• She is often referred to as the **Mother of Mohiniyattam** for her pivotal role in reviving and popularizing the dance form.
 
• She was honored with the prestigious **Padma Shri** award in 1977 for her dedication to Indian classical dance.
 
• Her efforts in training and choreographing have significantly enriched the repertoire and status of Mohiniyattam on the global stage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam**

 
 
• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form that originates from the state of Kerala in South India.
 
• The name Mohiniyattam comes from "Mohini," a mythical enchantress avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, and "attam," meaning dance.
 
• The dance is characterized by graceful, swaying body movements and subtle facial expressions, which are meant to enchant the audience.
 
• Mohiniyattam traditionally involves solo female performances, but it has evolved to include group performances as well.
 
 
 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India**
 
 
• India is home to eight recognized classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Sattriya, Manipuri, and Mohiniyattam.
 
• Each dance form is unique in its style, costumes, makeup, and music, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of different regions.
 
• These dance forms are deeply rooted in Indian mythology, spirituality, and folk traditions.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors in India, awarded to individuals for their distinguished contributions in various fields.
 
• They are classified into three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri, in the order of their significance.
 
• The awards are announced annually on Republic Day (26th January).

• Madhavi Mudgal is renowned for her expertise in **Odissi dance**, one of the eight classical dance forms of India.
 
• She has received numerous awards, including the prestigious **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in 2000 for her contribution to Odissi dance.

• She trained under the guidance of Guru **Kelucharan Mohapatra**, a legendary figure in Odissi dance.
 
• Her choreography and performances are known for their grace, technical precision, and adherence to the traditional Odissi style.

• **Odissi Dance**

 
 
• Odissi is one of the oldest surviving dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by its fluid movements, intricate footwork, and expressive gestures (mudras).
 
• Odissi dance is traditionally performed as a form of worship and storytelling, often depicting tales from Hindu mythology.
 
• The dance form is known for its distinct postures, such as the Tribhangi, which involves three bends in the body.
 
• Odissi music is based on classical Indian ragas and talas, adding a melodic dimension to the dance performances.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**

• The award was established by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama, in 1952.
 
• Recipients of this award are honored for their work in fields such as music, dance, theater, and other performing arts.
 
• The award includes a citation, a plaque, and a cash prize, reflecting the recipient's exceptional talent and dedication.
 
 
 
• **Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra**
 
 
• He was a legendary Odissi dancer, choreographer, and teacher who played a crucial role in reviving and popularizing Odissi dance.
 
• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra trained many renowned dancers, including Madhavi Mudgal and Sonal Mansingh.
 
• His contributions to Odissi dance earned him numerous accolades, including the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award.
 
• He is remembered for his innovative choreography, dedication to preserving traditional techniques, and nurturing new talent.

__
 
• **Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma** is a renowned icon in the **Kuchipudi** dance form.
 
• He is particularly famous for his expertise in **stree-vesham**, which involves male dancers performing female roles.
 
• His contributions have earned him a pre-eminent place in the Kuchipudi dance hall of fame.
 
• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma has played a significant role in popularizing Kuchipudi both in India and globally.
 
• He has received numerous awards for his exceptional skills and dedication to the art form.

• **Kuchipudi**

 
 
• Kuchipudi is one of the eight major Indian classical dances.
 
• It originated in a village named Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The dance form combines fast rhythms and fluid movements, creating a unique style that is both expressive and graceful.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often include intricate footwork, dramatic expressions, and complex hand gestures.
 
• It traditionally involves both dance and acting, often telling stories from Hindu epics and scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Stree-vesham**
 
 
• Stree-vesham refers to the portrayal of female characters by male dancers.
 
• This practice is rooted in ancient Indian theater and dance traditions.
 
• It requires exceptional skill in mimicking female mannerisms and expressions.
 
• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma is celebrated for his mastery of stree-vesham in Kuchipudi.
 
• Stree-vesham performances are often used to depict mythological stories and characters.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Dance Forms**

• Each dance form has its own unique style, history, and technique.
 
• These dances are known for their intricate footwork, expressive hand gestures, and elaborate costumes.
 
• They often narrate stories from Hindu mythology and Indian folklore.
 
• Classical dances play a significant role in preserving and promoting India's rich cultural heritage.

question: Kamala Lakshmi Narayanan is recognised all over the world as the foremost proponent of____ a southern Indian classical dance form that combines artistic expression with rhythmic footwork.

The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a major form of Indian classical dance that originated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• The dance form is traditionally performed by women and has its roots in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
 
• Bharatanatyam is renowned for its grace, purity, tenderness, and sculpturesque poses.
 
• It is one of the oldest classical dance traditions in India, documented as far back as 2,000 years ago.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History and Origin**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is believed to have been inspired by the sculptures of the ancient temple of Chidambaram.
 
• The dance form was revived in the 20th century by prominent artists such as Rukmini Devi Arundale.
 
 
 
• **Training and Performance**
 
 
• Training in Bharatanatyam involves rigorous practice and learning of complex rhythms and expressions.
 
• Performers wear traditional costumes, usually a sari, and adorn themselves with jewelry and makeup.
 
 
 
• **Musical Accompaniment**
 
 
• The dance is typically accompanied by Carnatic music, and a live orchestra including instruments like the mridangam, violin, and veena.
 
• Vocal support is also an essential part of Bharatanatyam performances.
 
 
 
• **Major Exponents**
 
 
• Some of the notable exponents of Bharatanatyam include Rukmini Devi Arundale, Padma Subrahmanyam, and Yamini Krishnamurthy.
 
• These artists have significantly contributed to the global recognition and preservation of this classical dance form.

__
 
• **Bharatnatyam** is one of the oldest and most renowned classical dance forms of India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is deeply rooted in **Natya Shastra**, the ancient treatise on performing arts written by Bharat Muni.
 
• Traditionally, Bharatnatyam was performed in temples as a form of devotional expression to narrate **mythological stories and spiritual ideas**.
 
• The dance form is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful gestures, and facial expressions known as **Abhinaya**, which convey emotions and tell stories.
 
• Bharatnatyam is recognized globally for its **rhythmic precision, aesthetic beauty, and spiritual significance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India**

 
 
• India has **eight recognized classical dance forms**, which include Bharatnatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.
 
• Each dance form originates from a specific region and reflects the cultural heritage of that area.
 
 
 
• **Natya Shastra**
 
 
• Natya Shastra is an ancient Indian Sanskrit text attributed to Bharat Muni, detailing the foundation of **music, dance, and drama**.
 
• It serves as a guide for the technical and aesthetic aspects of performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Devotional Aspect of Bharatnatyam**
 
 
• Bharatnatyam was historically performed as a form of worship in temples, primarily to honor Lord Shiva in his **Nataraja form**.
 
• The dance symbolizes the union of the soul with the divine.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Bharatnatyam**
 
 
• The dance form integrates three key elements: **Natya (dramatic art), Nritta (rhythmic dance), and Nritya (expressive dance).**
 
• The costumes are vibrant, adorned with intricate jewelry, and complement the storytelling aspect of the dance.

question: Kathak is a classical dance form that developed in which region of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Northern India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India.
 
• It originated and developed in the **northern regions** of India, particularly in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The term "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word **'Katha'**, meaning "story," as the dance form focuses on storytelling through movements and expressions.
 
• Kathak evolved during the Mughal era, blending Hindu devotional themes with Persian and Mughal influences, leading to its distinct style.
 
• This dance form is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressions (**'abhinaya'**) to convey emotions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gharanas in Kathak:** The dance form has three prominent gharanas (schools) – **Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras** – each with its distinct style and emphasis.
 
• **Devotional Roots:** Kathak was initially performed in temples to narrate mythological tales of gods like Krishna and Shiva.
 
• **Mughal Influence:** During the Mughal era, Kathak moved from temples to royal courts, adopting intricate rhythmic patterns and a refined presentation style.
 
• **Instruments:** The tabla, pakhawaj, harmonium, and manjira are commonly used to accompany Kathak performances.
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:** Kathak is recognized as an integral part of India's rich cultural heritage and continues to be performed worldwide.

question: Which classical dance form originated in Andhra Pradesh and incorporates both singing and dancing?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form that originated in Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• It is distinctive as it combines **singing and dancing**, making it unique among Indian classical dance styles.
 
• The dance form derives its name from **Kuchipudi village** in Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Kuchipudi performances are often based on **Hindu religious themes**, particularly stories from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• It involves elaborate **expressions (Abhinaya)**, intricate footwork, and rhythmic patterns, showcasing both grace and technical skill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of Kuchipudi:**

 
 
• Kuchipudi traces its origins to the **Bhakti movement** and was traditionally performed by male Brahmin performers called Bhagavatulu.
 
• The dance form was formalized in the 17th century by **Siddhendra Yogi**, a renowned saint and scholar.
 
• Initially, Kuchipudi was performed in temples as a way to narrate mythological stories and glorify deities.
 
 
 
• **Performance Style:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi integrates **dialogues, music, and dance**, often performed in groups or solo acts.
 
• It employs intricate hand gestures (**Mudras**) and facial expressions to convey emotions and stories.
 
• The dance has a unique feature called **Tarangam**, where the performer dances on a brass plate with precision and balance.
 
 
 
• **Music and Costumes:**
 
 
• The music for Kuchipudi is predominantly **Carnatic**, with lyrics in Telugu or Sanskrit.
 
• The costumes are vibrant, featuring traditional silk attire with intricate embellishments, complemented by jewelry and makeup.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi has gained international acclaim and is performed worldwide by artists trained in this classical art form.
 
• It is recognized as one of the eight major classical dance forms of India by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama form that originated in Kerala, India.
 
• It is renowned for its elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, and expressive gestures, which depict themes from Hindu epics like the **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata**.
 
• The dance form combines music, vocal performances, and hand gestures (**mudras**) to convey stories and emotions.
 
• Kathakali is traditionally performed during the night and can last for several hours, showcasing Kerala's rich cultural heritage.
 
• Renowned for its vibrant storytelling, Kathakali is recognized globally as one of the most visually impressive forms of Indian classical dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Costumes and Makeup:**

 
 
• Costumes are elaborate, featuring a large headgear, colorful attire, and intricate facial makeup.
 
• Facial makeup uses natural pigments and colors to emphasize characters' traits—green for noble characters, red for villains, etc.
 
 
 
• **Music and Instruments:**
 
 
• Kathakali performances are accompanied by traditional instruments like **chenda** (drum), **idakka**, and **shankh** (conch).
 
• Vocal music plays a crucial role, with lyrics often sung in Malayalam or Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Training and Preparation:**
 
 
• Kathakali artists undergo rigorous training, including mastering **kalaripayattu** (traditional martial art) for flexibility and stamina.
 
• The training includes learning complex gestures and expressions to convey emotions effectively.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Kathakali originated in the 17th century and is believed to have evolved from earlier temple art forms such as **Krishnanattam**.
 
• The dance form represents Kerala's cultural identity and is often performed during festivals and cultural events.

__
 
• **Sattriya** is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India.
 
• It was introduced by the Vaishnavite saint **Sankardev** in the 15th-16th centuries in Assam.
 
• The dance form was originally a medium to narrate and propagate **Vaishnavism** and teachings of Lord Krishna.
 
• Sattriya derives its name from “Satras,” the monasteries established by Sankardev to promote Vaishnavism.

• He was the pioneer of the Neo-Vaishnavite movement in the region.
 
• His contributions include writings like the "Kirtan Ghoxa" and translations of scriptures into Assamese.
 
 
 
• **Sattras:**
 
 
• Monastic institutions established by Sankardev to promote Vaishnavism.
 
• They serve as cultural and religious centers, preserving traditional art forms like Sattriya dance and music.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnavism:**
 
 
• A sect of Hinduism focused on the devotion to Lord Vishnu and his avatars, particularly Krishna and Rama.
 
• Sankardev emphasized the path of Bhakti (devotion) as a means to attain spiritual salvation.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya Dance Elements:**

question: Odissi classical dance originated in which Indian state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Odissi** is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India and originated in the state of **Odisha**.
 
• It is deeply rooted in the traditions and temples of Odisha, particularly the **Jagannath Temple in Puri**.
 
• The dance form is characterized by its **graceful movements, sculpturesque poses, and intricate footwork**.
 
• Odissi primarily focuses on expressing religious stories and spirituality through **"abhinaya" (expression) and "nritya" (pure dance)**.
 
• It is believed to have been performed as a form of devotion and offering in Odisha's temples since ancient times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India:**

 
 
• India officially recognizes **eight classical dance forms**, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi, and Sattriya.
 
• These dance forms are rooted in the **Natya Shastra**, an ancient Sanskrit text on performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Odissi Costume:**
 
 
• The dancers wear traditional attire made of silk with intricate designs inspired by temple sculptures.
 
• The jewelry includes silver ornaments, and the makeup emphasizes eye expressions (kohl-lined eyes).
 
 
 
• **Key Elements of Odissi:**
 
 
• It has two main components: **Nritya** (expressive dance) and **Nritta** (pure dance).
 
• Signature poses include the ** and chowk** (square stance).
 
 
 
• **Revival of Odissi:**
 
 
• Odissi faced decline during colonial rule but was revived in the mid-20th century by prominent dancers and scholars.
 
• Notable contributors include **Kelucharan Mohapatra** and **Guru Pankaj Charan Das**.

• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form of India, originating from Assam and deeply rooted in the **Vaishnavite movement**.

question: Which of the following does NOT form a part of the structure of a Buddhist Stupa?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Gopuram.__**

__
 
• **A stupa** is a dirt burial mound faced with stone.
 
• **Buddhist stupa** (dagoba, Chorten, pagoda) serves as a marker for a sacred space, a symbolic representation of the **Buddha’s burial mound**.
 
• In **Buddhism**, the earliest stupas contained portions of the Buddha's ashes, and as a result, the stupa began to be associated with the** body of the Buddha**.
 
• **The Great Stupa at Sanchi**, in central India, is one of the earliest stupas; it served as an architectural prototype for all others that followed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The stupa has **three special features** found in every stupa across the world. They are

 
 
• **A hemispherical mound (anda)**: The anda’s domed shape (green highlights) recalls a mound of dirt that was used to cover the Buddha’s remains.
 
• **A square railing (harmika)**: The harmika (red highlights) is inspired by a square railing or fence that surrounded the mound of dirt, marking it as a sacred burial site.
 
• **A central pillar supporting a triple-umbrella form (chattra)**: It was derived from umbrellas that were placed over the mound to protect it from the elements (purple highlights).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A Gopuram** is a monumental entrance tower, usually ornate, at the entrance of a **Hindu temple, in the Dravidian architecture**.

question: What does the Panchayatana style refer to?

options.text: A dance form of South India

solution:
The correct answer is __A temple architecture.__

__
 
• Panchayatana is a style of **temple construction** that has a **central shrine** surrounded by** four other shrines.**
 
• **Examples of Panchayatana temples.**
 
• **Jagdish Temple** in Udaipur.
 
• **Lakshmana Temple** in Khajuraho.
 
• **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** in Khajuraho.
 
• **Brahmeswara Temple** in Bhubaneswar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aad650d98ae0197c18fbe0754b593721cb8c1898493f61790d81f72b924f2fc5.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Nagara Style of Temple Architecture**
 **Dravidian Style of Temple Architecture**
 
 

 Temples located in **Northern India** are classified as **Nagara **Style.
 Temples located in **Southern India** are classified as **Dravidian Style.**
 
 

 Nagara Style has **multiple Shikharas.**
 The Dravidian style has **1 single Shikhara**.
 
 

 In Nagara Style, Central Tower is **Curvilinear** in shape.
 In Dravidian Style, Central Tower is shaped like a **Pyramid.**
 
 

 In Nagara style, pedestals are higher than the **ground.**
 Pedestals are at **ground level** in the Dravidian Style.
 
 

 In the Nagara style, the** most **prominent element is the **Shikhara**.
 In Dravidian Style, the most prominent element is the **Gopuram**.

__
 
• **Rajarajeshwara temple** is popularly known as **Brihadeshwara temple **and is locally known as **Thanjai Periya Kovil.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Rajaraja Chola (985-1014AD)**

 
• During his reign, the Chola empire expanded from **Kalinga in the north to Srilanka in the South.**
 
• He fought** battles with the Chalukyas** in the north and **the Pandyas** in the south.
 
• He also helped in the construction of a **Buddhist monastery in Nagapattinam.**

question: North Indian architecture is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagara style**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Nagara' temples typically have a North Indian style of architecture.**
 
• **Nagara or North Indian Temple Style:**
 
 
• Nagara (in North India) is associated with the land between the** Himalayas and Vindhyas.**
 
• The Nagara style is associated with the land between the Himalayas and Vindhyas, the Dravida style with the land between the Krishna and Kaveri rivers, while the Vesara style is sometimes associated with the area between the Vindhyas and the Krishna river.
 
• In North India, it is common for an entire temple to be built on a stone platform with steps leading up to it.
 
• It does not usually have elaborate boundary walls or gateways.
 
• While the earliest temples had just one tower or shikhara, later temples had several.
 
• The **garbhagriha** is always located directly under the tallest tower.
 
• There are many subdivisions of nagara temples depending on the shape of the **shikhara**.
 
• The second major type of architectural form in the nagara order is the **phamsana,** which tends to be broader and shorter than the Latina ones.
 
• Their roofs are composed of several slabs that gently rise to a single point over the centre of the building, unlike the Latina ones which look like sharply rising tall towers.
 
• The third main sub-type of the nagara building is generally called the** valabhi type.**
 
• These are rectangular buildings with a roof that rises into a** vaulted chamber.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Three main styles of temple architecture are the** Nagara or the Northern style, the Dravida or the Southern style, and the Vesara or Mixed style**. But at the same time, there are also some regional styles.
 
• A number of architectural texts known as the Shilpashastras were written in early medieval times. These refer to three major styles of temple architecture, Nagara, Dravida, and Vesara.
 
• **Dravida Or South Indian Temple Style:**
 
 
• Unlike the nagara temple, the Dravida temple is enclosed by a compound wall.
 
• The front wall has an entrance gateway in its centre, which is known as a gopuram.
 
• The shape of the main temple tower known as vimana in Tamil Nadu is like a stepped pyramid that rises up geometrically rather than the curving shikhara of North India.
 
• It is common to find a large water reservoir, or a temple tank, enclosed within the complex.
 
• Subsidiary shrines are either incorporated within the main temple tower or located as distinct, separate small shrines beside the main temple.
 
• Kanchipuram, Thanjavur or Tanjore, Madurai, and Kumbakonam are the most famous temple towns of Tamil Nadu, where, during the 8th-12th centuries, the role of the temple was not limited to religious matters alone.
