question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad?

options.text: It is an imitation of the Taj Mahal due to its similar designs.
It was built by Mughal prince Azam Shah.
It is built completely with marble.
It is the burial place of Aurangzeb's wife, Rabia-ud-Durrani.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is built completely with marble.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bibi ka Maqbara** is not entirely built with marble; only the dome and some parts are constructed with marble.
 
• The rest of the structure is made of basalt and lime plaster, giving it a distinct architectural style.
 
• It was built by **Mughal prince Azam Shah** in memory of his mother, Dilras Banu Begum, also known as Rabia-ud-Durrani.
 
• Bibi ka Maqbara is often referred to as the "Taj of the Deccan" due to its similar design to the Taj Mahal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bibi ka Maqbara**

 
 
• It is located in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, India.
 
• The monument was commissioned by Aurangzeb's son, Azam Shah, in 1660.
 
• The architectural design was done by Ata-ullah, who was the son of Ustad Ahmad Lahauri, the principal designer of the Taj Mahal.
 
• The mausoleum's layout and surrounding gardens follow the traditional Mughal Charbagh (four-quartered) garden layout.
 
 
 
• **Taj Mahal**
 
 
• It is located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• It was commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• The construction began in 1632 and was completed in 1653.
 
• The Taj Mahal is entirely built of white marble and is considered one of the finest examples of Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture**
 
 
• Mughal architecture is a unique blend of Islamic, Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles.
 
• It flourished between the 16th and 18th centuries under the Mughal Empire.
 
• Key features include large bulbous domes, slender minarets, large halls, massive vaulted gateways, and delicate ornamentation.
 
• Famous examples include the Red Fort, Jama Masjid, and Fatehpur Sikri.
 
 
 
• **Basalt**
 
 
• Basalt is a common extrusive igneous rock formed from the rapid cooling of basaltic lava.
 
• It is primarily composed of plagioclase, pyroxene, and olivine minerals.
 
• Basalt is known for its durability and is often used in construction.

question: The entrance gateway in Dravidian style temple is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopuram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Gopuram is a monumental entrance tower, usually ornate, at the entrance of a Hindu temple, particularly in Southern India.
 
• It is a distinct feature of Dravidian architecture and often richly decorated with sculptures and carvings.
 
• Gopurams are typically adorned with intricate sculptures depicting various deities, mythical creatures, and legends from Hindu mythology.
 
• They serve not just as entrance gateways but also as a prominent architectural focal point of the temple complex.
 
• The height and grandeur of the Gopuram symbolize the temple's importance and are meant to be visible from a distance, guiding devotees to the temple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shikhara**

 
 
• It is the tower or spire on a Hindu temple, typically found in North Indian temple architecture.
 
• The Shikhara rises above the sanctum where the main deity is enshrined.
 
• It symbolizes the mythical Mount Meru, the axis of the universe in Hindu cosmology.
 
 
 
• **Mandap**
 
 
• It is a pillared hall or pavilion for public rituals in a Hindu temple.
 
• The Mandap is used for religious and ceremonial activities, including weddings and other community gatherings.
 
 
 
• **Vimana**
 
 
• It refers to the tower above the Garbhagriha (sanctum sanctorum) in South Indian temples, similar to the Shikhara in North Indian temples.
 
• The Vimana is usually pyramid-shaped and richly decorated with carvings and sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Architecture**
 
 
• A style of architecture that emerged in the southern part of India, characterized by its pyramid-shaped towers and intricate carvings.
 
• It flourished primarily under the rule of the Chola, Chera, and Pandya dynasties.

question: Which of the following describes the Medhi part in Buddhist structure?

options.text: Ceremonial gateways in front of stupas
The circular terrace between the railing and dome
A low wall to enclose the structure
The umbrella-shaped structure placed at the top of the structure

solution:
The correct answer is __**The circular terrace between the railing and dome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Medhi is the circular terrace found in the structure of a Buddhist stupa.
 
• It is located between the railing (Vedika) and the dome (Anda) of the stupa.
 
• The Medhi is an important part of the architectural design of stupas, providing a platform for circumambulation (Pradakshina) by devotees.
 
• This terrace is often decorated and serves as a transitional element between the lower and upper parts of the stupa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vedika:** The railing around the stupa, which encloses the sacred area and provides a boundary for the Medhi.
 
• **Anda:** The dome-shaped structure representing the mound of earth, symbolizing the universe and the burial mound of the relics of the Buddha.
 
• **Chhatra:** The umbrella-like structure placed at the top of the stupa, symbolizing honor and respect.
 
• **Torana:** Ceremonial gateways that are often positioned at the cardinal points around the stupa, marking entrances to the sacred path.
 
• **Pradakshina Patha:** The circumambulatory path around the stupa, used by devotees for ritualistic walking in a clockwise direction to show reverence.

question: Which architectural style is best described by the following features: ribbed vaults, pointed arches, flying buttresses, and stained-glass windows?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gothic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gothic architecture** originated in 12th-century France and lasted until the 16th century, primarily in Europe.
 
• Key features include **ribbed vaults**, which distribute weight more efficiently, and **pointed arches**, allowing for taller and more flexible structures.
 
• The **flying buttress**, an external support, was instrumental in countering the weight of high vaulted ceilings and enabling large windows.
 
• Stained-glass windows were used extensively, not just for aesthetic appeal but also to depict biblical stories and create an ethereal light effect inside the building.
 
• Notable examples of Gothic architecture include the **Notre-Dame Cathedral** in Paris and the **Chartres Cathedral** in France.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribbed Vault:** A framework of intersecting ribs or arches that support the roof, allowing for lighter and more intricate designs.
 
• **Pointed Arches:** These arches direct the weight of the roof downward rather than outward, enabling taller structures and larger windows.
 
• **Flying Buttress:** An external arch or support that transfers the weight of the roof away from the walls, reducing structural stress and allowing for thinner walls.
 
• **Stained-Glass Windows:** Created by assembling pieces of colored glass, these windows often depicted religious narratives and added a spiritual ambiance through the play of light.
 
• **Historical Context:** Gothic architecture succeeded Romanesque architecture and was later replaced by Renaissance architectural styles, reflecting evolving artistic and engineering advancements.

question: Which temple, built by the Chandela dynasty in the 10th-11th centuries, is known for its exquisite sculptures?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kandariya Mahadeva Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is one of the largest and most ornate Hindu temples in the medieval temple group of Khajuraho, located in Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It was built during the reign of King Vidyadhara of the Chandela dynasty in the 10th-11th centuries.
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and derives its name "Kandariya" from the Sanskrit word meaning "cave" or "mountain," symbolizing Mount Kailash, Lord Shiva's abode.
 
• It is renowned for its intricate sculptures and carvings, which depict various aspects of life, including deities, celestial beings, and scenes of daily life.
 
• The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Khajuraho, famous for its architectural brilliance and erotic sculptures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandela Dynasty:** The Chandela dynasty ruled central India between the 9th and 13th centuries and is known for its patronage of art and architecture, particularly the Khajuraho Group of Monuments.
 
• **Khajuraho Group of Monuments:** This site comprises 85 temples at its peak, with only 22 surviving today, and is divided into three groups: western, eastern, and southern.
 
• **Nagara Style Architecture:** The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is an exemplary example of Nagara-style architecture, characterized by a curvilinear shikhara (spire) and intricate ornamentation.
 
• **Erotic Sculptures:** The temple features sculptures with sensual and erotic themes, which symbolize the Tantric traditions and the celebration of life and human emotions.
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:** The Khajuraho temples were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986, recognizing their cultural and artistic significance.

question: Which of the following correctly pairs a monument with its architectural style?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Qutub Minar - Indo-Islamic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Qutub Minar**, located in Delhi, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the finest examples of Indo-Islamic architecture.
 
• It was initiated by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1192 and completed by Iltutmish, reflecting the architectural blend of Islamic and Indian styles.
 
• The tower is primarily constructed from red sandstone, with intricate carvings of Arabic inscriptions and geometric patterns, showcasing Islamic artistry.
 
• Its tapering structure stands at a height of approximately 73 meters and consists of five distinct storeys.
 
• The Qutub Minar is surrounded by other historically significant structures, such as the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque and the Iron Pillar, adding to its cultural importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Islamic Architecture:**

 
 
• A distinctive blend of Indian and Islamic architectural styles that emerged during the medieval period in India.
 
• Features include domes, minarets, arches, intricate calligraphy, and geometric patterns, often combined with Indian motifs like lotus and floral designs.
 
• Prominent examples include Qutub Minar, Taj Mahal, and Humayun's Tomb.
 
 
 
• **Qutb-ud-din Aibak:**
 
 
• Founder of the Delhi Sultanate and the first ruler of the Slave Dynasty.
 
• Initiated the construction of Qutub Minar as a victory tower to commemorate his conquest of Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Iron Pillar at Qutub Complex:**
 
 
• Located near Qutub Minar, it is a 7-meter-high pillar made of wrought iron and dates back to the Gupta period.
 
• Known for its rust-resistant composition, it is a marvel of ancient Indian metallurgy.
 
 
 
• **Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque:**
 
 
• Situated within the Qutub Complex, it is one of the earliest mosques built in India.
 
• Constructed using materials from 27 demolished Hindu and Jain temples, showcasing the amalgamation of cultural influences.

question:
Consider the following statements about Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves:

1. These caves are near Bhubaneswar and were meant for Jain monks.

2. All caves are shaped like flowers and are carved from independent boulders.

3. Each cave has multiple shrines dedicated to different Buddhist deities.

Which of the above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves** are a group of rock-cut caves located near Bhubaneswar in Odisha, India.
 
• The caves were primarily **meant for Jain monks**, serving as their dwellings and meditation spaces.
 
• These caves are believed to have been commissioned by King Kharavela of the Mahameghavahana dynasty in the 2nd century BCE.
 
• The caves are not shaped like flowers or carved from independent boulders; they are instead **excavated from the hillside**.
 
• While primarily Jain in nature, the caves do not have multiple shrines dedicated to Buddhist deities, making statements 2 and 3 incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jain Influence:**

 
 
• The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves are among the earliest Jain rock-cut architecture in India.
 
• They reflect the ascetic practices and the art patronage of Jainism during the rule of King Kharavela.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Highlights:**
 
 
• The most notable caves include the **Hathi Gumpha (Elephant Cave)**, which has inscriptions detailing King Kharavela's reign, and the **Rani Gumpha (Queen's Cave)**, known for its elaborate carvings.
 
• The caves are adorned with sculptures of Jain Tirthankaras and scenes depicting Jain mythology.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The inscriptions in the caves provide valuable insights into the socio-political and religious landscape of ancient Odisha.
 
• They highlight the spread of Jainism and its integration into local culture during the early Common Era.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Preservation:**
 
 
• The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves are a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
 
• The site attracts tourists and scholars interested in ancient Indian art, history, and religion.

3.Gujarat's architectural style strictly avoided any decorative influence from indigenous practices.
solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gujarat’s medieval architecture displayed a blend of Islamic and local Hindu traditions, integrating features from temple architecture.
 
• Elements like toranas (arched gateways) and bell motifs, commonly found in Hindu temples, were adapted into mosques and tombs during the medieval period.
 
• Regional architectural styles in Gujarat reflected a cultural synthesis rather than strict segregation, rejecting the notion of avoiding indigenous decorative influences.
 
• Gujarat's architecture evolved through the adaptation of local craftsmanship and materials, ensuring a unique regional identity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Toranas**: These are intricately carved arch-like structures that are often associated with Hindu and Jain temples but were incorporated into Islamic architecture in Gujarat.
 
• **Bell Motifs**: Decorative patterns resembling bells, commonly found in temple designs, were adapted in Islamic structures to harmonize aesthetics.
 
• **Cultural Synthesis**: The coexistence of Hindu, Jain, and Islamic architectural elements in Gujarat showcases the region's pluralistic cultural history.
 
• **: Local architectural practices included the use of sandstone and marble, along with intricate carvings, reflecting the craftsmanship of Gujarat.
 
• Solanki Style**: This refers to the architectural style during the Solanki dynasty, which influenced later medieval structures in Gujarat.

• She received numerous accolades, including the Padma Bhushan in 1987 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2002.
 
• Amonkar was also known for her innovative approach and experimentation within the framework of classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Classical Music**

 
 
• It is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• This tradition dates back to the Vedic times, around 1000 BCE.
 
• It is typically performed in two main genres: Dhrupad and Khayal.
 
• Ragas and Talas form the basic framework for improvisation and composition.
 
 
 
• **Gharanas**
 
 
• A gharana is a system of social organization linking musicians or dancers by lineage or apprenticeship, and by adherence to a particular musical style.
 
• Some well-known gharanas in Hindustani classical music include Jaipur-Atrauli, Gwalior, Kirana, and Patiala.
 
• Each gharana has its own unique style and repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• These are one of the highest civilian awards in India, given in various disciplines/fields of activities such as art, social work, public affairs, etc.
 
• They are classified into three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
 
 
• **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana**
 
 
• It was founded by Alladiya Khan in the late 19th century.
 
• This gharana is known for its complex and intricate raga structures.
 
• Prominent exponents include Kesarbai Kerkar, Mogubai Kurdikar, and Kishori Amonkar.

question: Which of the following is a prominent form of Hindustani classical vocal music?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhrupad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dhrupad** is one of the oldest and most prominent forms of Hindustani classical vocal music.
 
• It traces its roots back to the **Samaveda**, one of the ancient Hindu scriptures, which contained melodic chants.
 
• This vocal style is characterized by its emphasis on purity of notes and disciplined melodic progression.
 
• Dhrupad is performed in two parts: **Alap** (a slow and elaborate introduction) and **Bandish** (the composition set to a rhythmic cycle).
 
• Renowned Dhrupad vocalists include the **Dagar family**, who played a pivotal role in preserving and propagating this art form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Classical Music**

 
 
• It is one of the two main traditions of Indian classical music, alongside Carnatic music.
 
• Hindustani music emphasizes improvisation and exploration of ragas (melodic frameworks).
 
• It has evolved over centuries, incorporating influences from Persian and Mughal music traditions.
 
 
 
• **Samaveda**
 
 
• One of the four Vedas, Samaveda is dedicated to chants and melodies.
 
• It is considered the foundational text for Indian musical traditions, including Dhrupad.
 
 
 
• **Ragas in Dhrupad**
 
 
• Dhrupad compositions are based on specific ragas, which define the melodic structure.
 
• These ragas are performed in a meditative and disciplined manner.
 
 
 
• **Instruments Used**
 
 
• Dhrupad performances are often accompanied by the **pakhawaj** (a barrel-shaped drum) and the tanpura (a stringed instrument).
 
• These instruments add rhythm and resonance to the vocal renditions.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Trinity of Camatic Music and choose the correct option:

Statement 1: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Shyama Shastri lived during the 17th century.

Statement 2: The trinity elevated the kriti form to its highest artistic expression.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Statement 1 is incorrect as Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Shyama Shastri, the Trinity of Carnatic Music, lived during the 18th and early 19th centuries, not the 17th century.
 
• Statement 2 is correct because the Trinity is credited with elevating the kriti form of Carnatic music to its highest artistic and devotional expression.
 
• The kriti form is a structured composition that combines intricate melodies (ragas) with profound lyrics, often devotional in nature.
 
• The Trinity's compositions remain central to Carnatic music performances and pedagogy even today.
 
• They contributed significantly to the development and popularization of Carnatic music, making it a sophisticated classical art form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kriti:** A kriti is a composition in Carnatic music that typically consists of three sections – Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam. It is both a melodic and lyrical piece.
 
• **Tyagaraja:** He composed primarily in Telugu and is renowned for his devotion to Lord Rama. His works include the Pancharatna Kritis (Five Gems).
 
• **Muthuswami Dikshitar:** He was known for his Sanskrit compositions and his use of complex ragas. He often invoked deities in his works.
 
• **Shyama Shastri:** He composed in Telugu, Sanskrit, and Tamil and is known for his kritis dedicated to the goddess Kamakshi.
 
• **Carnatic Music:** It is a system of classical music associated with South India, characterized by intricate rhythmic patterns, devotional themes, and improvisational elements.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the structure of Carnatic music compositions and choose correct option:

Statement 1: Varnam is typically performed at the end of a Carnatic concert to summarize key ragas.

Statement 2: Alapana involves improvisational elaboration of a raga without rhythm (tala).
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Carnatic music**, the structure and components of compositions are highly organized and follow traditional patterns.
 
• **Statement 1 is incorrect:** Varnam is not performed at the end of a Carnatic concert. Instead, it is typically performed at the beginning as a warm-up piece to introduce the key raga and set the tone for the concert.
 
• **Statement 2 is correct:** Alapana is an improvisational aspect of Carnatic music that involves the **elaboration of a raga** without rhythm (tala). It is an expressive and free-form exploration of the raga's melodic framework.
 
• **Alapana** focuses on the mood and emotion of the raga, offering the performer creative freedom to showcase the raga's essence.
 
• Varnam, in contrast, is a structured composition that has lyrics and rhythm, typically used as a learning tool for students and as a concert starter.
 
• Alapana is an essential feature of Carnatic music concerts, especially in the presentation of kritis (main compositions).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Varnam**__

 __
 
• Varnam is a type of composition that is primarily used as a practice piece in Carnatic music.
 
• It serves as a foundation for students to master both **raga and tala**.
 
• Varnams are generally performed at the beginning of a concert to warm up the voice and introduce the raga.
 
 
 
• **Alapana**__
 
 
• Alapana is a creative and improvisational aspect of Carnatic music.
 
• It is devoid of lyrics and rhythm and is performed to provide an outline of the raga.
 
• This segment highlights the artist's command over the raga and their ability to innovate within its framework.

__
 
• **Kriti** is a highly structured musical composition in Carnatic music, typically featuring three main sections: Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam.
 
• In Carnatic tradition, Kriti compositions are rich in lyrical content, emphasizing devotion and poetic depth, often set to specific ragas and talas.
 
• **Tillana** is a vibrant and rhythmic composition, frequently used to conclude a Carnatic recital, showcasing intricate rhythmic patterns and syllables.
 
• Tillanas are known for their dynamic nature and focus on rhythmic cadences, often including short phrases of lyrics towards the end.
 
• Both Kriti and Tillana are integral components of the Carnatic music tradition, reflecting its depth and diversity in melodic and rhythmic exploration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic Music:**

 
 
• A classical music tradition from South India characterized by complex compositions and improvisations.
 
• It emphasizes the use of ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
 
 
• **Kriti Compositions:**
 
 
• Often attributed to renowned composers like Tyagaraja, Dikshitar, and Shyama Shastri.
 
• Serve as a medium for spiritual expression and devotion through music.
 
 
 
• **Tillana Compositions:**
 
 
• Typically composed by musicians like Lalgudi Jayaraman and Balamuralikrishna.
 
• Known for their vibrant and rhythmic syllables like "ta", "nam", "dhim", etc.
 
 
 
• 
 
 
• Usually begins with a Varnam, followed by Kriti, Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi, and concludes with Tillana.
 
• Demonstrates the performer's expertise in melody, rhythm, and improvisation.

question: What is a one act play of Sattriya called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ankiya Nat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ankiya Nat:-**

 
 
• **A one-act play of Sattriya is called an Ankiya Nat. It is a form of Assamese one-act play that combines the aesthetic and the religious.**
 
• Ankiya Nats were developed by Sankardev, the 15th-century polymath from Assam, as a way to promote the spiritual values of Vaisnavism.
 
• They are typically performed in Sattras, which are communities of live-in devotees belonging to the Ekasarana dharma, the religion established by Sankardev.
 
• Ankiya Nats are characterized by their use of ballad, dance, and drama. The ballad narrates the story, the dance provides commentary and expression, and the drama brings the characters and themes to life.
 
• The plays are often based on stories from Hindu mythology, but they can also deal with contemporary social and political issues.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ekam Nat:-**

 
 
• Ekam Nat, meaning "one-act play," is a short, self-contained play that typically focuses on a single theme or character.
 
• It is often used as a teaching tool or for entertainment.
 
 
 
• **Vishesham Nat:-**
 
 
• Vishesham Nat, meaning "special play," is a longer and more complex type of Sattriya play.
 
• It typically deals with a historical or mythological story. Vishesham Nats are often performed at festivals and special occasions.
 
 
 
• **Anant Nat:-**
 
 
• Anant Nat, meaning "endless play," is a type of Sattriya play that has no predetermined ending.
 
• The play continues until the audience loses interest or the performers are exhausted. Anant Nats are often improvised and can be very humorous.

• **Kathakali is a form of classical Indian dance-drama which originated in the present-day state of Kerala during the 17th century and has developed over the years. **

• The vocal performance of Kathakali is known as geet or sopanam. It is performed by a group of trained singers who are positioned off-stage and accompany the dancers with their singing.

• **The singing is synchronized with the dance-acting on the stage, and the vocalists help to set the context and express the inner state of the character by modulating their voice.**
 
• For example, anger is expressed by the use of a sharp high voice and pleading is expressed by the use of a sad tone. Music is also central to a Kathakali performance. It sets the mood and triggers emotions resonant with the nature of the scene.

question: Mohi Bahauddin Dagar, a renowned musician, is known for playing which of the following instruments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudra Veena.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Mohi Bahauddin Dagar** is the son of renowned North Indian musician Zia Mohiuddin Dagar, he plays the Rudra veena.
 
• He performs **Dagarbani-style Rudra veena.**
 
• Referring to Nayak Haridas Dagar of the 16th century, he represents the 20th generation of the Dagar dynasty.
 
• He received the highest honour for performing artists in 2012 when the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama, presented him with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Sarangi **

 
• **A bowed stringed instrument with a resonator covered in skin is called a sarangi.**
 
• Typically, a **single block of wood** is used to handcraft a sarangi.
 
• The seventeen sympathetic strings on this instrument are constructed of steel, while the four playing strings are made of goat gut.
 
• The sarangi is a common instrument in India with numerous regional variations, but it plays a significant role in the Hindustani music of North India.
 
• The sarangi is the only musical instrument that can accurately produce all of the nuances of vocal music, including khayal, dhrupad, khayal, thumri, tappa, ghazal, and even bhajan, with embellishments and intonations.

**Sitar**

 
• **Sitar is a plucked stringed instrument, originating from the Indian subcontinent, used in Hindustani classical music.**
 
• The instrument was made of wood. It had a thin violin-type of the bridge and it was played by a plectrum worn on the right hand. It was invented by Amir Khusrau.

**Santoor **

 
• **The Santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer often made of walnut wood and has 72 strings**, which are struck with two delicate carved wooden mallets.
 
• The santoor is essentially a folk instrument that originated in the Kashmir Valley, and it achieved the status of a classical instrument due to the persistent efforts and genius of Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was an Indian famous classical musician, who attained international fame by playing the musical instrument, the santoor.**
 
• With his hard work, determination and talent, Pandit Shivkumar Sharma made the santoor a global name.

__
 
• **Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia:-**

 
 
• **He is an Indian flautist and a prominent figure in the Hindustani classical music tradition. **
 
• Renowned as the "Wizard of the Flute," Chaurasia has captivated audiences worldwide with his mastery of the bansuri, a simple bamboo flute.
 
• Under the tutelage of renowned flautist Bholanath Prasanna of Varanasi, Chaurasia honed his skills for eight years, developing a unique style that blended traditional techniques with his own innovative flair.
 
• Acknowledged for his exceptional contributions to Hindustani classical music, Chaurasia has received numerous accolades from the Government of India.
 
• He was bestowed the Padma Bhushan in 1992 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2000.
 
• His achievements have also earned him prestigious awards such as the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, Dada Saheb Phalke Award, and Padma Shri.

• **Veena:-**

 
 
• The veena is the oldest of the three instruments, and it is thought to have been invented over 5,000 years ago.
 
• It is a versatile instrument that can be used to play a wide variety of music, from devotional hymns to folk songs to complex ragas.
 
• **The veena has a large, hollow body that is made of wood or gourd, and it has four main strings that are played with a metal plectrum.**
 
 
 
• **Sitar:-**
 
 
• The sitar is a more recent invention, dating back to the 16th century.
 
• It is a popular instrument in Hindustani classical music, and it is known for its distinctive sound, which is characterized by its use of sympathetic strings.
 
• **The sitar has a long, narrow neck with a gourd resonator at the top, and it has four main strings and up to 20 sympathetic strings.**
 
 
 
• **Sarod:-**
 
 
• The sarod is another popular instrument in Hindustani classical music, and it is known for its rich, deep sound.
 
• **The sarod is similar to the sitar in many ways, but it has a shorter neck and a different tuning. **
 
• **The sarod has four main strings and up to 15 sympathetic strings.**

• **Chitti Babu** was a renowned veena player from India known for his exceptional skills and contributions to Carnatic music.

• **Veena:**

 
 
• The veena is a traditional Indian string instrument used primarily in Carnatic and Hindustani classical music.
 
• It has a large resonating body and a long neck, typically made from jackwood.
 
• The veena is played by plucking the strings with a plectrum (called a mizrab) and pressing the strings on the frets to produce different notes.
 
• There are several types of veenas, including the Saraswati veena, Rudra veena, and Vichitra veena, each with its unique structure and sound.

• It is one of the two main sub-genres of Indian classical music, the other being Hindustani music.
 
• Carnatic music is known for its complex rhythm patterns (tala) and intricate melodic structures (raga).
 
• It places a strong emphasis on vocal performance, although instrumental performances are also highly regarded.
 
 
 
• **Famous Veena Players:**
 
 
• Besides Chitti Babu, other renowned veena players include E. Gayathri, Dr. S. Balachander, and Veena Jayanthi Kumaresh.
 
• These musicians have contributed significantly to the popularity and evolution of veena music in India and globally.
 
 
 
• **Recognition:**

Statement 1: The Mridangam is a melodic percussion instrument used to outline the raga.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

__
 
• **Statement 1 is incorrect:** The Mridangam is a percussion instrument used to provide rhythmic accompaniment in Carnatic music, not to outline the raga, which is the role of melodic instruments.
 
• **Statement 2 is correct:** The Nadaswaram is a double-reed wind instrument widely used in South Indian classical music, especially in temples and during auspicious occasions such as weddings.
 
• The Nadaswaram is often considered an auspicious instrument, symbolizing traditional and cultural heritage in South Indian ceremonies.
 
• The Mridangam, though crucial in Carnatic music performances, is primarily a rhythm-providing instrument and does not define the melodic structure of the raga.

• It is a double-headed drum made of jackwood, with heads covered by animal skin.
 
• The Mridangam is tuned to the tonic note of the vocalist or lead instrumentalist and is played with the hands.
 
• It is an integral part of Carnatic music concerts, providing complex rhythmic patterns.
 
 
 
• **Nadaswaram:**
 
 
• It is one of the loudest non-brass acoustic instruments and is made of wood, often from the aacha or blackwood tree.
 
• The instrument has a conical bore, which helps produce a rich, resonant tone.
 
• It is traditionally accompanied by the Thavil, a percussion instrument.
 
 
 
• **Raga in Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• Raga is a melodic framework that defines the mood and structure of a composition in Carnatic music.
 
• It is elaborated using melodic instruments such as the violin, flute, or veena, and through vocal improvisation.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• A classical music tradition of South India with a rich history and theoretical foundation.
 
• It is characterized by intricate compositions and improvisational techniques such as alapana, neraval, and swara kalpana.

question: Which of the following is the correct explanation of painting and sculpture of Ajanta and Elora caves?

options.text: They are designed in Persian art form
They are representations of medieval Islamic art
They are symbolic representations of Gods in Judaism.
They are depiction of Buddhist religious art.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They are**__ __**depiction of Buddhist religious art**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ajanta caves, which date back to the 2nd century BCE to 480 CE, are renowned for their exquisite Buddhist murals and sculptures.
 
• The Ellora caves, constructed between the 6th and 9th centuries, also include significant Buddhist artwork alongside Hindu and Jain art.
 
• These caves were used as monasteries, worship halls, and living quarters for Buddhist monks and are rich in iconography of the Buddha and various Bodhisattvas.
 
• The paintings and sculptures in these caves depict scenes from the life of the Buddha as well as Jataka tales, which are stories of the Buddha's previous lives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajanta Caves:**

 
 
• Located in Maharashtra, India, the Ajanta caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The caves were rediscovered in 1819 by a British officer on a hunting expedition.
 
• The artworks are considered masterpieces of Buddhist religious art, influencing Indian art that followed.
 
 
 
• **Ellora Caves:**
 
 
• Ellora is also located in Maharashtra and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The site includes 34 caves excavated from the basalt cliffs, featuring Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain temples and monasteries.
 
• The Kailasa temple (Cave 16) is the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Iconography:**
 
 
• Buddhist art in these caves typically includes depictions of the Buddha, Bodhisattvas, and various scenes from Buddhist scriptures.
 
• The use of symbols such as the lotus flower, the wheel, and the Bodhi tree are prevalent in Buddhist art.
 
 
 
• **Jataka Tales:**
 
 
• These are a voluminous body of literature concerning the previous births of Gautama Buddha in both human and animal form.
 
• The tales are intended to convey moral lessons and are often depicted in the artwork of the Ajanta caves.

question: The sculptures under the Gandhara School of Art were made of stone, terracotta and _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**ivory**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gandhara School of Art flourished during the Kushan period, particularly under the rule of Kanishka the Great in the 1st and 2nd centuries CE.
 
• It is known for blending Greek, Roman, and Indian artistic influences, creating a unique style of Buddhist art.
 
• Sculptures from this school were primarily made from materials like stone, terracotta, and notably ivory.
 
• Ivory was a prized material used for its smooth texture and fine grain, which allowed for intricate detailing in the artwork.
 
• The use of ivory in Gandhara art reflects the high level of craftsmanship and the trade connections of the region with distant lands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhara Region**

 
 
• The Gandhara region covered parts of modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan, particularly the Peshawar Valley and the Swat Valley.
 
• It served as a cultural crossroads for numerous civilizations including Greek, Persian, and Indian.
 
 
 
• **Features of Gandhara Art**
 
 
• Gandhara art is characterized by realistic representation of human figures, attention to anatomical details, and elaborate drapery styles.
 
• The art often depicts scenes from the life of Buddha, along with other Buddhist themes.
 
 
 
• **Influences**
 
 
• The Gandhara School of Art was heavily influenced by Hellenistic (Greek) art, evident in the naturalistic treatment of human figures and the use of contrapposto stance.
 
• Roman art also influenced the style, particularly in the depiction of clothing and physical features.
 
 
 
• **Important Sites**
 
 
• Key archaeological sites of Gandhara art include Taxila, Peshawar, Swat, and Bamiyan.
 
• These sites have yielded numerous artifacts including sculptures, stupas, and monasteries.
 
 
 
• **Significance**
 
 
• The Gandhara School of Art played a crucial role in the spread of Buddhist iconography and religious art across Asia.
 
• Its influence can be seen in the Buddhist art traditions of Central Asia, China, and Japan.

question: What is one of the major benefits of providing Geographical Indication (GI) tags to local products made by rural artisans?

options.text: It increases dependency on imported goods
It helps preserve traditional knowledge and boosts rural incomes
It removes the need for skill development in rural areas
It allows unrestricted copying of the product by other regions

solution:
The correct answer is __**It helps preserve traditional knowledge and boosts rural incomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Geographical Indication (GI) tags** protect the unique identity of products that are deeply rooted in specific regions, ensuring the preservation of traditional knowledge and skills.
 
• GI tags contribute to **increasing the economic value of artisanal products**, which directly boosts rural incomes and promotes economic stability in rural areas.
 
• They prevent unauthorized use of the registered product name, ensuring that **only authorized producers from the designated region** can market the product under the GI tag.
 
• By granting legal protection to traditional products, GI tags **promote sustainable development** and preserve cultural heritage.
 
• Examples of GI-tagged products in India include **Darjeeling Tea, Channapatna Toys, Kanjeevaram Silk, and Madhubani Paintings**, which are globally recognized for their uniqueness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Indication (GI) Definition:**

 
 
• A GI is a sign used on products that have a specific geographical origin and possess qualities or a reputation due to that origin.
 
• It is governed by the **Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999** in India.
 
 
 
• **Legal Protection:**
 
 
• GI registration provides legal protection to the product, preventing misuse by unauthorized producers.
 
• It ensures **global recognition of locally produced goods** and facilitates access to international markets.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Products with GI tags often command a premium price, benefiting rural artisans and farmers economically.
 
• They help in creating **rural employment opportunities** and ensuring fair trade practices.
 
 
 
• **Notable Examples of GI in India:**
 
 
• Handicrafts: Mysore Silk, Pashmina Shawls, Banarasi Sarees.
 
• Agricultural Products: Alphonso Mango, Basmati Rice, Nagpur Orange.
 
• Food Items: Tirupati Laddu, Hyderabadi Haleem.
 
 
 
• **International Recognition:**
 
 
• GI tags are recognized globally under the **WTO's Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS).**
 
• This ensures that products with GI tags are protected in member countries of the WTO.

question: ______ is a form of folk theatre based exclusively on the life of Lord Krishna.
solution:
The Correct Answer is **__Raasleela__. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Raasleela is based exclusively on **Lord Krishna legends.**
 
• It is believed that **Nand Das wrote the initial plays based on the life of Krishna.**
 
• In this theatre form, the dialogues in prose combined beautifully with songs and scenes from Krishna's pranks.
 
• It is a combination of two words- **rasa meaning "aesthetics" and Lila meaning "act," "play" or "dance".**
 
• Two types of Rasleela: **Braj Ras **of Mathura and **Manipuri Ras **of Manipur.
 
• Braj Raasleela is different from Manipuri Rasleela in proposing dance, dialogue, costumes, and style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Nautanki:-**

 
• Nautanki is usually associated with **Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• The most popular centres of this traditional theatre form are Kanpur, Lucknow, and Hathras.
 
• The meters used in the verses are Doha, Chaubola, Chhappai, Behar-e-tabeel.
 
• There was a time when only men acted in Nautanki but nowadays, women have also started taking part in the performances. Among those remembered with reverence is Gulab Bai of Kanpur. She gave a new dimension to this old theatre form.

**Tamaasha:-**

 
• Tamaasha is a traditional folk theatre form of **Maharashtra.**
 
• It has evolved from folk forms such as Gondhal, Jagran, and Kirtan.
 
• Unlike other theatre forms, in Tamaasha the female actress is the chief exponent of dance movements in the play.
 
• She is known as Murki. Classical music, footwork at lightning-speed, and vivid gestures make it possible to portray all the emotions through dance.

**Maach:-**

 
• Maach is the traditional theatre form of **Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• The term Maach is used for the stage itself as also for the play. In this theatre, form songs are given prominence in between the dialogues.
 
• The term for dialogue in this form is bol and rhyme in narration is termed vanag. The tunes of this theatre form are known as rangat.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhikari Thakur was a Bhojpuri author popularly known as the "Shakespeare of Bhojpuri Literature“**.

 
 
• Thakur was born in a barber-family on 18 December 1887 at **Kutubpur (Diyara) Village in Saran District now in Bihar. **
 
• **He is best known for the creation of the twentieth-century theatre form “Bidesia”.**
 
• Bhikari Thakur was a barber (a backward Caste) who abandoned home and hearth to form a group of actors who dealt with issues of confrontation: between the traditional and the modern, between urban and rural, between the haves and the have-nots.
 
• Appreciative native Bhojpuri audiences consider Bhikari Thakur as the incomparable founder father, propagator, and exponent par excellence of this form.
 
• He was a folk poet, a folk singer, a folk dancer, and an actor.
 
• In nineteenth-century when Bhikhari Thakur was struggling to end his meet, he was impressed and inspired by movement carried out then by famous Bengali social reformers such as Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ram Krishna Paramhans & Swami Viveka Nanda. 
 
• **This simple and poor young man, quiet impressed by Bengal’s ‘Punarjagran Andolan’, returned to his native place Qutubpur, and watched, noticed his society’s problems minutely and enriched and enlighten with ideas on every social level which can be seen and felt in his compositions.**
 
• He took ‘the Renaissance spirit’ positively and decided to deliver it to the Bhojpuri society through songs, poems, drama, etc.

• After repeated destruction by several invaders and rulers, reconstructed several times in the past, the present temple was rebuilt in the Chaulukya style of Hindu temple architecture and completed in May 1951.
 
• Under the orders of the **Home Minister of India, Vallabhbhai Patel, **reconstruction began and was completed after his death.
 
• **Narendra Modi**, currently the Prime Minister of India, is the President of the Somnath Mandir Trust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga **is one of the twelve Jyotirlingams, shrines that are said to be Lord Shiva's most sacred abodes, and is a Hindu temple devoted to Lord Shiva. It is situated in the state of Madhya Pradesh in the ancient city of Ujjain.
 
• One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, the most sacred dwellings of Shiva, is the **Vaidyanatha Jyotirlinga temple (Baidyanath Dham)**. It is situated in Deoghar in the state of Jharkhand's Santhal Parganas district.
 
• **The Hindu temple of Omkareshwar** is dedicated to God Shiva. It is one of Shiva's 12 revered Jyotirlinga shrines. It is in the Narmada River on an island called Mandhata or Shivpuri in the Khandwa district of Madhya Pradesh.

question: Which temple is the epicenter for the Rath Yatra in Odisha?
solution:
The correct answer is **Jagannath Puri Temple.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RathaYatra or Ratha Jatra **or Chariot Festival is a Hindu festival associated with Lord Jagannath held at Puri in the state of Odisha, India.
 
• It is the **oldest RathaYatra taking place in India and the World**, whose descriptions can be found in **Brahma Purana, Padma Purana, Skanda Purana and Kapila Samhita.**
 
• The festival is** celebrated on the 2nd day of Shukla Paksha of Ashadh**, the third month, according to the traditional Oriya calendar.
 
• It is a **9 day-long event and marks the return of Lord Krishna to Vrindavan with his brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra to Gundicha Temple via Mausi Maa Temple (maternal aunt's home) near Saradha Bali, Puri.**
 
• The **chariot pulling starts after performing the rituals of 'Chhera pahanra'**.
 
• During the festival, the **three holy chariots carrying idols of Lord Jagannath, his brother Balaram (Balabhadra), and sister Subhadra are pulled by thousands of devotees from India and abroad.**
 
• The Lord Jagannath Rath Yatra is also known as **Car Festival**.
 
• The return journey of the three siblings from Gundicha temple is known as ‘Bahuda Yatra’ (the return journey).
 
• The** Chariot of Lord Jagannath is called 'Nandighosha'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Jagannath Temple:**

__
 
• The temple is believed to be constructed in the **12th century by King Anatavarman Chodaganga Deva of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty.**
 
• Jagannath Puri temple is called** ‘Yamanika Tirtha’ **where, according to the Hindu beliefs, the power of ‘Yama’, the god of death has been nullified in Puri due to the presence of Lord Jagannath.
 
• This temple is called the “**White Pagoda**” and is a **part of Char Dham's pilgrimages (Badrinath, Dwaraka, Puri, Rameswaram).**
 
• There are **four gates to the temple- Eastern ‘Singhdwara’ which is the main gate with two crouching lions, Southern ‘Ashwadwara’, Western 'Vyaghra Dwara, and Northern ‘Hastidwara’.**
 
• There is a **carving of each form at each gate.**
 
• In front of the **entrance stands the Aruna stambha or sun pillar, which was originally at the Sun Temple in Konark.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Chief Minister - Mohan Charan Majhi
 
• Governor - Shri Raghubar Das
 
• Number of Districts - 30

• Diwali is celebrated during the **Amavasya of Kartik month.**
 
• Diwali symbolizes the spiritual victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance.
 
• The festival usually lasts five days and is celebrated during the Hindu lunisolar month Kartika (between mid-October and mid-November).
 
• Diwali is observed on Amavasya (or new moon) the 15th day of the month of Kartika, every year.

 Lohri

 Holi
 
 
 
• Holi is the festival of love or colors that signifies the victory of superior over immoral.
 
• Holi festival is commemorated in February end or starting March.
 
 
 
 

 Makar Sankranti
 
 
 
• It is a festival day in the Hindu calendar, dedicated to the deity Surya (sun).

question: Ullambana festival is primarily celebrated by which of the following communities in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhist.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ullambana is a festival primarily celebrated by the Buddhists following the Mahayana tradition.**
 
• Still, a number of Theravada Buddhists( **Laos, Cambodia, and Thailand**), too, celebrate this jubilee which lasts for around half a month- from the first to the fifteenth of the eighth month of the lunar timetable.
 
• This coincides with the month of July in the **Gregorian timetable.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The first day of the festival is considered the one when the Gates of Hell open and the ghosts are permitted to visit the earth for the **next fifteen days.**
 
• The fifteenth day is Ancestors Day and has the families visiting cemeteries to pay respect to their ancestors.
 
• People also make food offerings to the wandering spirit during this festival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jain:**

 
 
• Jainism is one of the three most ancient persuasions of India, with roots that go back to at least the mid-first century B.C.E.
 
• Today, it's still an integral part of Indian culture.
 
• Jainism teaches that the path to enlightenment is through pacifism and reducing detriment to living effects( including shops and creatures) as much as possible.
 
 
 
• **Parsi:**
 
 
• The Parsis, also known as the Parsees, constitute a subsection of the larger Zoroastrian community who migrated to India from Persia in the 7th century AD during the Arab invasion of their homeland. 
 
 
 
• **Sindhi:**
 
 
• Sindhis are an Indo- Aryan ethnical group who speak the Sindhi language and are native to the province of Sindh in Pakistan.
 
• After the partition of the British Indian conglomerate in 1947, numerous Sindhi Hindus and Sindhi Sikhs migrated to the recently independent Dominion of India and other corridors of the world.

__
 
• **Onam:-**

 
 
• It is th**e most popular festival celebrated in the state of Kerala, India.**
 
• It is a** 10-day harvest festival **that usually falls in the month of August or September.
 
• The festival is marked by various cultural events and traditional activities such as boat races, flower decorations, and feasting.
 
• **Onam is celebrated to honor the legendary king Mahabali and to welcome his annual visit to Kerala. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ugadi:**

 
 
• Ugadi is a major festival celebrated in the southern states of India, especially in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.
 
• It marks the beginning of the Hindu lunar calendar and is celebrated on the first day of the month of Chaitra, which usually falls in March or April.
 
• The festival is also known as Yugadi, which means 'the beginning of a new age.'
 
• It symbolizes the start of a new year and the onset of spring.
 
• On this day, people clean and decorate their homes, wear new clothes, prepare special dishes, and offer prayers to the gods.
 
• They also exchange greetings and gifts with friends and family
 
 
• It is a harvest festival celebrated in the state of Assam.
 
 
 
 
 
• Nuakhai 
 
 
• It is an agricultural festival celebrated by the people of Odisha.
 
• It is the greatest harvesting festival of Odisha.
 
• It is observed to welcome the new rice of the season.
 
• Nua means new and Khai means food i.e. Nuakhai's Hindi meaning is 'new food'. 
 
• ‘Nuakhai’ festival is celebrated one day after the Ganesh Chaturthi festival.__
 
• The festival has a big significance for farmers and the agricultural community.
 
 
 
• **Gudi Padwa****​**
 
 
• Gudi Padwa, which is mostly observed in the state of Maharashtra, ushers in the harvest season.
 
• According to the lunisolar Hindu calendar, Maharashtrians celebrate the day as New Year's Day.
 
• Gudi, which refers to Brahma's flag, and Padwa, Padva, or Paddava, which refers to the first day of the moon's bright phase, are the two terms that make up the phrase "Gudi Padwa."

• Vesak, also known as Buddha Purnima, is another major Buddhist festival that marks the birth, enlightenment, and death of Buddha.
 
• It is celebrated on the full moon day in the month of Vaishakha (April/May).
 
 
 
• **Significance of Saga Dawa**
 
 
• Saga Dawa is believed to multiply the merits of good deeds performed during this month many times over.

• **Traditional Practices**

question: In which year did UNESCO recognize Durga Puja as an Intangible Cultural Heritage?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• UNESCO recognized Durga Puja as an **Intangible Cultural Heritage** in the year **2021**.
 
• Durga Puja was added to UNESCO’s **Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**, highlighting its cultural significance.
 
• The recognition took place during the **16th session of the Intergovernmental Committee** for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage held in December 2021.
 
• This marked a significant milestone for India, as Durga Puja became the **first festival from India** to be included in this prestigious list.
 
• The inclusion showcases the **social practices, rituals, artistry, and festive spirit** surrounding Durga Puja, celebrated predominantly in West Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage:**

 
 
• The Intangible Cultural Heritage list aims to protect and promote cultural elements that are passed down through generations.
 
• It includes practices, representations, expressions, knowledge, and skills that are significant to communities worldwide.
 
• India has several elements inscribed, including Yoga, Kumbh Mela, and the Vedic Chanting.
 
 
 
• **Durga Puja:**
 
 
• Durga Puja is a Hindu festival celebrating Goddess Durga’s victory over the buffalo demon Mahishasura.
 
• It is widely observed in West Bengal, Assam, Odisha, Tripura, and other parts of India.
 
• The festival involves elaborate rituals, artistic idols, pandal decorations, cultural performances, and community participation.
 
 
 
• **Significance of UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• The recognition helps safeguard the cultural practices associated with Durga Puja.
 
• It promotes awareness of the festival globally, enhancing tourism and cultural exchange.
 
• It supports the preservation of traditional craftsmanship and rituals tied to the celebration.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Elements on the List:**
 
 
• India has a rich representation on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list, including Traditional Vedic Chanting, Ramlila, and Chhau Dance.
 
• Yoga and Kumbh Mela are globally recognized as cultural practices with deep roots in Indian tradition.
 
• These elements demonstrate the diversity and richness of India’s intangible heritage.

• It is observed in the **Bhadrapada month** of the Hindu calendar, typically in August or September.
 
• The festival lasts for **10 days**, culminating in the immersion (visarjan) of Ganesha idols in water bodies.
 
• Maharashtra is known for its grand and elaborate celebrations, with public installations of **large Ganesha idols** and cultural events.
 
• The festival was popularized in the 19th century by freedom fighter **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** to unite people during the Indian independence movement.

• He is the son of **Lord Shiva** and **Goddess Parvati**.
 
• His iconic attributes include an **elephant head**, a trunk, and a pot-bellied body, symbolizing wisdom and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Visarjan (Immersion):**
 
 
• The immersion of Ganesha idols signifies the cycle of creation and dissolution in nature.
 
• Eco-friendly idols made of biodegradable materials are increasingly used to prevent water pollution.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak's Role:**

question:

Assertion (A): The jaherthan plays a central role in the sacrificial rituals of Erok Sim.

Reason (R): The jaherthan is a sacred grove believed to be inhabited by spirits, including Jaherera, the Lady of the Sacred Grove.

options.text: Both A and R are correct, but R does not explain A.
Both A and R are correct, and R correctly explains A.
A is correct, but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect, but R is correct.

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The jaherthan is a sacred grove central to the religious practices of the Santhal tribe, particularly during the sacrificial rituals of Erok Sim.
 
• The jaherthan is believed to be inhabited by spirits and deities, including Jaherera, the Lady of the Sacred Grove, who is considered the guardian of the space.
 
• The assertion (A) that the jaherthan plays a central role in sacrificial rituals is correct, as it serves as the primary site for these practices.
 
• The reason (R) is also correct, as the belief in the spirits and deities inhabiting the jaherthan explains its sacredness and central role in rituals.
 
• Thus, both A and R are true, and R provides a valid explanation for A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santhal Tribe**

 
 
• The Santhal tribe is one of the largest tribal communities in India, primarily residing in Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Bihar, and Assam.
 
• They have a rich cultural heritage and follow animistic religious practices, emphasizing the worship of nature and spirits.
 
 
 
• **Jaherthan**
 
 
• The jaherthan, also known as "sacred grove" or "holy grove," is a designated area for worship and rituals among the Santhal tribe.
 
• It is considered a spiritual space where offerings are made to spirits and deities, including the supreme deity, Thakur, and other ancestral spirits.
 
 
 
• **Erok Sim**
 
 
• Erok Sim refers to a significant sacrificial ritual performed by the Santhal tribe to honor spirits and deities and seek their blessings.
 
• These rituals involve animal sacrifices, offerings, and prayers conducted in the jaherthan under the guidance of the village priest (Pahan).
 
 
 
• **Jaherera**
 
 
• Jaherera, also known as the Lady of the Sacred Grove, is a revered deity believed to reside in the jaherthan.
 
• She is considered the protector of the sacred grove and plays a central role in the religious beliefs of the Santhal tribe.

question:
Which of the following is true about the Gudi Padwa festival?

1. It marks the beginning of the Hindu New Year based on the lunisolar calendar.

2. The term Gudi refers to a sacred scripture recited on this day.

3. Traditionally, celebrations begin with the consumption of sweets for good luck.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gudi Padwa** marks the beginning of the Hindu New Year, as per the lunisolar calendar followed in Maharashtra and some other regions of India.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the first day of the Chaitra month, which typically falls in March or April.
 
• The term **"Gudi"** refers to a flag or banner-like structure decorated with a colorful cloth, flowers, and a copper or silver pot, symbolizing victory and prosperity.
 
• It does not involve the recitation of a sacred scripture as implied in the question, nor does the celebration traditionally begin with the consumption of sweets for good luck.
 
• Gudi Padwa is also associated with the arrival of spring and the harvest season, making it a time of joy and renewal for the community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lunisolar Calendar:** The Hindu calendar combines both lunar and solar movements to determine months and years. Gudi Padwa is based on this system.
 
• **Chaitra Navratri:** Gudi Padwa also marks the beginning of Chaitra Navratri, a nine-day festival dedicated to Goddess Durga.
 
• **Symbolism of the Gudi:** The Gudi symbolizes victory and is believed to ward off evil, attract prosperity, and signify the triumph of good over evil.
 
• **Regional Variations:** While Gudi Padwa is celebrated in Maharashtra, similar festivals are observed in other parts of India, such as Ugadi in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, and Cheti Chand among the Sindhi community.
 
• **Cultural Practices:** The festival includes cleaning homes, decorating with rangoli, hoisting the Gudi, and preparing traditional dishes like puran poli and shrikhand.

question: Bihu, the festival of Assam, is celebrated to mark:

options.text: The victory of good over evil

solution:
The correct answer is __**The new harvest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bihu** is the most prominent cultural festival of Assam, celebrated with enthusiasm by all communities.
 
• The festival marks the **harvest season** and is celebrated to express gratitude to nature and honor the hard work of farmers.
 
• There are three main types of Bihu – **Bohag Bihu** (Rongali Bihu), **Magh Bihu** (Bhogali Bihu), and **Kati Bihu** (Kongali Bihu).
 
• **Bohag Bihu**, celebrated in April, marks the Assamese New Year and the beginning of the sowing season.
 
• **Magh Bihu**, celebrated in January, marks the end of the harvesting season and is accompanied by feasting and bonfires.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rongali Bihu:** Celebrated in April, this is the most vibrant and widely celebrated Bihu. It marks the Assamese New Year and the start of the agricultural cycle.
 
• **Bhogali Bihu:** Also known as Magh Bihu, it is celebrated in January after the harvest, signifying a time of abundance and community feasting.
 
• **Kongali Bihu:** Celebrated in October, this marks the end of the sowing season and is a quieter festival with prayers for a good harvest.
 
• The word "Bihu" originates from the Sanskrit word "**Vishuv**", signifying the solar equinox. It is closely tied to the agrarian lifestyle of Assam.
 
• During Bihu, traditional folk dances and songs like the **Bihu dance** and **Bihu geet** are performed to celebrate joy and prosperity.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about Urs at Ajmer Sharif?

options.text: It follows the lunar calendar and marks the saint's death.
It is celebrated annually based on the solar calendar.
It marks the birth anniversary of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti.
It is held only once every five years during Ramzan.

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urs** at Ajmer Sharif is an annual festival commemorating the death anniversary of **Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti**, a revered Sufi saint.
 
• The term **Urs** means "wedding" in Arabic, symbolizing the union of the saint's soul with the divine.
 
• It is observed based on the **lunar calendar**, particularly during the first six days of the Islamic month of **Rajab**.
 
• The festival involves religious rituals, prayers, and devotional music, attracting thousands of pilgrims from **India and abroad**.
 
• The shrine of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, also known as the **Dargah Sharif**, is located in **Ajmer, Rajasthan.**
 
• Visitors offer **chadars (sacred cloth)** to the saint's tomb as an act of reverence and devotion.
 
• Various cultural and spiritual events, including **qawwali performances**, are held during the Urs, creating a vibrant and inclusive atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 2: "It is celebrated annually based on the solar calendar"**__

 __
 
• The **solar calendar** is not used for determining the dates of Islamic festivals, which follow the **lunar calendar**.
 
• Islamic months are shorter than Gregorian months, leading to variations in annual dates.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "It marks the birth anniversary of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti"**__
 __
 
• Urs specifically marks the **death anniversary** of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, not his birth anniversary.
 
• The term "Urs" is a celebration of spiritual union with the divine, which is associated with death rather than birth.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "It is held only once every five years during Ramzan"**__
 
 
• Urs is an **annual event** and is not tied to the month of **Ramzan**.
 
• It is observed in the month of **Rajab**, which is different from Ramzan.

question: Which of the following styles of temple architecture was developed between Himalaya to Vindhya?
solution:
__**Nagara styles**__ of temple architecture was developed between Himalaya to Vindhya

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**** ****Nagara or North Indian Temple Style**

__
 
• In North India, it is common for an entire temple to be built on a** stone platform with steps leading up to it.**
 
• It does not usually have elaborate b**oundary walls or gateways.**
 
• While the earliest temples had just **one tower or shikhara**, later temples had several.
 
• The **garbhagriha **is always located directly under the tallest tower.
 
• There are many subdivisions of nagara temples depending on the shape of the **shikhara.**
 
• The second major type of architectural form in the nagara order is the **phamsana**, which tends to be broader and shorter than Latina ones.
 
• Their roofs are composed of several slabs that gently rise to a single point over the center of the building, unlike the Latina ones which look like sharply rising tall towers.
 
• The third main sub-type of the nagara building is generally called the **valabhi type**.
 
• These are rectangular buildings with a roof that rises into a **vaulted chamber**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Dravida Or South Indian Temple Style**

 
• Unlike the nagara temple, the Dravida temple is enclosed within a compound wall.
 
• The front wall has an entrance gateway in its center, which is known as a **gopuram**.
 
• The shape of the main temple tower known as** vimana in Tamil Nadu **is like a stepped pyramid that rises up geometrically rather than the curving shikhara of North India.
 
• It is common to find a large **water reservoir, or a temple tank, enclosed within the complex.**
 
• Subsidiary shrines are either incorporated within the main temple tower or located as distinct, separate small shrines beside the main temple.
 
• **Kanchipuram, Thanjavur or Tanjore, Madurai, and Kumbakonam are the most famous temple towns of Tamil Nadu, **where, during the 8th-12th centuries, the role of the temple was not limited to religious matters alone.

The correct answer is__** Fatehpur Sikri**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Temples in Vrindavan, near Mathura,** were built in a style similar to the Mughal palaces in Fatehpur Sikri.**
 
• The architecture of the **temples in Vrindavan was influenced by the style **of the Sultanates of Bijapur and Golconda. 
 
• Many buildings in F**atehpur Sikri were influenced by the architectural styles of Gujarat and Malwa. **
 
• Mughal rulers were skilled at adapting regional architectural styles in their buildings. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It enshrines the burial place of the Sufi saint, Salim Chisti (1478 – 1572), a descendant of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti of Ajmer, and who lived in a cavern on the ridge at Sikri.
 
• The mausoleum was constructed by Akbar as a mark of his respect for the Sufi saint.
 
• Fatehpur Sikri is a town in the Agra District of Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• The city itself was founded as the capital of the Mughal Empire in 1571 by Emperor Akbar, serving this role from 1571 to 1585, when Akbar abandoned it due to a campaign in Punjab and was later completely abandoned in 1610.

question: The Vesara style of temple architecture is a combination of which two styles?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravidian and Nagara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vesara style of temple architecture is a **fusion of Dravidian and Nagara styles**, prominently seen in the Deccan region of India.
 
• This style emerged during the rule of the **Chalukyas of Badami** (6th-8th centuries CE) and further evolved under the Hoysalas (12th-13th centuries CE).
 
• **Dravidian style** originated in South India, known for its pyramidal towers (vimanas) and intricately carved structures.
 
• **Nagara style** is a North Indian architectural tradition, characterized by beehive-shaped towers (shikharas) and the absence of elaborate boundary walls.
 
• The Vesara style incorporates a mix of both elements, with **curvilinear towers** and intricate carvings, making it distinct and versatile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:**

 
 
• **Vimana:** The pyramidal tower above the sanctum in Dravidian temples.
 
• **Shikhara:** The curvilinear or pyramidal tower in Nagara temples.
 
• **Garbha Griha:** The sanctum sanctorum where the deity resides in temples.
 
 
 
• The Chalukyas of Badami were instrumental in blending the Nagara and Dravidian styles, resulting in the Vesara style. Examples include the temples at Pattadakal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• Examples of Vesara temples include the **Virupaksha Temple** at Pattadakal and the **Chennakesava Temple** at Belur (Hoysala era).
 
• The Hoysalas further refined the Vesara style, introducing **soapstone carvings** and star-shaped platforms in their temples.
 
• The Vesara style is often referred to as the **"middle style"** due to its geographical and stylistic position between the Dravidian South and Nagara North.

question: The Jamia Masjid in Srinagar does NOT resemble any of the great mosques of the larger Islamic World, owing to the replacement of domes by the multi-tiered roofs in the shape of ______.
solution:
The Correct Answer is __**pyramids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The Jamia Masjid** in Srinagar does NOT resemble any of the great mosques of the larger Islamic world, owing to the replacement of domes by the multi-tiered roofs in the shape of pyramids.
 
• One of the best examples of traditional Kashmiri wooden architectural forms is the** khanqah.**
 
• **INTACH literature** defines it as being entirely made of solid wooden blocks used with brick infill as headers and stretchers.
 
• A double-height hall with a collection of seven small cloisters on both sides, intended for spiritual retreats, is the central room on the ground floor of this 14th-century shrine.
 
• The layout is similar to a Buddhist chaitya hall, while four wooden columns, often seen in the temples of medieval Kashmir, support the ceiling of the central chamber.
 
• A multi-tiered pyramidal roof with an open square pavilion (brangh) in the middle surmounts the entire building. A spire is crowned the brangh, officially establishing the continuity of the practices of Hindu and Buddhist construction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **An unusual combination of vernacular architecture with Mughal elements** is considered to be the **mausoleum-shrine complex of Shaikh Hamza Makhdum,** who was a leading Suharwardi Saint of Kashmir during the 16th century.
 
• It was commissioned in 1600 during Akbar's reign and was renovated in 1703. The shrine combines design techniques such as taq and naqashi ornamental instruments, and a three-tiered pyramidal roof surmounts the main room.

question: Sake, a Japanese alcoholic beverage, is made from fermented______.
solution:
The correct answer is **__rice.__**

__
 
• Sake is a Japanese alcoholic beverage made from** fermented rice**.
 
• Sake is light in **colour, is non-carbonated**, has a sweet flavour, and contains about 14 to 16 per cent alcohol.
 
• It is made in a process known as **multiple parallel fermentation**, in which a grain (rice) is converted from **starch to sugar** followed by conversion to alcohol.
 
• **Special strains of rice are precisely milled** to remove the outer layers, a process that reduces the grain to **50 to 70 per cent** of its original size.
 
• Production begins with **kome-koji**, a preparation of steamed rice and **koji (Aspergillus oryzae)**, a fungus that converts the rice starch to fermentable sugars.
 
• In Japan, where it is the** national beverage**, sake is served with a special ceremony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The soybean is economically the most important bean in the world, providing vegetable protein for millions of people.
