question: Which of the following sites was included in UNESCO’s World Heritage List in July 2019?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaipur City, Rajasthan**__

__
 
• The historic walled city of Jaipur in Rajasthan was founded under the patronage of** Sawai Jai Singh II.**
 
• It was founded in **1727 AD.** 
 
• It is also known as the** Pink City**
 
• Famous tourist spots include Hawa Mahal, Jaigarh Fort, Jal Mahal, City Palace, Jantar Mantar, Nahargarh Fort, and Amer Fort.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• A **World Heritage Site** is a landmark or area with legal protection by an international convention administered by the **United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).**

question: As on 31st May 2020, how many languages enjoy the status of classical language in India?
solution:
The correct answer is__** 6.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** language** that has a **substantial and lengthy corpus** of** written literature**, as well as its **own autonomous literary tradition**, is said to be** classical.**
 
• Classical languages have **advantages** such as the** establishment of study centres** and the **provision of international awards for its scholars.**
 
• **Six languages** currently hold the designation of "Classical":
 
 
• Tamil (announced in 2004),
 
• Sanskrit (2005),
 
• Kannada (2008),
 
• Telugu (2008),
 
• Malayalam (2013), and
 
• Odia (2014).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **criteria for designating** a language as **"Classical"** are as follows:

 
 
• High antiquity of its **early texts/recorded history **over a period of **1500–2000 years;**
 
• A **body of ancient literature/texts, **which is regarded as a **priceless legacy** by** generations of speakers;**
 
• The **literary tradition** be **original and not borrowed** from another speech community;
 
• The classical language and literature **being distinct from modern,** there may also be a** discontinuity **between the classical language and its **later forms or its offshoots."**

question: Which of the following religious communities in India primarily celebrates the Pateti festival?
solution:
The correct answer is Parsi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pateti is the **new year festival** of the Parsis.
 
• Pateti comes from the Persian word '**Patet'** which means '**confession' or 'repentance'.**
 
• On this festival, Parsis mark the beginning of the new year, go to the agyari and spend the day with family members.
 
• The Parsis don’t just believe in celebrating the new year and forgetting about the past. Rather they cherish the past and look back on the year that has passed and ask for repentance.
 
• This generally occurs just before the New year or the last day of the previous year and usually encompasses **5 days **of repentance which has now been reduced to **one**. 
 
• New year's day which historically falls on the **spring equinox** is now celebrated in **mid-August every year**.
 
• The **Shahenshahi** calendar used by the Parsis is itself known as **Nowroz.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Parsi community**

 
 
• **​**One of the most well-known minority communities in the country is the Parsis who follow the **4000-year-old** ancient **Zoroastrianism religion** from **Persia**.
 
• Zoroastrianism spread to the world via the Silk Route and influenced other religions such as Judaism and Christianity. It is a monotheistic religion established by the Prophet Zarathustra who was the contemporary of Cyrus the Great, back in 1200 BC.
 
• The Parsis, came to India after the Arab conquest started. Historians believe that they sailed across the Arabian Sea to reach **Gujarat sometime in 785 AD.** Today, around **60,000** Parsis reside in the country.
 
• The Parsis are a distinctive community in the country who are known for their distinct cuisine and way of life. Many of them such as **Jamshedji Tata** have contributed to building this nation.
 
• This community is predominantly based in the western region, especially in **Maharashtra and Gujarat.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Islam (Muslim) religion -**

 
 
• **Hazrat Muhammad Sahib **was the founder of the Islam religion.
 
• Hazrat Muhammad Sahib was born in Mecca in 570 AD.
 
• Hazrat Muhammad Sahib died in 632 AD. After his death, Islam got divided into two sects called **Sunni and Shia**.
 
• The successors of Prophet Muhammad were called **Khalifa**.
 
 
 
• **Sikh religion -**
 
 
• The credit for the establishment of the Sikh religion goes to **Guru Nanak (the first Guru).** The followers of Guru Nanak are called **Sikhs**.
 
• There are 10 Gurus in Sikhism. 10th Guru was **Guru Govind Singh Ji.**
 
• In **1699** AD, on the day of Baisakhi, Guru Gobind Singh established the **Khalsa Panth.**

question: According to the classification of modern Indian languages, which linguistic family accounts for the largest share of the Indian population?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-European (Aryan)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indo-European (Aryan) linguistic family accounts for the largest share of the Indian population, encompassing major languages like Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, and Urdu.
 
• Approximately 70% of India's population speaks languages belonging to the Indo-European family.
 
• The Indo-European family of languages originated from a common ancestral language known as Proto-Indo-European, which spread across Europe and South Asia.
 
• Hindi, a major Indo-European language, is the most widely spoken language in India and serves as one of the official languages of the Indian government.
 
• The Indo-European linguistic family in India is primarily concentrated in the northern, central, and western regions of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sino-Tibetan (Kirata):** Languages in this family include Manipuri, Bodo, and other tribal languages in northeastern India. It accounts for a smaller share of the population compared to Indo-European and Dravidian families.
 
• **Dravidian:** This linguistic family is prominent in southern India, including languages like Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam. It is the second-largest linguistic family in India.
 
• **Austric (Nishada):** Includes languages like Santali and Mundari, primarily spoken by tribal communities in eastern and central India.
 
• **Indo-European Spread:** The Indo-European languages spread to India during ancient migrations and later evolved into many distinct languages, forming the largest linguistic group in the country.
 
• **Language Demographics:** Census data and linguistic studies consistently show the dominance of Indo-European languages in India's population distribution.

• It is an** organization dedicated to the promotion of literature in the languages of India.**

• The Akademi conducts literary programs and publishes books in all **24 languages.**
 
• It also translates literary works from one Indian language into others to promote a multilingual and inclusive literary environment.
 
• It is the highest literary honor in India, and it confers awards for outstanding works of literary merit.

question: Professor ______, who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2019, is the oldest Nobel laureate ever.
solution:
The correct answer is __**John Goodenough**__.

 
• Nobel Prizes are given in the name of **Sir Alfred Nobel **the inventor of **dynamite **(an explosive device).
 
• It is not a single prize but **5 separate prizes** that are given to those people who have conferred the **greatest benefit to humankind** in the areas of
 
 
• **Physics**
 
• **Chemistry**
 
• **Physiology**
 
• **Medicine**
 
• **Literature**
 
• **Peace**
 
 
 
• Nobel Prizes in **all fields** are given in **Stockholm, Sweden country** except the **Peace Prize **which is awarded in **Norway**.
 
• It was first awarded in **1901**.
 
• The first person to receive the Nobel Prize was **Henry Dunant **for his role in **founding the International Red Cross Movement and initiating the Geneva Convention**.
 
• The first Indian person to receive a Nobel Prize was **Rabindranath Tagore** in the field of **Literature** i.e for his contribution to a collection of **104 poems** called **Gitanjali in 1913**.
 
• The first Indian female to receive Nobel Prize was **Mother Teresa **in **1979 **and the first woman to receive this Prize was **Marie Curie **in **1903** and Marie Curie had won this prize **twice**.
 
• **Amartya Sen **was the first Indian person to receive a Nobel Prize in the field of **Economics **in the year 1998.
 
• Professor **John Goodenough (American Scientist) **was the **oldest person **to receive a Nobel prize in the field of **Chemistry**. i.e at the age of **97 years**.
 
• He was honoured with a Nobel Prize for his valuable contribution to the development of **LIthium-ion batteries**.

question: Who among the following received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1936 for ‘studying the molecular structure through the investigation of dipole moments and the diffraction of X-rays and electrons in gases’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Peter Debye**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Peter Debye**

__
 
• **Peter Debye was the Dutch chemist who best knows his work on X-ray diffraction and dipole moments.**
 
• Some of his notable works are the Debye model, Debye relaxation, Debye frequency, Debye–Huckel equation, Debye-Waller factor​ , etc.
 
• He was the recipient of the **Nobel prize in the year 1936 for his work on X-ray diffraction and dipole moments.**
 
• The magnitude of the dipole moment is given in Debye units to honor him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** ​Arnold Sommerfeld**

 
• Arnold Sommerfeld was a **German physicst. **
 
• He investigated the atomic spectra of the Bohrs Model and concluded that the orbits of electrons in atoms are elliptical.
 
• **The nucleus is one of the foci of this ecliptical path.**
 
• He also introduced the ideas of Azimuthal and magnetic quantum numbers. 

**Paul Hermann Scherrer **

 
• Paul Hermann Scherrer was a **Swiss physicist.**
 
• **In 1916, while still working on his dissertation, he and his tutor, Peter Debye, developed the “Debye–Scherrer powder method”, a procedure using X-rays for the structural analysis of crystals.**
 
• This made an important contribution to the development of the scattering techniques that are still used in the large facilities at the Paul Scherrer Institute to this day.

**Erich Huckel**

 
• Erich Armand Arthur Joseph Huckel was **a German physicist and physical chemist.**
 
• He is known for two major contributions:
 
 
• The** Debye–Huckel theory of electrolytic solutions.**
 
• The Huckel method of approximate molecular orbital calculations on π electron systems.

question: Who among the following is the Padma Shri 2022 awardee Kuchipudi dancer credited with reviving the Kakatiyam dance form?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Padmaja Reddy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Padmaja Reddy is a renowned Kuchipudi dancer who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for her contributions to Indian classical dance.
 
• She is credited with reviving the ancient Kakatiyam dance form, bringing it back into the cultural mainstream.
 
• Her efforts have been instrumental in preserving and promoting this traditional dance form, which was almost forgotten.
 
• Padmaja Reddy has performed extensively both in India and abroad, showcasing the rich heritage of Kuchipudi and Kakatiyam dance.
 
• Her dedication to dance and her innovative choreography have earned her numerous accolades and recognition in the field of performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi**

 
 
• Kuchipudi is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms originating from Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is known for its fast rhythms, fluid movements, and vibrant expressions.
 
• The dance form integrates elements of dance, music, and acting, often telling stories from Indian epics and mythology.
 
• Kuchipudi performances typically include a combination of pure dance (nritta), expressive dance (nritya), and dramatic storytelling (natya).
 
 
 
• **Kakatiyam Dance Form**
 
 
• The Kakatiyam dance form has its roots in the Kakatiya dynasty, which ruled parts of South India in the 12th and 13th centuries.
 
• It is characterized by its unique movements and postures, which are different from mainstream classical dance forms.
 
• The dance form was largely forgotten over the centuries and has been revived thanks to the efforts of dedicated dancers like Padmaja Reddy.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri Award**
 
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India.
 
• It is awarded to individuals for their distinguished contributions in various fields such as arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• Instituted in 1954, the award recognizes exceptional and distinguished service in any field.
 
• Recipients of the Padma Shri are announced annually on Republic Day.

question: Who was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature for Geetanjali?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabindranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature for his collection of poems, **Geetanjali**, in 1913.
 
• The Nobel Prize was awarded to Tagore for his "profoundly sensitive, fresh, and beautiful verse," making him the first non-European to receive this honor.
 
• **Geetanjali**, also known as "Song Offerings," is a collection of 103 poems originally written in Bengali and later translated into English by Tagore himself.
 
• Tagore was not only a poet but also a novelist, painter, philosopher, and composer who made significant contributions to Indian and global literature.
 
• His Nobel Prize brought Indian literature into the global spotlight, establishing Tagore as an international literary figure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabindranath Tagore:**

 
 
• Born on 7 May 1861 in Kolkata, Tagore was a polymath who reshaped Bengali literature, music, and art.
 
• He founded **Visva-Bharati University** at Santiniketan, which became a center for cultural and educational exchange.
 
 
 
• **Geetanjali:**
 
 
• Originally written in Bengali, Tagore translated it into English, which led to his Nobel Prize recognition.
 
• The work reflects themes of spirituality, divine love, and human connection.
 
 
 
• **The Nobel Prize:**
 
 
• Established by Alfred Nobel in 1895, it is awarded annually in categories like Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore’s Nobel Prize in 1913 was the first for an Asian in the Literature category.
 
 
 
• **Tagore's Legacy:**
 
 
• Tagore composed the national anthems of both India ("Jana Gana Mana") and Bangladesh ("Amar Shonar Bangla").
 
• He remains a revered figure in Indian and world literature, continuing to inspire generations with his works.

question: Which analytical inference best explains why Prof. Govindarajan Padmanabhan received the Vigyan Ratna award in Biological Sciences?

options.text: For elucidating malaria parasite metabolism and boosting biotech start-ups
For promoting chemical synthesis in pharma

solution:
The correct answer is __**For elucidating malaria parasite metabolism and boosting biotech start-ups**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Prof. Govindarajan Padmanabhan is renowned for his **pioneering research on malaria parasite metabolism**, which has significantly contributed to the understanding of the disease’s biochemistry.
 
• He identified key **metabolic pathways in the malaria parasite Plasmodium**, which are crucial for its survival and offer potential targets for drug development.
 
• His work has played a pivotal role in driving research and innovation in **biotechnology-based start-ups**, particularly in the field of infectious diseases.
 
• He has been associated with promoting **biomedical research and innovation** in India, fostering the development of cutting-edge technologies and therapeutics.
 
• The Vigyan Ratna award recognizes his **extraordinary contributions to biological sciences** and his efforts in translating fundamental research into applied technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Malaria Parasite Metabolism:**

 
 
• The metabolism of Plasmodium involves unique pathways such as the **heme biosynthesis pathway** and **polyamine biosynthesis**, which are absent or significantly different in humans, making them attractive drug targets.
 
• The parasite's reliance on host hemoglobin degradation and its detoxification of heme are critical for its survival.
 
 
 
• **Biotechnology and Start-ups:**
 
 
• Biotech start-ups play a crucial role in transforming fundamental research into practical applications such as diagnostics, vaccines, and therapeutics.
 
• India has witnessed a surge in biotech entrepreneurship due to initiatives like **Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC)**.
 
 
 
• **Vigyan Ratna Award:**
 
 
• This award is conferred to recognize exemplary contributions in the field of science and technology.
 
• It highlights the importance of translating scientific research into applications that address societal needs.
 
 
 
• **Plasmodium and Malaria:**
 
 
• Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, transmitted through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• It remains a significant global health challenge, with ongoing efforts to develop effective vaccines and treatments.
 
 
 
• **Drug Development in Malaria:**
 
 
• Discoveries in parasite metabolism have led to the development of drugs like **artemisinin** and its derivatives.
 
• Targeting metabolic pathways unique to the parasite minimizes the risk of harming human cells.

question: The "Golden Boot" is awarded in which sport ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Football**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Golden Boot" is awarded to the top goal scorer in football tournaments, including major events like the FIFA World Cup and UEFA European Championship.
 
• The award recognizes individual excellence in scoring goals and is a prestigious accolade in football.
 
• The Golden Boot is determined based on the number of goals scored by a player during the competition. If tied, assists and minutes played may be considered.
 
• Prominent footballers like Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, and Harry Kane have earned the Golden Boot in various tournaments.
 
• The award encourages players to perform exceptionally in front of the goal and contributes to the excitement of competitive football tournaments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FIFA World Cup Golden Boot:**

 
 
• This award is given to the highest goal scorer in the FIFA World Cup tournament.
 
• Past winners include Miroslav Klose (Germany), James Rodríguez (Colombia), and Harry Kane (England).
 
• The award was first introduced in the 1982 FIFA World Cup as the "Golden Shoe," later renamed the "Golden Boot."
 
 
 
• **UEFA Champions League Top Scorer:**
 
 
• While not officially called the Golden Boot, UEFA recognizes the top scorer in its Champions League tournament annually.
 
• Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have dominated this category for years.
 
 
 
• **Golden Boot in Domestic Leagues:**
 
 
• Many domestic leagues, such as the English Premier League and La Liga, award a Golden Boot to their top scorer each season.
 
• It symbolizes exceptional performance and goal-scoring prowess in league competitions.
 
 
 
• **Golden Boot Criteria:**
 
 
• If players are tied in goals scored, the number of assists and total minutes played are often used as tie-breakers.
 
• This ensures fairness in determining the most impactful player.

question: In which of the following categories did Anindita Neogy Anaam receive National Nritya Shiromani award?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anindita Neogy Anaam;-**

 
 
• **She is a renowned Indian classical dance Kathak artist, instructor, performer, and choreographer.**
 
• She is currently based in Wisconsin, United States, and is widely recognized for her exceptional talent and contributions to the field of Kathak dance. 
 
• **Anindita Neogy Anaam's dedication and passion for Kathak have garnered her numerous accolades, including the prestigious Shri Jayadev Rashtriya Yuva Puraskar, Bidagdha Nartaki Samman, and National Nritya Shiromani awards.**
 
• She is also a coveted Indian Raga Fellow, recognizing her profound understanding and mastery of Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **National Nritya Shiromani Award:-**
 
 
• It is an annual award bestowed upon exceptional classical dancers and musicians of India for their contribution to art and culture.
 
• The award is conferred by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri:-**

 
 
• **It is a classical Indian dance form originating from the state of Manipur in northeastern India. **
 
• It is characterized by its graceful and fluid movements, which are often accompanied by narrative chanting and choral singing.
 
• The dance is traditionally performed by women, who wear colorful costumes and adorn themselves with intricate jewelry.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam:-**
 
 
• **It is one of the oldest and most well-known classical Indian dance forms. **
 
• It originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu, in southern India, and is considered to be a sacred dance form.
 
• Bharatanatyam is characterized by its expressive hand gestures, intricate footwork, and rhythmic patterns.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi:-**
 
 
• **It is another well-known classical Indian dance form, originating in the state of Andhra Pradesh, in southeastern India. **
 
• It is characterized by its expressive facial expressions, intricate footwork, and dynamic movements.
 
• Kuchipudi is often performed in groups, and it is known for its storytelling and theatrical elements.

question: Who among the following had written the novel ‘Untouchable’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mulk Raj Anand**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mulk Raj Anand's 'Untouchable' is a novel about a day in the life of one of **India's lowest untouchables, sweepers who clean up the excreta left by the poor who do not have access to toilets or even outhouses.**
 
• It narrates the sufferings and humiliations of an **18-year-old boy, Bakha, born in a low-caste and serving as a toilet sweeper.**
 
• At that time, the caste system had been in place for over two thousand years. Society was divided into four tiers of privilege. The highest ranks comprise the wealthy, the intellectuals, and other positions of power.
 
• The Untouchables were actually even lower than the lowest caste, comprising a fifth class outside of rank, and are seen as filthy, even to the point of being able to pollute upper caste members through their touch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mulk Raj Anand (1905 – 2004) along with** R. K. Narayan (1906 – 2001), Ahmad Ali (1910 -1994), and Raja Rao (1908 – 2006)** is considered some of the pioneers of Indo-Anglian fiction.

 
 
• He was known for his depiction of the lives of the poorer castes in traditional Indian society and was one of the first India-based writers in English to gain an international readership. 
 
• He was a recipient of the Padma Bhushan.

question: Which of the following books was NOT written by Jyotiba Phule?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Untouchables**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Untouchables was **not written by Jyotiba Phule.**
 
• **Jyotiba Phule wrote Gulamgir**i, Shetkaryacha Asud, and other books. 
 
• Jyotirao Govindrao Phule (1827-1890)** was a social reformer and writer from Maharashtra, India.**
 
• He was a** leader of the non-Brahmin movemen**t and fought against caste restrictions.
 
• He also worked for** women's education and the rights of low-caste people. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **The Untouchables**

 
 
• This refers to the group of people historically known as "Dalits" or "untouchables" in the caste system of India.
 
• The term was used by social reformers to describe those outside the traditional four-fold caste system.
 
 
 
• **Gulamgiri**
 
 
• **"Gulamgiri"** (translated as "Slavery") is a famous book written by **Jyotirao Phule** in 1873.
 
• In this work, Phule critiques the social structure of caste discrimination and exposes the exploitation of the lower castes by the higher castes and the Brahminical system.
 
 
 
• **Shetkaryacha Asud**
 
 
• **"Shetkaryacha Asud"** (translated as "The Farmer’s Whipcord") is a Marathi book written by **Narayan Meghaji Lokhande**.
 
• The book is a call to action for the rights and betterment of farmers, focusing on their struggles and exploitation.
 
 
 
• **Brahmananche Kasab**
 
 
• **"Brahmananche Kasab"** (translated as "The Brahmin's Slave") is another work by **Jyotirao Phule**.
 
• It critiques the upper caste Brahmins who held power and perpetuated the social and economic exploitation of lower castes.

• **S Somanath** assumed charge as the Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in January 2022.
 
• Prior to this role, he was the Director of the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) in Thiruvananthapuram.
 
• S Somanath succeeded **K Sivan**, who served as ISRO Chairman from January 2018 to January 2022.
 
• S Somanath has a strong background in aerospace engineering, particularly in the area of launch vehicle design and development.
 
• He has been associated with ISRO since 1985 and has contributed significantly to various space missions, including the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) and the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**

 
 
• ISRO is the space agency of the Government of India, headquartered in Bengaluru.
 
• Founded in 1969, its vision is to "harness space technology for national development while pursuing space science research and planetary exploration."
 
• ISRO has launched numerous missions, including the Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan missions, which have significantly contributed to space research and exploration.
 
• ISRO operates a series of satellite launch vehicles, including the PSLV and GSLV, to deploy satellites into various orbits.
 
 
 
• **Launch Vehicles**
 
 
• The PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) is known for its reliability and versatility in deploying satellites into polar orbits.
 
• The GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) is used for launching heavier payloads into geostationary orbits.
 
• ISRO is also developing the GSLV Mk III, which is intended for future crewed space missions under the Gaganyaan program.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan Missions**
 
 
• Chandrayaan-1, launched in 2008, was India's first lunar probe and helped confirm the presence of water/hydroxyl on the Moon.
 
• Chandrayaan-2, launched in 2019, aimed to explore the lunar south pole region with an orbiter, lander, and rover, although the lander crash-landed.
 
 
 
• **Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)**
 
 
• Launched in 2013, it made India the first Asian country to reach Mars orbit and the first nation globally to do so on its first attempt.
 
• The mission's primary objective was to develop the technologies required for interplanetary missions.

question: Which of the following is the specific port facility within Chabahar Port that India is primarily developing and operating?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shahid Beheshti Port**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India is primarily developing and operating the **Shahid Beheshti Port**, which is one of the two terminals at Chabahar Port, Iran.
 
• The development of Shahid Beheshti Port is part of India's strategy to create a trade and transit corridor to Afghanistan and Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan.
 
• India Ports Global Limited (IPGL), a joint venture between the Shipping Corporation of India and Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust, is responsible for managing the Shahid Beheshti Port.
 
• The port is critical for India's connectivity initiatives, including the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC), which aims to reduce transportation time and costs between India, Iran, Russia, and Europe.
 
• India has committed to investing in the modernization and expansion of the Shahid Beheshti Port, including the supply of equipment and financial resources for its operational efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chabahar Port:**

 
 
• Chabahar Port is located in southeastern Iran, along the Gulf of Oman, and consists of two terminals: Shahid Beheshti and Shahid Kalantari.
 
• The port is strategically important as it provides Iran with direct access to the Indian Ocean and allows India to bypass Pakistan for trade with Afghanistan.
 
• Chabahar is considered a gateway for regional cooperation among India, Iran, and Afghanistan.
 
 
 
• **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC):**
 
 
• INSTC is a 7,200 km-long multimodal transportation network linking India with Russia and Europe through Iran.
 
• It aims to reduce the cost and time of freight transport compared to the traditional Suez Canal route.
 
 
 
• **India Ports Global Limited (IPGL):**
 
 
• IPGL was established by the Indian government to enhance its overseas port operations and investments.
 
• It plays a key role in India's involvement in the development of the Shahid Beheshti Port at Chabahar.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Importance:**
 
 
• Chabahar Port provides India with an alternative to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) and Gwadar Port in Pakistan.
 
• It is vital for India's energy security and trade diversification in the region.

question: Which pair is correctly matched with India's geopolitical interest?

options.text: SAGAR Policy - Maritime ties in the Indian Ocean

solution:
The correct answer is __**SAGAR Policy - Maritime ties in the Indian Ocean**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SAGAR Policy stands for **Security and Growth for All in the Region**, which emphasizes India's strategic vision for the Indian Ocean Region (IOR).
 
• It was **introduced in 2015** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to enhance maritime cooperation and ensure security in the Indian Ocean.
 
• The policy aims to safeguard India’s maritime interests, promote sustainable economic growth, and enhance connectivity in the Indian Ocean region.
 
• It focuses on **strengthening maritime ties with IOR littoral states**, disaster risk management, and combating maritime threats like piracy and terrorism.
 
• Key components include promoting **blue economy initiatives**, ensuring maritime safety, and fostering bilateral and multilateral partnerships in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Ocean Region (IOR):**

 
 
• The IOR is a strategically significant region connecting Asia, Africa, and Oceania.
 
• It houses critical sea lanes that facilitate global trade, carrying nearly **80% of the world’s seaborne oil trade**.
 
• India’s geographical location places it at the center of the IOR, making maritime security vital for its interests.
 
 
 
• **Blue Economy:**
 
 
• The blue economy refers to the sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth, improved livelihoods, and ocean ecosystem health.
 
• It includes sectors like fisheries, renewable energy, maritime transport, and tourism.
 
• India has been actively promoting blue economy initiatives under the SAGAR policy framework.
 
 
 
• **Maritime Security Threats:**
 
 
• Maritime threats in the IOR include piracy, illegal fishing, terrorism, and trafficking of arms, drugs, and humans.
 
• India collaborates with regional partners to counter these threats and ensure secure sea lanes.
 
 
 
• **BIMSTEC vs SAGAR:**
 
 
• BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) focuses on regional cooperation among South and Southeast Asian countries.
 
• In contrast, SAGAR is specifically centered on maritime ties and security in the Indian Ocean Region.

question: The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) is often viewed as a strategic counter-initiative to which other major global connectivity projects?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) is designed to enhance connectivity and promote economic integration between India, the Middle East, and Europe.
 
• IMEC is widely regarded as a strategic counter-initiative to China's ambitious Belt and Road Initiative (BRI).
 
• The BRI, launched by China in 2013, aims to build a global network of infrastructure and trade routes, connecting Asia, Africa, and Europe.
 
• IMEC focuses on creating alternative trade routes and fostering partnerships that align with democratic values and transparent economic practices.
 
• By emphasizing connectivity, IMEC seeks to reduce reliance on China's BRI and provide nations with a more diversified and competitive economic framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI):**

 
 
• An infrastructure development and investment initiative launched by China in 2013.
 
• Aims to create a network of trade routes connecting Asia, Europe, and Africa, often referred to as the "New Silk Road."
 
• BRI includes projects like railways, highways, ports, and energy pipelines, funded by Chinese loans.
 
• Critics often cite concerns about debt traps and lack of transparency in BRI projects.
 
 
 
• **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC):**
 
 
• IMEC was unveiled during the G20 Summit in September 2023, involving India, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the EU, and other partners.
 
• Aims to connect India to Europe via the Middle East through rail and shipping networks.
 
• Focuses on sustainable development, clean energy, and digital connectivity.
 
• Seeks to offer an alternative to China's BRI for global infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of IMEC:**
 
 
• Enhances geopolitical influence of participating nations by creating a new trade route.
 
• Strengthens economic ties between India, the Middle East, and Europe.
 
• Promotes transparent and inclusive economic practices compared to BRI.
 
 
 
• **Global Connectivity Initiatives:**
 
 
• Other notable initiatives include the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), Asia-Africa Growth Corridor (AAGC), and the Global Gateway by the EU.
 
• These efforts aim to foster sustainable trade and development while reducing dependency on specific countries or regions.

To improve connectivity with Eurasia via multimodal routes

solution:
The correct answer is __**To improve connectivity with Eurasia via multimodal routes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) is a **multimodal transportation network** involving sea, rail, and road routes for moving goods between India, Iran, Russia, and Europe.
 
• The primary goal is to **enhance connectivity with Eurasia**, facilitating trade and economic integration between India and countries in Central Asia, the Caucasus region, and Russia.
 
• INSTC offers an alternative route to traditional maritime shipping via the Suez Canal, **reducing transit time and transportation costs** significantly.
 
• This initiative is pivotal for India's **geo-economic and geopolitical strategy**, enabling better access to untapped markets in Eurasia and boosting regional connectivity.
 
• India's involvement in INSTC strengthens its position in global supply chains and **promotes regional cooperation**, particularly with Iran and Russia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multimodal Transport:** Refers to the use of more than one mode of transport (e.g., rail, road, sea) to move goods, ensuring efficient logistics and reduced costs.
 
• **Eurasia:** A geopolitical term for the combined continental landmass of Europe and Asia, which includes key markets for trade and energy resources.
 
• **Suez Canal Route:** Traditionally used for India-Europe trade, it is longer and more expensive compared to the INSTC's proposed alternative.
 
• **Strategic Partners:** Countries like Iran, Azerbaijan, and Russia play crucial roles in the INSTC, offering key transit points and infrastructure support.
 
• **Trade Benefits:** INSTC is expected to reduce transit time between India and Russia by up to 40% and lower transportation costs by up to 30%, making it a game-changer for regional trade.

• Key strategic initiative to boost India’s trade and connectivity within the Eurasian region.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Significance of Chabahar Port**
 
 
• Chabahar provides India a foothold in Iran, enhancing its strategic and economic presence in the region.
 
• The port counters China’s Belt and Road Initiative by offering an alternative trade route.
 
• It strengthens India-Afghanistan connectivity, especially for humanitarian aid and trade.
 
 
 
• **India’s Connect Central Asia Policy**
 
 
• Launched in 2012 to deepen engagement with Central Asian nations.
 
• Focuses on energy security, trade, cultural ties, and regional connectivity.
 
• Chabahar Port is a key infrastructure development under this policy.
 
 
 
• **India-Iran Relations in Context of Chabahar**
 
 
• India and Iran signed agreements for port development and strategic cooperation in 2016.
 
• Iran’s Chabahar Port complements India’s foreign policy objectives for regional stability and connectivity.
 
• Sanctions on Iran have posed challenges but efforts to mitigate them are ongoing.

question: Which of the following is NOT included in the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022?

options.text: Decision to expand the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) governing council
Setting up of a carbon credit trading scheme
A non-fossil-fuel mandate for designated consumers
Reducing the purview of energy consumption standards

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reducing the purview of energy consumption standards.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022:-**

 
 
• **It aims to strengthen the regulatory framework for energy efficiency and conservation in India, not reduce the purview of energy consumption standards. **
 
• In fact, the bill expands the scope of energy consumption standards by empowering the central government to specify energy efficiency standards for a wider range of appliances and equipment.
 
• **Decision to expand the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) governing council:-**
 
 
• The bill does expand the BEE governing council to include more representatives from industry, academia, and non-governmental organizations.
 
 
 
• **Setting up of a carbon credit trading scheme:-**
 
 
• The bill introduces a carbon credit trading scheme to promote the use of renewable energy and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
 
 
 
• **Non-fossil-fuel mandate for designated consumers:-**
 
 
• The bill mandates that designated consumers, such as industries, commercial buildings, and the transport sector, must meet a minimum share of their energy consumption from non-fossil sources.

question: What is the purpose of the two-day Hands-on Training Workshop on the e-SAKSHI Portal held in June 2024?

options.text: To demonstrate biometric tracking of MPLAD assets
To train officials on the revised fund flow procedure under MPLAD Scheme
To launch a new e-commerce platform for district development
To train MPs in drafting local development plans

solution:
The correct answer is __**To train officials on the revised fund flow procedure under MPLAD Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The two-day Hands-on Training Workshop on the e-SAKSHI Portal was organized to **train officials on the revised fund flow procedure under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development (MPLAD) Scheme.**
 
• The workshop focused on equipping officials with the knowledge and skills to **navigate and utilize the e-SAKSHI portal** effectively for monitoring MPLAD projects.
 
• The revised fund flow procedure aims at **greater transparency and efficiency** in the disbursement and utilization of MPLAD funds.
 
• Participants were trained on the **digital processes** required for project approval, fund allocation, and monitoring progress through the portal.
 
• The initiative is part of the government’s push towards **digitization and accountability** in public schemes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MPLAD Scheme:**

 
 
• Launched in 1993, the MPLAD Scheme enables Members of Parliament to recommend development projects in their constituencies.
 
• The scheme focuses on creating durable community assets such as roads, schools, health centers, and drinking water facilities.
 
• Each MP is allocated a fixed amount annually to implement development works.
 
 
 
• **e-SAKSHI Portal:**
 
 
• The e-SAKSHI portal is an online platform designed to **track and monitor MPLAD projects** in real-time.
 
• It ensures **transparency and accountability** in project implementation by providing stakeholders with access to project updates.
 
• The portal is aligned with the government’s vision of leveraging technology for better governance.
 
 
 
• **Fund Flow Procedure:**
 
 
• The revised fund flow procedure under MPLAD Scheme emphasizes **direct electronic transfer of funds** to implementing agencies.
 
• This minimizes delays and ensures timely utilization of allocated resources.
 
 
 
• **Training Workshops:**
 
 
• Workshops like these are critical for **capacity building** among government officials.
 
• They help in the **adoption of new technologies and procedures** for efficient governance.

question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to Thiru K. Kamaraj on his birth anniversary. He is remembered for his contributions to which of the following areas?

options.text: Freedom struggle and social welfare governance

solution:
The correct answer is __**Freedom struggle and social welfare governance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thiru K. Kamaraj, popularly known as the "Kingmaker," was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and politician from Tamil Nadu.
 
• He played a vital role in India's freedom struggle, participating in movements such as the Non-Cooperation Movement and the Quit India Movement.
 
• Kamaraj was instrumental in introducing mid-day meals and free education in Tamil Nadu, laying the foundation for social welfare governance.
 
• His efforts significantly improved literacy rates and access to education for the underprivileged in Tamil Nadu.
 
• He served as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu from 1954 to 1963 and focused on developmental policies, including rural electrification and industrialization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**

 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, this movement aimed at boycotting British goods, titles, and institutions.
 
• Kamaraj joined the movement and actively participated in protests against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Mid-Day Meal Scheme:**
 
 
• Kamaraj introduced the mid-day meal scheme in Tamil Nadu during his tenure as Chief Minister.
 
• It aimed at improving school enrollment and reducing dropout rates among underprivileged children.
 
 
 
• **Rural Electrification:**
 
 
• Kamaraj prioritized electrification of villages in Tamil Nadu, boosting agricultural productivity and rural development.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• He is remembered as a leader who remained committed to social welfare and development.
 
• The "Kamaraj Plan" encouraged senior leaders to resign from ministerial positions to focus on party work, emphasizing organizational strength.

question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to Mahatma Jyotiba Phule on his birth anniversary. Phule is best known for his contributions to which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Social Reform and Anti-Caste Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Jyotiba Phule was an Indian social reformer, thinker, and writer who significantly contributed to the **abolition of the caste system** and the upliftment of marginalized communities.
 
• He, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, pioneered the cause of **women's education in India**, establishing the first school for girls in Pune in 1848.
 
• Phule is best known for his efforts to eradicate untouchability and caste-based discrimination through his writings and activism.
 
• He founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** (Society of Truth Seekers) in 1873 to promote social equality and fight against caste oppression.
 
• Jyotiba Phule's literary works, such as "Gulamgiri" (Slavery), criticized the social hierarchies and supported the empowerment of oppressed communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anti-Caste Movement:** It refers to the various social and political movements that aimed to eradicate caste-based discrimination and untouchability in India, led by reformers like Jyotiba Phule, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and Periyar.
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj:** Founded by Phule in 1873, this organization worked for the rights of women, Dalits, and other marginalized communities, emphasizing the need for education and social reform.
 
• **Savitribai Phule:** Jyotiba’s wife and collaborator, she was one of India's first female educators and a key figure in the movement for women's rights and education.
 
• **Gulamgiri (Slavery):** A book written by Phule in 1873, it draws parallels between the oppression of African slaves and India’s lower castes, calling for social justice and equality.
 
• **Legacy:** Jyotiba Phule's contributions to social reform laid the foundation for later movements against caste discrimination, inspiring leaders like Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in the Indian freedom struggle and social justice movement.

question: According to Section 21 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha sanhita, 2023, which of the following statements is correct regarding the | trial of offences under Sections 64 to 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?

options.text: The trial must be conducted by any police officer of the rank of DSP and above.
These offences must be tried only in a High Court under a male judge.
Such offences are exclusively triable by Executive Magistrates.
These offences shall, as far as practicable, be tried by a court presided over by a woman.

solution:
The correct answer is __**These offences shall, as far as practicable, be tried by a court presided over by a woman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Section 21 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 emphasizes gender inclusivity in judicial proceedings.
 
• Offences under Sections 64 to 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 are recommended to be tried by courts presided over by women to ensure sensitivity in handling specific cases.
 
• The provision aims to promote a gender-balanced judiciary and foster trust among vulnerable communities.
 
• Although not mandatory, this guideline is designed to ensure fairness and representation in the trial process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023:** This code consolidates laws related to criminal procedures, emphasizing efficiency and justice.
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:** A comprehensive legal framework replacing the Indian Penal Code, focusing on modernization and inclusivity.
 
• **Gender Inclusivity in Judiciary:** Promoting female judges ensures sensitivity in handling gender-based crimes and fosters balanced representation.
 
• **Executive Magistrates:** Officials with administrative authority who occasionally oversee specific legal matters, distinct from judicial magistrates.
 
• **Judicial Reforms in India:** The introduction of updated legal codes like Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita reflects a shift toward modernizing India's judicial system.

question: What is the maximum time limit for completing the trial of a case under the POCSO Act?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, trials of cases involving child sexual abuse must be completed **within one year** from the date of cognizance by the court.
 
• The time limit aims to ensure speedy justice to the victims of child abuse and prevent prolonged trauma.
 
• This provision is mandated under **Section 35** of the POCSO Act, 2012, which emphasizes the importance of expediting child-related cases.
 
• The Act requires that all proceedings, including evidence collection and judgment, are conducted in a **child-friendly manner** to minimize distress for the victim.
 
• The one-year time frame is part of broader measures introduced to strengthen the judicial framework for protecting children’s rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012:**

 
 
• The POCSO Act was enacted to address the issue of sexual exploitation and abuse of children and provides safeguards for children at every stage of the judicial process.
 
• It defines a "child" as any person below the age of 18 years.
 
• The Act is gender-neutral and applies to offenses committed against both boys and girls.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to the POCSO Act:**
 
 
• The POCSO Act was amended in 2019 to include stricter punishments, including the death penalty, for sexual offenses against children.
 
• The amendment also aimed at ensuring faster trials and reducing delays in delivering justice.
 
 
 
• **Special Courts under POCSO:**
 
 
• The Act mandates the establishment of Special Courts to exclusively handle POCSO cases to ensure a child-sensitive judicial process.
 
• These courts are equipped with trained professionals to handle child witnesses and evidence collection.
 
 
 
• **Child-friendly Procedures:**
 
 
• POCSO emphasizes that the statement of the child victim should be recorded at their residence or a place of their choice in the presence of a trusted adult.
 
• Cross-examinations are conducted in-camera to prevent further trauma to the child.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Obligations:**
 
 
• The Act makes it mandatory for any person with knowledge of a child being sexually abused to report the incident to the police.
 
• Failure to report such cases can lead to penalties under the Act.

question: In February 2023, who was appointed as the Governor of Bihar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar was appointed as the Governor of Bihar in February 2023.
 
• He succeeded Phagu Chauhan, who was the previous Governor of Bihar.
 
• Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar is a prominent political figure associated with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• Before his appointment as the Governor of Bihar, he served as the Governor of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• Arlekar has also held various significant positions in the state of Goa, including that of the Speaker of the Goa Legislative Assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governorship in India**

 
 
• The Governor of a state is appointed by the President of India for a term of five years.
 
• The Governor acts as the nominal head while the real power lies with the Chief Minister and the state cabinet.
 
• Governors have the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense against any law.
 
• They also play a crucial role during state emergencies and have the power to dissolve the state legislative assembly.
 
 
 
• **Role of a Governor**
 
 
• The Governor's primary responsibility is to ensure that the state government acts within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• They appoint the Chief Minister and other members of the Council of Ministers.
 
• Governors have the power to summon or prorogue the state legislature and dissolve the legislative assembly.
 
• They also oversee the administration of the oath of office to the Chief Minister and other ministers.
 
 
 
• **Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar's Background**
 
 
• Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar was born on 23 April 1954 in Goa.
 
• He is an experienced politician with a long-standing association with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• Arlekar has served as a member of the Goa Legislative Assembly and has held various ministerial positions in the state government.
 
• His tenure as Speaker of the Goa Legislative Assembly was marked by significant legislative developments.
 
 
 
• **Recent Governor Appointments**
 
 
• In 2023, several new governors were appointed across various states in India.
 
• Sushri Anusuiya Uikye was appointed as the Governor of Manipur.
 
• Ramesh Bais was appointed as the Governor of Maharashtra.
 
• Gulab Chand Kataria was appointed as the Governor of Assam.

question: In March 2023, who took charge as the 28th Controller General of Accounts (CGA) of Ministry of Finance of the Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**S.S Dubey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• S.S Dubey took charge as the 28th Controller General of Accounts (CGA) of the Ministry of Finance, Government of India in March 2023.
 
• The CGA is the principal advisor to the Government of India on accounting matters and responsible for establishing and maintaining a technically sound management accounting system.
 
• The CGA's office was set up in 1976 under the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance.
 
• The CGA oversees the payment and accounting system for the Government of India and prepares the annual accounts of the central government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Controller General of Accounts (CGA)**

 
 
• The CGA is a part of the Indian Civil Accounts Service (ICAS).
 
• The CGA is responsible for the compilation and consolidation of the government accounts and is responsible for the preparation of a critical report named the 'Union Government Finance Accounts'.
 
• The CGA is the head of the Indian Civil Accounts Organisation, which functions through the Principal Accounts Office of various ministries and departments.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Finance**
 
 
• The Ministry of Finance is a critical ministry within the Government of India, responsible for managing the economy, financial resources, and revenue collection.
 
• It oversees the financial institutions and markets, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• The ministry is divided into five departments: Economic Affairs, Expenditure, Revenue, Financial Services, and Investment and Public Asset Management.
 
 
 
• **Indian Civil Accounts Service (ICAS)**
 
 
• ICAS is a central civil service under the Department of Expenditure in the Ministry of Finance.
 
• The service was constituted in 1976 following the separation of accounts from audit.
 
• The primary responsibility of ICAS officers is to maintain the accounting and financial management system for the Government of India.

question: Who was appointed as the CEO (Chief Executive Officer) of NITI Aayog in February 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**BVR Subrahmanyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• BVR Subrahmanyam was appointed as the CEO of **NITI Aayog** in February 2023, succeeding Parameswaran Iyer.
 
• He is a 1987-batch IAS officer of the Chhattisgarh cadre and has held several key positions in the government.
 
• BVR Subrahmanyam previously served as the Commerce Secretary of India before taking up the position of NITI Aayog CEO.
 
• He is well-known for his role as the Chief Secretary of Jammu & Kashmir during the region's transition into a Union Territory in 2019.
 
• His appointment is expected to bring strategic leadership to NITI Aayog's initiatives, focusing on policy formulation and implementation for India's development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India)**

 
 
• Established in 2015, NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission to serve as the premier policy think tank of the Government of India.
 
• It focuses on fostering cooperative federalism through structured support and guidance to states.
 
• NITI Aayog is responsible for strategic planning, innovation, and monitoring the implementation of sustainable development goals (SDGs).
 
• The organization plays a pivotal role in formulating policies for economic growth, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Role of a CEO in NITI Aayog**
 
 
• The CEO ensures effective coordination among various departments and stakeholders in policy creation and implementation.
 
• Provides leadership in driving transformative projects and initiatives that align with India's development priorities.
 
• Serves as the link between the government, private sector, and civil society for collaborative efforts.
 
• Focuses on innovation and technology-driven solutions for achieving national and global objectives.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives by NITI Aayog**
 
 
• **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM):** Promotes entrepreneurship and innovation across India.
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** Monitors and supports India's progress on global SDG targets.
 
• **National Energy Policy:** Frames strategies for energy security and sustainability.
 
• **Digital India:** Promotes technology-driven governance and digital infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **BVR Subrahmanyam's Previous Contributions**
 
 
• Played a significant role in administrative reforms in Jammu & Kashmir during its transition to Union Territory status.
 
• As Commerce Secretary, he contributed to enhancing India's trade policy and export strategies.
 
• Known for his administrative acumen and ability to handle complex governance challenges.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Madhabi Puri Buch became the first woman to head SEBI in March 2022.

2. Tuhin Kanta Pandey has been appointed as the new SEBI Chief for three years from February 28, 2025.

3. Saudi Arabia has awarded PM Narendra Modi the Order of Mubarak Al-Kabeer.

Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Madhabi Puri Buch** became the first woman chairperson of SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) in March 2022.
 
• Tuhin Kanta Pandey has not been appointed as the SEBI Chief. His current role is Secretary of the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM).
 
• Saudi Arabia has not awarded PM Narendra Modi the "Order of Mubarak Al-Kabeer." This statement is factually incorrect.
 
• Therefore, only **statements 1 and 2** are correct.
 
• Option 4 aligns with the correct interpretation of the facts provided.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**

 
 
• SEBI is the regulator for the securities market in India, established in 1988 and given statutory powers in 1992.
 
• Its primary functions include protecting investor interests, regulating the securities market, and promoting its development.
 
• Madhabi Puri Buch is the first woman chairperson of SEBI, succeeding Ajay Tyagi in March 2022.
 
 
 
• **Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM)**
 
 
• DIPAM is responsible for managing the government's investments in public sector enterprises and facilitating disinvestment.
 
• Tuhin Kanta Pandey serves as Secretary of DIPAM, overseeing various strategic disinvestment initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Awards Conferred on PM Narendra Modi**
 
 
• PM Narendra Modi has received several international awards, including the "Order of Zayed" from the UAE and "Legion of Merit" from the United States.
 
• However, there is no record of him receiving the "Order of Mubarak Al-Kabeer" from Saudi Arabia.
 
 
 
• **Women's Role in Leadership**
 
 
• The appointment of Madhabi Puri Buch as SEBI chairperson is a milestone for women's representation in India's financial regulatory sector.
 
• It underscores the growing role of women in leadership positions across government and corporate sectors.

question: What is the rank of India in the World Happiness Index 2020?
solution:
The Correct Answer is **__144__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **As the United Nations released its World Happiness Report**, **India** was ranked at a dismal **144**. It surveyed a total of 156 nations. India scored 3.573 points, lower than Pakistan, which received 5.693 points, out of all the countries surveyed, ranking 66.

question: What is a major difficulty in the data collection process for the Happiness Index across different countries?

options.text: Lack of financial resources for advertising
Ensuring consistent and uniform survey methods globally

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ensuring consistent and uniform survey methods globally**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Consistency in survey methods is crucial for ensuring the accuracy and comparability of data collected across diverse countries.
 
• Different nations may have varying levels of expertise, infrastructure, and resources for conducting surveys, leading to potential discrepancies in methodology.
 
• Global surveys like the Happiness Index rely on standardized questionnaires and data collection processes, which can be challenging to implement uniformly.
 
• Cultural and social differences across countries may influence how questions are interpreted, further complicating the standardization of survey methods.
 
• Organizations such as the United Nations and World Happiness Report strive to create frameworks for uniform data collection but face logistical and financial hurdles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Happiness Report:**

 
 
• An annual publication by the United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network.
 
• Ranks countries based on factors such as GDP per capita, social support, life expectancy, freedom, generosity, and corruption perceptions.
 
• Uses survey data from the Gallup World Poll as its primary source of information.
 
 
 
• **Standardization Challenges:**
 
 
• Language differences require accurate translation of survey questions, which can impact meaning and understanding.
 
• Local customs and practices may influence respondents’ willingness to participate or provide truthful answers.
 
• Technological disparities, such as access to internet or mobile devices, can limit survey outreach in certain regions.
 
 
 
• **Sampling Techniques:**
 
 
• Random sampling is often used to ensure representation, but implementation can vary by country.
 
• Non-representative samples can lead to biased or skewed results, impacting global comparisons.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Dimensions in Surveys:**
 
 
• Hofstede's cultural dimensions theory highlights differences in societal values that may impact survey responses.
 
• These include power distance, individualism vs. collectivism, and uncertainty avoidance, among others.

__
 
• The World Happiness Report identifies **6 key variables** to explain variations in happiness levels across countries.
 
• The six factors include: **GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption.**
 
• These variables are derived from the **Gallup World Poll** data, which surveys residents of various countries on subjective well-being and social factors.
 
• The report evaluates happiness levels as a combination of these objective and subjective indicators, allowing cross-country comparisons.
 
• The annual World Happiness Report is published by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (UN SDSN).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita:** A measure of economic output per person, used to evaluate the wealth and standard of living in a country.
 
• **Social Support:** Reflects the availability of family, friends, or social systems to provide support during difficult times.
 
• **Healthy Life Expectancy:** Indicates the average number of years a person can expect to live in good health.
 
• **Freedom to Make Life Choices:** Measures individuals’ perceptions of their ability to make personal and professional decisions independently.
 
• **Generosity and Perceptions of Corruption:** Generosity assesses acts of giving, while corruption perceptions evaluate trust in public institutions and fairness of governance.
 
• The World Happiness Report was first published in **2012** and has become a key resource for policymakers worldwide, emphasizing the importance of well-being as an indicator of progress.

question: Which of the following statement is incorrect regarding global indices as of July 2025?

options.text: The World Happiness Report 2024 highlights social support, life expectancy, and GDP per capita as key happiness factors.
AQI consistently above 200 signals general health risks and requires urgent policy action.
Despite being discontinued, the Ease of Doing Business report remains influential for investors assessing startup procedures.
A rise in GNI per capita alone can significantly improve HDI, even with falling life expectancy and education.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) is calculated using three primary indicators: life expectancy, education (mean years and expected years), and GNI per capita (Gross National Income).
 
• A rise in GNI per capita alone cannot significantly improve the HDI score if other parameters like life expectancy and education decline.
 
• The HDI approach emphasizes balanced improvement across all dimensions for holistic human development assessment.
 
• Global HDI rankings and trends reflect a country's socio-economic and public health development over time.
 
• The claim that "a rise in GNI per capita alone can significantly improve HDI, even with falling life expectancy and education" is incorrect, as HDI depends on simultaneous performance across all indicators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• Developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to measure a country's overall achievement in its social and economic dimensions.
 
• HDI is a composite index based on three dimensions: health (life expectancy), education, and standard of living (GNI per capita).
 
• It is widely used to compare development levels among nations and regions.
 
 
 
• **Gross National Income (GNI):**
 
 
• GNI represents the total income earned by a country's residents and businesses, including income from abroad.
 
• It is an important economic indicator used in HDI calculation to reflect the standard of living.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Life expectancy serves as a proxy for the health dimension in HDI.
 
• It reflects the average number of years a person is expected to live, based on current mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **Education Indicators in HDI:**
 
 
• Mean years of schooling (average years of education received by people aged 25 and older).
 
• Expected years of schooling (number of years a child of school-entry age is expected to spend in school).
 
 
 
• **Balanced Development:**
 
 
• Improvement in one dimension (e.g., GNI) cannot compensate for declines in others (e.g., education or health).
 
• Holistic growth across all dimensions is crucial for sustainable human development.

question: What kind of approach does the Happiness Index encourage in governance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Citizen-centric**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Happiness Index promotes governance that prioritizes the **well-being, satisfaction, and happiness of citizens** over purely economic or resource-driven goals.
 
• This approach ensures that policies and initiatives are designed to address the **physical, mental, and emotional needs of the population**.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of **inclusive growth, social equity, and environmental sustainability** in decision-making.
 
• Governments adopting a citizen-centric approach focus on **education, healthcare, income equality, and environmental quality** as key determinants of happiness.
 
• The Happiness Index is aligned with the idea that governance should aim to **enhance the overall quality of life** rather than prioritizing mere economic indicators like GDP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Happiness Index**

 
 
• The Happiness Index, also known as the World Happiness Report, is an annual publication by the United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network.
 
• It ranks countries based on factors like GDP per capita, social support, life expectancy, freedom, generosity, and corruption perception.
 
• The report uses data from surveys conducted by organizations like Gallup and relies on the Cantril Ladder method to measure happiness.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Citizen-Centric Governance**
 
 
• Bhutan's Gross National Happiness (GNH) framework prioritizes cultural preservation, environmental conservation, and citizen well-being.
 
• Scandinavian countries, such as Finland and Denmark, consistently rank high on the Happiness Index due to their focus on social welfare, healthcare, and education.
 
 
 
• **Legalistic vs. Citizen-Centric Approach**
 
 
• A legalistic approach emphasizes adherence to laws and regulations, often prioritizing institutional frameworks over individual needs.
 
• A citizen-centric approach focuses on creating policies and systems that directly address the needs and aspirations of citizens.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Citizen-Centric Governance**
 
 
• Enhances trust between the government and its citizens.
 
• Improves overall satisfaction and productivity within the population.
 
• Encourages participatory governance and inclusive decision-making.

question: Select the FALSE statement with reference to the food chain.

options.text: Inter-relation between different food chains is known as a food web.
All the chains formed by nutritional relations is used to understand energy flow.
Only producers of food chain form a trophic level.
Every component of the food chain forms a trophic level.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only producers of the food chain form a trophic level.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are unique interactions and relationships which are involved in the transportation of energy.
 
• The energy, once produced and captured, is distributed throughout the various living organisms.
 
• **This transfer of energy is termed the food web.**
 
• In specialized terms, Food Chain is the sequence through which the transfer of energy takes place within a particular ecosystem.
 
• **Energy transfer is pivotal for the survival and food of living organisms.**
 
• Trophic position refers to the successional stages in a food chain, starting with directors at the bottom, followed by primary, secondary, and tertiary consumers.
 
• **Every position in a food chain is known as a trophic position**. ***Hence, the Option 3 is Incorrect.​***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76869f6f1f571bea548e433fe63b566a3e342b4b9e645e1165b8cdd2f3d1edd4.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dd88533bd479397c8ff098b2f7d94cd87266b920004f4f2f9d17ef4fb30dd9b.png] 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• Both food chains and food webs, share three types of organisms in a food chain:** Producers, Consumers, and decomposers**.

 
 
• **Producers:** The producers in a food chain include all autotrophs such as phytoplankton.

 
 
• This is the first stage in a food chain.
 
• The producers make up the first level of a food chain.
 
 
 
• **Consumers:** Consumers are all organisms that are dependent on plants or other organisms for food.
 
 
• This is the largest part of a food web, as it contains almost all living organisms.
 
• It includes herbivores which are animals that eat plants, carnivores which are animals that eat other animals, parasites that live on other organisms by harming them, and lastly scavengers, which are animals that eat dead animals’ carcasses.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:** Decomposers are organisms that get energy from dead or waste organic material.
 
 
• This is the last stage in a food chain.
 
• Decomposers are an integral part of a food chain, as they convert organic waste materials into inorganic materials, which enriches the soil or land with nutrients.

__
 
• **DFC** stands for **Detritus Food Chain**.
 
• It is a process that recycles nutrients back into the ecosystem.

• This food chain is essential for the **decomposition of organic matter and nutrient cycling.**
 
• It contrasts with the grazing food chain, which starts from living plants.

 Ecosystem Component
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Producers**
 Organisms that produce their own food (e.g., plants).
 
 

 **Consumers**
 Organisms that consume other organisms for energy.
 
 

 **Decomposers**
 Organisms that break down dead organic matter, returning nutrients to the soil.
 
 

 **Detritivores**
 Specialized decomposers that consume detritus (dead particulate organic material).
 
 

 **Food Web**
 A complex network of interconnected food chains within an ecosystem.
