question: __________are circular and biconcave for easy passage through blood capillaries and to transport oxygen.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Red blood cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Red blood cells (RBCs) are also known as erythrocytes.
 
• They are circular and biconcave in shape, which increases their surface area for gas exchange.
 
• The primary function of RBCs is to transport oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues and return carbon dioxide from the tissues to the lungs.
 
• RBCs contain hemoglobin, a protein that binds oxygen and gives blood its red color.
 
• They are produced in the bone marrow and have an average lifespan of about 120 days in the human body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hemoglobin:**

 
 
• A protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
 
• Each hemoglobin molecule can bind up to four oxygen molecules.
 
• Hemoglobin also helps in transporting carbon dioxide back to the lungs for exhalation.
 
 
 
• **Erythropoiesis:**
 
 
• The process of red blood cell production.
 
• Occurs in the bone marrow.
 
• Stimulated by the hormone erythropoietin, which is produced by the kidneys in response to low oxygen levels.
 
 
 
• **Anemia:**
 
 
• A condition in which there is a deficiency of red blood cells or hemoglobin in the blood.
 
• Leads to symptoms like fatigue, weakness, and shortness of breath.
 
• Common causes include iron deficiency, chronic diseases, and genetic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Blood Groups:**
 
 
• Red blood cells have surface antigens that determine blood group (e.g., A, B, AB, O).
 
• Blood groups are important for blood transfusions to prevent immune reactions.
 
• The Rh factor, another antigen, classifies blood as positive or negative.

question: When focusing on a tree while on an anti-clockwise merry-go-round, from which side does it appear and exit?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Left**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When you are on an anti-clockwise merry-go-round, your position is constantly changing relative to a stationary object such as a tree.
 
• As the merry-go-round rotates anti-clockwise, the tree will first appear on your right side as you move toward it.
 
• Due to the continuous rotation, the tree will seem to move from your right side to your left side as you pass it.
 
• This apparent motion is a result of the relative positioning between the observer (you) and the stationary object (tree) during the anti-clockwise movement.
 
• The correct interpretation of this phenomenon aligns with the principles of relative motion in physics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relative Motion:** The concept of relative motion describes how the position of an object changes with respect to an observer. In this case, the tree’s apparent motion is relative to the observer’s position on the rotating merry-go-round.
 
• **Anti-clockwise Rotation:** A rotation is termed anti-clockwise when it proceeds in the opposite direction to the movement of clock hands. This impacts the observer’s perception of stationary objects.
 
• **Frame of Reference:** The observer on the merry-go-round is in a non-inertial frame of reference. Stationary objects like the tree appear to move due to the observer’s rotational motion.
 
• **Perception of Motion:** The apparent movement of the tree from right to left is a result of the observer’s changing position and orientation relative to the tree.
 
• **Practical Example:** Similar observations can be made in other rotational systems, such as carousels or spinning platforms, where objects appear to move in a direction opposite to the rotation.

question: On the basis of which phenomenon does a Jet engine work?
solution:
__
 
• The Jet engine works on the phenomenon of **Conservation of Linear Momentum**__.
 
• It produces a large volume of gases through the combustion of fuel, which is allowed to escape in backward direction through a jet.
 
• The backward rushing gas gains large momentum because of high velocity.
 
• It thus imparts an equal and opposite momentum to the jet engine.
 
• The jet engine, thus, moves forward with high speed.
 
• Conservation of Linear Momentum states that a body in motion retains its total momentum (product of mass and vector velocity) unless an external force is applied to it.

A body performing circular motion is acted upon by a force that is always directed towards the centre of the circle. This force is called **__centripetal force__**.

__Explanation:__

Centripetal Force: 

It is a force required to move a body uniformly in a circular motion. This force acts along the radius and towards the centre of the circle.

• When a body moves in a circle, its direction of motion at any instant is along the tangent of a circle.
 
• But according to Newton’s first law of motion, A body cannot change its direction of itself an external force is required for this purpose. This external force is the centripetal force

question: According to the Law of Periods, the square of a planet's time period is proportional to:

options.text: The square of its distance from the sun
The cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit
The square root of its orbital radius
The product of its mass and orbital speed

solution:
The correct answer is __**The cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Law of Periods, also known as Kepler's Third Law, states that the square of the orbital period of a planet is directly proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as: **T² ∝ a³**, where T is the orbital period and a is the semi-major axis.
 
• This law applies to planets, moons, and other celestial bodies orbiting a central body, such as the Sun or a star.
 
• The semi-major axis is the longest radius of an elliptical orbit, representing the average distance of the planet from the central body.
 
• Kepler's Third Law is derived from Newton's law of gravitation and provides a foundation for understanding orbital mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion:**

 
 
• 1st Law (Law of Ellipses): Planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus.
 
• 2nd Law (Law of Equal Areas): A line joining a planet and the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time.
 
• 3rd Law (Law of Periods): The square of the orbital period of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.
 
 
 
• **Semi-Major Axis:**
 
 
• The semi-major axis is the average distance between the center of an orbiting body and the central body it orbits.
 
• For circular orbits, the semi-major axis is equivalent to the radius of the circle.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation:**
 
 
• Newton extended Kepler's laws by deriving them using his law of gravitation: F = G * (m1 * m2) / r², where G is the gravitational constant.
 
• It explains how gravitational forces govern the motion of celestial objects.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Kepler's Third Law:**
 
 
• It is used in calculating orbital periods of planets, satellites, and space missions.
 
• It helps in understanding the dynamics of exoplanets and binary star systems.

question: Which of the following quantities remains conserved when an object moves under the gravitational pull of another object?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Angular momentum and mechanical energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Angular momentum** remains conserved for an object moving under the gravitational pull of another object due to the absence of external torque in such a system.
 
• **Mechanical energy** (the sum of kinetic and potential energy) is conserved in a gravitational system when non-conservative forces like friction are absent.
 
• Conservation laws stem from symmetries in nature, as per **Noether's theorem**, with conservation of angular momentum linked to rotational symmetry.
 
• Gravitational force acts as a central force, ensuring no torque is exerted, which leads to the conservation of angular momentum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Angular Momentum:** It is the rotational equivalent of linear momentum and is given by the product of moment of inertia and angular velocity. Its conservation is crucial in orbital mechanics.
 
• **Mechanical Energy:** The total energy of a system in the form of kinetic and potential energy. In gravitational interactions, the conversion between these forms keeps the total mechanical energy constant.
 
• **Central Forces:** Forces that act along the line joining the centers of two interacting bodies. Gravitational force is an example of a central force, ensuring no external torque.
 
• **Noether's Theorem:** A fundamental principle in physics stating that every conservation law corresponds to a symmetry in the physical system.
 
• **Applications:** The conservation of angular momentum is observed in celestial phenomena like planetary orbits, spinning ice skaters pulling in their arms, and the behavior of rotating neutron stars.

question: Butter Paper is an example of ________ object.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**translucent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Butter Paper** is an example of a **translucent object**.
 
• A **translucent object** allows some amount of light to pass through it, but not entirely. This property makes objects behind it appear **blurry** or unclear.
 
• Butter paper is widely used in **baking and cooking** to prevent food from sticking, as well as in **arts and crafts** for tracing purposes.
 
• Examples of other **translucent materials** include **frosted glass, wax paper, and thin plastic sheets.**
 
• The property of being translucent lies between **opaque** (which does not allow light to pass) and **transparent** (which allows light to pass completely).
 
• In scientific terms, **translucency** is a material characteristic where light is scattered as it passes through the object, preventing the formation of a clear image on the other side.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Opaque**__

 __
 
• **Opaque objects** do not allow light to pass through. As a result, no image is visible through them.
 
• Examples of opaque materials include **wood, metal, and stone.**
 
 
 
• **Luminous**__
 __
 
• **Luminous objects** are those that emit their own light.
 
• Examples include the **sun, stars, and electric bulbs.**
 
 
 
• **Transparent**__
 
 
• **Transparent objects** allow light to pass through completely, making objects on the other side clearly visible.
 
• Examples include **clear glass, clean water, and thin air.**

question: How is the image formed by a plane mirror?
solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A plane mirror forms an image that is **virtual**, meaning the image cannot be projected onto a screen.
 
• The image formed is **erect**, maintaining the same orientation as the object.
 
• Images formed by plane mirrors are also **laterally inverted**, meaning the left and right sides are swapped.
 
• The distance of the image from the mirror is equal to the distance of the object from the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Virtual Image**

 
 
• A virtual image is formed when rays of light appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror.
 
• It cannot be captured on a screen as it does not involve actual light convergence.
 
 
 
• **Lateral Inversion**
 
 
• Lateral inversion refers to the reversal of the left and right sides in the image formed by a mirror.
 
• This is why text appears reversed when viewed in a mirror.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Plane Mirrors**
 
 
• Plane mirrors have a flat reflective surface.
 
• They produce images with the same size as the object.
 
• The image is always at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front of it.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Plane Mirrors**
 
 
• Used in everyday items such as bathroom mirrors and dressing mirrors.
 
• Important in optical instruments like periscopes and kaleidoscopes.
 
• Used in rear-view mirrors in vehicles to provide a virtual image of the road behind.

question: Which of the following is not a magnetic material?
solution:
__CONCEPT__:

Diamagnetic Substance:

__
 
• Diamagnetic substances are those which develop feeble magnetization in the opposite direction of the magnetizing field.
 
• Such substances are feebly repelled by magnets and tend to move from stronger to weaker parts of a magnetic field.
 
• Magnetic susceptibility is small and negative i.e. -1 ≤ χ ≤ 0.
 
• Examples: Bismuth, copper, lead, zinc, etc.

Paramagnetic substances:

 
• Paramagnetic substances are those which develop feeble magnetization in the direction of the magnetizing field.
 
• Such substances are feebly attracted by magnets and tend to move from weaker to stronger parts of a magnetic field. Therefore option 2 is incorrect.
 
• Magnetic susceptibility is small and positive i.e. 0

Ferromagnetic substances:

 
• Ferromagnetic substances are those which develop strong magnetization in the direction of the magnetizing field.
 
• They are strongly attracted by a magnet and tend to move from weaker to the stronger part of a magnetic field.
 
• Magnetic susceptibility is very large and positive i.e. χ > 1000.
 
• Example: Iron, cobalt, nickel, gadolinium, and alloys like alnico.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• From the above options, only **wood does not have unpaired electron spins** that can line up with a magnet, and so it is a **non-magnetic material**.

question: A conductor rod moving with a velocity v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B. If the length of the rod perpendicular to both v and B is L, the induced EMF across its ends is given by?
solution:
The correct answer is __**BLv**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The induced EMF across the ends of a moving conductor rod is given by the formula **EMF = B × L × v**, where B is the magnetic field, L is the length of the rod perpendicular to the field, and v is the velocity of the rod.
 
• This phenomenon is based on the principle of **electromagnetic induction**, discovered by Michael Faraday.
 
• The motion of the rod through the magnetic field causes the charges in the conductor to experience a force (Lorentz force), resulting in the separation of charges and the generation of EMF.
 
• The direction of the induced EMF can be determined using **Fleming's Right-Hand Rule**, which relates the direction of the magnetic field, motion, and the induced current.
 
• This formula is specific to cases where the motion of the rod is perpendicular to both the magnetic field and its length.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic Induction:**

 
 
• This is the process of generating an EMF or current in a conductor due to its interaction with a changing magnetic field.
 
• The principle was discovered by Michael Faraday in 1831.
 
• Faraday's Law states that the induced EMF is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux.
 
 
 
• **Lorentz Force:**
 
 
• It is the force experienced by a charged particle moving in a magnetic and electric field.
 
• The force is given by **F = q(E + v × B)**, where q is the charge, E is the electric field, v is the velocity, and B is the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Fleming's Right-Hand Rule:**
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of induced current or EMF.
 
• It states: Stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of your right hand perpendicular to each other. The thumb points in the direction of motion, the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger gives the direction of induced current.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Induced EMF:**
 
 
• Used in the working of electric generators and dynamos.
 
• Essential in electromagnetic braking systems.
 
• Forms the basis of inductive charging for devices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Induced EMF is given by Faraday’s law, which depends on the rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil.
 
• **Magnetic flux is maximum when the coil’s plane is perpendicular to the field lines (flux change is zero here).**
 
• **EMF is maximum when the flux changes most rapidly, which occurs when the coil’s plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines**__ (flux = 0 but rate of change is maximum).
 
• At this orientation, every small rotation produces the greatest possible change in flux, resulting in maximum induced EMF.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is – When the coil's plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option (1): At 45°, some EMF is induced, but not maximum since the flux change rate is not the greatest.
 
• Option (2): When flux is maximum, EMF is zero because there is no change in flux at that instant.
 
• Option (3): When the coil’s plane is perpendicular, flux is maximum but EMF = 0 (same as above).
 
• Option (4): Correct, because maximum EMF is induced when flux = 0 and change of flux is maximum.

question: A conductor of length L and resistance R is cut into two equal halves. These two halves are then connected in parallel. Find the equivalent resistance of this parallel combination?
solution:
The correct answer is __**R/4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a conductor of length L and resistance R is cut into two equal halves, the resistance of each half becomes **R/2**.
 
• If these two halves are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination is given by the formula for parallel resistors: **1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2**.
 
• Substituting R1 = R/2 and R2 = R/2, the calculation becomes **1/Req = 2/(R/2) = 4/R**.
 
• Therefore, the equivalent resistance of the combination is **Req = R/4**.
 
• This result arises due to the inverse relationship of resistance in parallel circuits, which reduces the overall resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistance in Parallel Combination:**

 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the reciprocal of the total resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of individual resistances: **1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...**.
 
• Parallel connections lead to a decrease in the overall resistance due to the multiple paths for current flow.
 
 
 
• **Resistance and Length Relationship:**
 
 
• The resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to its length (R ∝ L).
 
• When the conductor is divided into two equal parts, the resistance of each part becomes half of the original.
 
 
 
• **Ohm’s Law:**
 
 
• Ohm’s Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points and inversely proportional to the resistance.
 
• The formula is **V = IR**, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
 
 
• **Applications:** Understanding parallel and series resistance is crucial in designing electrical circuits for household appliances, power distribution, and electronic systems.
 
• **Practical Observation:** In real-world scenarios, parallel circuits are preferred in many cases as they ensure that a failure in one path does not disrupt the entire circuit.

question: According to Lenz's Law, what determines the direction of an induced current in a conductor?

options.text: It continuously reduces the applied magnetic flux,
It always enhances the existing magnetic field.
It flows to oppose the variation in magnetic flux causing it.
It is proportional to the strength of the magnetic field.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It flows to oppose the variation in magnetic flux causing it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lenz's Law states that the direction of the induced current in a conductor is such that it **opposes the change in magnetic flux** that caused it.
 
• The law is based on the **principle of conservation of energy**, ensuring that the induced current doesn't create energy out of nothing.
 
• This opposition is achieved by the induced current generating a magnetic field that counters the change in the external magnetic flux.
 
• Lenz's Law can be mathematically expressed as part of Faraday's Law: **E = -dΦ/dt**, where the negative sign indicates opposition to the change.
 
• It plays a critical role in understanding electromagnetic induction and is widely applied in devices like electric generators, transformers, and inductors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction:**

 
 
• It states that a change in magnetic flux through a circuit induces an electromotive force (EMF) in the circuit.
 
• The induced EMF is proportional to the rate of change of the magnetic flux.
 
• Faraday's Law forms the foundation for Lenz's Law.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• Lenz's Law ensures that the induced current's opposition prevents the creation of perpetual motion, adhering to energy conservation.
 
• The opposing magnetic field consumes energy equivalent to the work done to change the magnetic flux.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Lenz's Law:**
 
 
• Lenz's Law is crucial in designing **electric generators**, where mechanical energy is converted into electrical energy.
 
• It is also applied in **transformers** to regulate voltage levels and prevent energy losses.
 
• Induction cooktops utilize Lenz's Law to generate heat efficiently.
 
 
 
• **Key Terminology:**
 
 
• **Magnetic Flux (Φ):** The measure of the total magnetic field passing through a surface.
 
• **Electromotive Force (EMF):** The voltage generated by changing magnetic flux.
 
• **Induced Current:** The current generated due to electromagnetic induction.

question: Which of the following phenomena occurs when a wave passes through a narrow slit?

__
 
• **Diffraction** is the bending of waves around obstacles or the spreading of waves as they pass through narrow slits or openings.
 
• The phenomenon is more pronounced when the size of the slit or obstacle is comparable to the wavelength of the wave.
 
• Diffraction occurs for all types of waves, including light waves, sound waves, and water waves.
 
• This bending allows waves to propagate into the geometrical shadow region, creating interference patterns.
 
• In optics, diffraction effects are essential in understanding the behavior of light in devices such as diffraction gratings and optical instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Interference Patterns:** Diffraction often produces constructive and destructive interference patterns, leading to regions of bright and dark fringes.
 
• **Huygens' Principle:** A foundational principle in wave optics stating that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets, which combine to form the observed wave.
 
• **Applications of Diffraction:** Used in X-ray crystallography to determine atomic structures, and in spectrometers and diffraction gratings for analyzing light spectra.
 
• **Double-Slit Experiment:** A classic demonstration of diffraction and interference, highlighting the wave nature of light and other particles.

• The speed of sound depends on the medium's density and elasticity.
 
 
 
• **Elastic Modulus and Density:**

• Density affects sound speed inversely: lower density generally leads to slower sound speed in gases compared to solids.
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Forces:**
 
 
• Stronger intermolecular forces in solids ensure quicker energy transfer between particles.
 
• In gases, weaker forces and larger intermolecular distances result in slower sound transmission.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Sound in Different Media:**

• Water: ~1,480 m/s
 
• Air: ~343 m/s
 
• These values vary with temperature and material composition.

question: Latent heat of fusion of ice is ________.
solution:

SUBLIMATION

 
 
 
Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase without undergoing the intermediate liquid phase. Eg: Camphor, Dry Ice

 
 
 

 DESUBLIMATION
 Desublimation or deposition where substances convert directly from the gaseous state to a solid without first undergoing a liquid state. Eg: Refrigerant R-135 solidifies directly from a gas.
 
 

 
 
LIQUEFACTION

 
 
 
Liquefaction of gases is the process by which substances in their gaseous state are converted to the liquid state

 
 
 

 
 
LATENT HEAT OF FUSION

 
 
 
Amount of heat energy that is required to change 1 kg of a solid into liquid at atmospheric pressure at its melting point

 
 
 

 
 
LATENT HEAT OF VAPORIZATION

 
 
 
The heat absorbed per unit mass of a given material at its boiling point that completely converts the material to a gas at the same temperature

subject: GK
question: The ______ is the most common unit for measuring ozone concentration.
solution:
The correct answer is **__dobson unit.__**

__
 
• **The Dobson Unit** is a way to describe how much ozone there would be in the column if it were all squeezed into a single layer.
 
• The** average amount of ozone** in the atmosphere is roughly **300 Dobson Units**, equivalent to a layer 3 millimetres (0.12 inches) thick.
 
• One Dobson Unit is the equivalent of **2.69 × 10¹⁶ molecules** of ozone per square centimetre.
 
• Alternatively, 1 Dobson unit corresponds to a layer of ozone **10 μm thick**, if the ozone were held at standard temperature and pressure (273 K, 1 atm pressure).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concentration of a certain trace gas, for example, ozone and SO₂, in a column of air in the earth's atmosphere is often given in Dobson Unit.
 
• The** "Dobson Unit"** is named after professor **G.M.B. Dobson (1889 - 1976)**, who has from the 1920s onwards done research on the ozone layer. 
 
• The "Dobson Unit" indicates how much of a given trace gas there is in the air above a certain point on earth.
 
• A proper unit in the International System of units would thus be **"kilogram per square meter".**

question: Which among the following has the same dimension as that of energy?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Torque.__**

__
 
• Torque is the **measure** of the force that can **cause** an **object** to **rotate** about an **axis.**
 
• **Torque **Formula

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10f1e4d63f00fa058c8f6883d178207dd3b20d34e5de2b53def6e06ba8622d17.png] 

 
• In **physics** and **mechanics**, torque is the** rotational equivalent **of linear force. It is also referred to as the **moment**, **moment of force**, **rotational force **or** turning effect**, depending on the field of study.
 
• Torque is commonly denoted with a capital **“T,”** but the correct symbol is the Greek letter tau,** “τ.”** When torque is referred to as a moment of force, the symbol** “M”** is used.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Moment of inertia**
 
 
**The moment of inertia** is defined as the quantity expressed by the body resisting angular acceleration which is the sum of the product of the mass of every particle with its square of a distance from the axis of rotation.

 
**Formula**

 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d5d6c1cd3994cbaafdb04b4666241be7dca5dfb36f61361f61faa522a5c99d5d.png] 

 
 
 

 **Linear momentum**
 
 
**Linear momentum** is defined as the product of a system's mass multiplied by its velocity. In symbols, **linear momentum** is expressed as p = mv. Momentum is directly proportional to the object's mass and also its velocity.

 
**Formula**

 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f0ab47607459dbc367a44e36e8ea7a6c55ce9926f8d7ab9de362fb9ced5f3e5.png] 

 
 
 

 **Angular momentum**
 
 
In physics, **angular momentum** is the rotational equivalent of linear **momentum**. It is an important quantity in physics because it is a conserved quantity the total **angular momentum** of a closed system remains constant.

 
**Formula**

• **Applications of Density**
 
 
• Density is used in buoyancy calculations for ships and submarines.
 
• It helps in identifying substances and determining their purity.
 
 
 
• **Related Concepts**
 
 
• Specific Gravity: The ratio of the density of a substance to the density of water.
 
• Buoyancy: The ability of an object to float in a fluid due to density differences.
 
 
 
• **Important Figures**
 
 
• Archimedes: Discovered the principle of buoyancy which relates to density.

• **They include fruits, vegetables, flowers, herbs, and ornamental plants. **
 
• **Examples of horticultural crops **
 
 
• Fruits: Apples, bananas, grapes, guava, litchi, and tomatoes
 
• Vegetables: A variety of vegetables
 
• Flowers: A variety of flowers, including those used in landscaping
 
• Ornamental plants: Plants used in landscaping, such as ornamental trees and shrubs

question: How much maximum amount of loan can be taken from Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (2015)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) was launched by the Government of India in April 2015.
 
• The primary objective of PMMY is to provide financial support to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
• The maximum loan amount that can be availed under PMMY is up to Rs. 10 lakh.
 
• Loans under PMMY are categorized into three products: Shishu (up to Rs. 50,000), Kishore (Rs. 50,001 to Rs. 5 lakh), and Tarun (Rs. 5,01,000 to Rs. 10 lakh).
 
• PMMY aims to promote entrepreneurship among the youth and encourage small businesses to grow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**

 
 
• Any Indian citizen with a business plan for a non-farm income-generating activity can avail of a loan under PMMY.
 
• The applicant must be at least 18 years old.
 
• Individuals, proprietary concerns, partnership firms, and other legal entities are eligible for the loan.
 
 
 
• **Types of Loans:**
 
 
• **Shishu:** Covering loans up to Rs. 50,000, aimed at startups and early-stage businesses.
 
• **Kishore:** Covering loans ranging from Rs. 50,001 to Rs. 5 lakh, for businesses in the growth phase.
 
• **Tarun:** Covering loans from Rs. 5,01,000 to Rs. 10 lakh, for established businesses looking to scale up.
 
 
 
• **Interest Rates:**
 
 
• Interest rates under PMMY are decided by the lending institution, based on the RBI guidelines.
 
• Generally, these loans are offered at competitive rates to make them affordable for small entrepreneurs.
 
 
 
• **Application Process:**
 
 
• Interested applicants can approach any of the lending institutions, including public sector banks, private sector banks, regional rural banks, and microfinance institutions.
 
• The application process involves submitting a detailed business plan and relevant documents as required by the lending institution.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• Since its inception, PMMY has significantly contributed to the financial inclusion of small and micro-enterprises in India.
 
• It has helped in the creation of millions of jobs and has empowered women entrepreneurs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Donate-a-Pension is an initiative under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) scheme, announced by the Union Labour and Employment Minister in March 2022.
 
• The initiative allows citizens to contribute to the pension funds of unorganized workers, thereby supporting their old-age protection.
 
• This scheme is targeted at workers in the unorganized sector who are not covered under any formal pension scheme.
 
• Individuals can donate the premium amount on behalf of their domestic workers, drivers, or any other unorganized workers who are eligible for the PM-SYM scheme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) Scheme**

 
 
• Launched on 5 March 2019 by PM Narendra Modi, the scheme aims to provide old age protection and social security to unorganized workers.
 
• It targets individuals aged between 18-40 years with a monthly income of ₹15,000 or less.
 
• Beneficiaries receive a monthly pension of ₹3,000 after attaining the age of 60.
 
• Contributions vary depending on the age of the beneficiary, starting from ₹55 to ₹200 per month.
 
• Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) of India is the pension fund manager for the scheme.
 
 
 
• **Unorganized Sector in India**
 
 
• The unorganized sector comprises workers who are not covered by formal employment contracts and social security benefits.
 
• This includes domestic workers, street vendors, construction workers, and agricultural laborers.
 
• It represents a significant portion of India's workforce, with an estimated 42 crore workers.
 
• Workers in this sector often face economic vulnerabilities and lack access to pension and health benefits.
 
 
 
• **Pension Schemes in India**
 
 
• India has several pension schemes aimed at providing financial security to different segments of the population.
 
• National Pension System (NPS) is a government-sponsored pension scheme for employees in the public, private, and unorganized sectors.
 
• Atal Pension Yojana (APY) targets unorganized sector workers, offering a guaranteed pension based on their contributions.
 
• Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) is a retirement benefits scheme for employees in the organized sector.

• PMMY aims to provide loans up to Rs. 10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
• The loans under PMMY are classified into three categories: Shishu (up to Rs. 50,000), Kishore (Rs. 50,001 to Rs. 5 lakh), and Tarun (Rs. 5,00,001 to Rs. 10 lakh).

• Offers refinance to banks and microfinance institutions (MFIs) that provide loans to micro units.

• Includes initiatives like Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), which provides universal access to banking facilities.

• **Stand-Up India** scheme was launched on **5 April 2016** by the Government of India.
 
• The scheme aims to **promote entrepreneurship among Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and women entrepreneurs**.
 
• Under the scheme, loans ranging from **₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore** are provided to eligible entrepreneurs for setting up greenfield enterprises.

• Under Stand-Up India, the focus is on creating such enterprises by SC, ST, and women entrepreneurs.

• The applicant must be an SC/ST or a woman entrepreneur.
 
• The age of the applicant should be between 18-65 years.
 
• The enterprise must be a greenfield project in manufacturing, services, or trading sectors.

• Margin money requirement is limited to 25% of the project cost.

question: The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) focuses on:

options.text: Developing industrial clusters in backward regions

solution:
The correct answer is __**Enhancing development in underdeveloped districts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) was launched by the Government of India in **January 2018** under the auspices of NITI Aayog.
 
• It aims to rapidly transform **117 districts** identified as the most underdeveloped in India across various socio-economic indicators.
 
• The programme focuses on sectors such as **health and nutrition, education, agriculture and water resources, financial inclusion, and skill development**.
 
• ADP emphasizes **data-driven governance** through real-time monitoring and ranking of districts based on their progress in key indicators.
 
• Collaboration among central ministries, state governments, and district administrations ensures targeted interventions for accelerated development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog's Role:** NITI Aayog spearheads the Aspirational Districts Programme by providing technical support and monitoring the progress of districts using a **dashboard system**.
 
• **Delta Ranking:** Districts are ranked based on their improvement in key indicators. The ranking system encourages competition and accountability among districts.
 
• **Focus Areas:** The programme prioritizes development in areas such as **maternal and child health, education outcomes, rural infrastructure, and skill development**.
 
• **Convergence Model:** ADP integrates efforts from various schemes like **Poshan Abhiyaan, PM Awas Yojana, and Skill India Mission** to ensure holistic development.
 
• **UNDP Collaboration:** The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) supports the programme by identifying best practices and providing analytical assistance.

question: Which major reform was introduced in the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020?

options.text: Replacement of the 10+2 system with a 5 + 3 + 3 + 4 structure
Mandatory board exams for all grades

solution:
The correct answer is __**Replacement of the 10+2 system with a 5 + 3 + 3 + 4 structure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 introduced a new structural framework for school education, replacing the 10+2 system with the **5+3+3+4 structure**.
 
• The **5+3+3+4 structure** corresponds to the foundational stage (ages 3–8), preparatory stage (ages 8–11), middle stage (ages 11–14), and secondary stage (ages 14–18).
 
• This reform emphasizes the importance of **early childhood care and education (ECCE)**, integrating preschool education into the formal schooling system.
 
• The new structure aims to align the Indian education system with global standards and emphasizes **experiential, skill-based, and holistic learning**.
 
• It also focuses on reducing the rigid separations between academic streams, vocational education, and extracurricular activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foundational Stage**: Covers ages 3–8, including three years of preschool and two years of primary education. It focuses on play-based and activity-based learning.
 
• **Preparatory Stage**: Covers ages 8–11 (grades 3–5) and emphasizes discovery-based and interactive classroom learning.
 
• **Middle Stage**: Covers ages 11–14 (grades 6–8) and introduces subject-specific learning, including vocational education.
 
• **Secondary Stage**: Covers ages 14–18 (grades 9–12) and allows students to choose subjects based on their interests, with a multidisciplinary approach.
 
• **Other Reforms under NEP 2020**: Focus on mother tongue/local language as the medium of instruction, introduction of coding and computational thinking from an early stage, and flexibility for students to select subjects across streams.

• PM-MITRA stands for **Pradhan Mantri Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel** scheme.
 
• The scheme aims to **boost India’s textile sector** by establishing seven integrated textile parks across the country.
 
• These parks will serve as hubs for **textile manufacturing, export promotion, and job creation**.
 
• The scheme focuses on **attracting domestic and foreign investments** in the textile sector and enhancing global competitiveness.
 
• It also emphasizes the creation of a **world-class infrastructure ecosystem** for the textile industry, integrating spinning, weaving, dyeing, and garmenting facilities.

• India is the **second-largest exporter of textiles** and apparel globally.
 
• The textile and apparel sector contributes approximately **2.3% to India’s GDP** and 11% to total merchandise exports.
 
• It provides employment to over **45 million people** directly and 100 million indirectly.
 
 
 
• **Features of PM-MITRA Scheme:**
 
 
• The parks will be developed on the **hub-and-spoke model**, integrating textile value chains.
 
• The scheme offers **financial support of up to ₹500 crores per park** from the central government.
 
• It promotes sustainability by incorporating **environmental and green manufacturing practices**.
 
 
 
• **Global Competitiveness:**
 
 
• The scheme is aligned with the government’s goal to make India a **global textile hub**.

question: What was the objective of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan?

options.text: Creating jobs in the rural sector

solution:
The correct answer is __**Achieving universal sanitation coverage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission) was launched by PM Narendra Modi on **2nd October 2014**, coinciding with Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary.
 
• The primary objective of the mission was to **achieve universal sanitation coverage** and eliminate open defecation in India.
 
• The campaign aimed to construct toilets in rural and urban areas to provide access to safe and hygienic sanitation facilities.
 
• It encouraged behavioral changes among citizens to adopt proper sanitation practices and maintain cleanliness in their surroundings.
 
• The Swachh Bharat Mission is divided into two sub-missions: **Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)** and **Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)**, targeting urban and rural areas respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Open Defecation Free (ODF) Status:**

 
 
• Under the Swachh Bharat Mission, villages, towns, and cities were declared Open Defecation Free (ODF) upon achieving 100% toilet coverage.
 
• ODF+ and ODF++ statuses were introduced to focus on sustained sanitation practices and cleanliness beyond toilet construction.
 
 
 
• **Behavioral Change Campaigns:**
 
 
• The mission emphasized mass awareness campaigns to promote hygiene and sanitation.
 
• Programs like "Darwaza Band" and collaboration with celebrities were used to spread awareness regarding toilet usage.
 
 
 
• **Financial Support:**
 
 
• In rural areas, financial assistance was provided for the construction of individual household toilets under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin).
 
• Various state governments also supplemented central funds to ensure the success of the mission.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• According to government data, more than 10 crore toilets were constructed across India under the mission.
 
• The initiative significantly contributed to reducing health issues caused by poor sanitation and unhygienic practices.

question: Which government scheme aims to phase out unfit and polluting vehicles from India's roads to reduce emissions and boost automotive industry recycling?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Voluntary Vehicle Fleet Modernisation Programme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Voluntary Vehicle Fleet Modernisation Programme (V-VMP), also known as the **Vehicle Scrappage Policy**, was introduced by the Government of India in **2021**.
 
• The policy aims to phase out **unfit, old, and polluting vehicles** to reduce environmental pollution and improve road safety.
 
• It mandates fitness tests for commercial vehicles older than **15 years** and private vehicles older than **20 years**.
 
• Unfit vehicles that fail the fitness test or are not re-registered will be scrapped, promoting the recycling of automotive materials.
 
• The initiative is expected to **boost demand in the automotive industry** by encouraging the purchase of new, fuel-efficient, and cleaner vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fitness Tests:**

 
 
• Mandatory automated fitness tests are conducted at **Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities (RVSFs)**.
 
• These tests ensure vehicles meet minimum environmental and safety standards.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of the Policy:**
 
 
• Reduction in air pollution caused by older, high-emission vehicles.
 
• Promotion of recycling industries, creating economic and environmental benefits.
 
• Fuel savings through the use of modern, fuel-efficient vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Incentives for Vehicle Owners:**
 
 
• Owners of scrapped vehicles are offered incentives like **tax concessions** and discounts on the purchase of new vehicles.
 
• Scrappage certificates issued to vehicle owners can be redeemed for benefits while buying new vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Automotive Industry:**
 
 
• The policy is expected to increase demand for new vehicles, leading to growth in the automotive sector.
 
• It supports the Make in India initiative by encouraging domestic manufacturing.

question: What is the main focus of the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) scheme launched in 2015?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Girl child survival & education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)** scheme was launched on **22 January 2015** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Panipat, Haryana.
 
• The main objective of the scheme is to address the declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)** and promote the survival, protection, and education of the girl child.
 
• The initiative is a tri-ministerial effort involving the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**, the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, and the **Ministry of Education** (formerly MHRD).
 
• The scheme focuses on generating awareness and improving the efficiency of welfare services intended for girls across India.
 
• **District-level implementation:** The scheme was initially implemented in 100 districts with a low Child Sex Ratio and later expanded to cover all districts in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):** CSR refers to the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the 0-6 age group. A decline in CSR reflects social issues such as gender-based discrimination and female foeticide.
 
• **Key Components of BBBP:**
 
 
• **Advocacy and media campaigns:** To create awareness and change societal attitudes towards the girl child.
 
• **Multi-sectoral interventions:** In targeted districts to ensure access to education and health services for girls.
 
• **Monitoring:** Regular monitoring of CSR and other indicators to evaluate the scheme's impact.
 
 
 
• **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY):** A savings scheme under BBBP that promotes financial security for the girl child by offering attractive interest rates and tax benefits.
 
• **Impact of BBBP:** The scheme has led to significant improvements in CSR in several districts, increased enrollment of girls in schools, and enhanced awareness about gender equality.
 
• **Global Perspective:** BBBP aligns with the United Nations' **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 5 (Gender Equality) and Goal 4 (Quality Education).

• **Mission Shakti** is an integrated women empowerment programme launched by the Government of India in 2022.
 
• The programme is implemented by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** (MoWCD).
 
• It aims to promote gender equality and provide support for women's safety, security, and empowerment.
 
• The scheme includes two key sub-schemes: **Samarthya** (focusing on women’s empowerment) and **Sambal** (focusing on women’s safety and security).
 
• The scheme consolidates various existing initiatives and introduces new measures to address issues faced by women comprehensively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samarthya Sub-Scheme:** Focuses on women’s empowerment through skill development, education, and livelihood opportunities.
 
• **Sambal Sub-Scheme:** Aims to ensure safety and security for women through initiatives like One Stop Centres (OSCs), Women Helplines, and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.
 
• **One Stop Centres (OSCs):** Provide integrated support and assistance to women affected by violence in both private and public spaces.
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao:** A component of Mission Shakti focused on addressing the declining child sex ratio and promoting the education of the girl child.
 
• **National Database on Women:** A proposed initiative under Mission Shakti to improve data collection and monitoring related to women’s welfare schemes.

question: What is the purpose of the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' scheme ?

options.text: Saving and educating the girl child

solution:
The correct answer is __**Saving and educating the girl child**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** (BBBP) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India in **January 2015**.
 
• The primary aim of the scheme is to address the declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)** and promote the survival, protection, and education of the girl child.
 
• It is a joint initiative by three ministries: **Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD)**, **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)**, and **Ministry of Education (MoE).**
 
• The scheme focuses on **community-level engagement** and awareness campaigns to challenge societal norms and discrimination against girls.
 
• It also emphasizes **ensuring girls' access to quality education** and improving their overall status in society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):** CSR refers to the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the age group of 0–6 years. As per the 2011 Census, the CSR in India was 919, indicating a declining trend.
 
• **Implementation Strategy:** The scheme operates in **multi-sectoral districts** with poor CSR, focusing on community mobilization, institutional support, and stringent enforcement of laws like the **PCPNDT Act** (Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act).
 
• **Increased Awareness:** BBBP has popularized slogans like **"Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao"** and campaigns that encourage gender equality and educate parents about the importance of girls' education.
 
• **Key Achievements:** The scheme has led to an improvement in CSR in certain districts and increased enrollment of girls in schools, particularly at the secondary level.
 
• **Related Programs:** BBBP is synergized with other schemes like **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana** (a savings scheme for girl children) to provide financial security and encourage education.

question:
Which of the following is true about the Voluntary Vehicle Fleet Modernisation Programme?

1. It promotes scrapping of old vehicles to reduce emissions.

2. The 'Ministry of Road Transport and Highways' is the nodal agency.

3. The scheme incentivizes buyers of fuel-efficient new vehicles only in urban areas.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Voluntary Vehicle Fleet Modernisation Programme (VVMP)** is an initiative launched by the **Government of India** to reduce vehicular emissions and improve fuel efficiency.
 
• The programme aims to promote the scrapping of **old, inefficient, and polluting vehicles** to replace them with new, fuel-efficient, and environment-friendly vehicles.
 
• The nodal agency for implementing this programme is the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH).**
 
• This initiative is in line with India’s commitment to reducing **carbon emissions** and transitioning to a greener economy.
 
• There is no restriction under the VVMP that incentives for purchasing new vehicles are limited only to **urban areas**. The programme applies nationwide, covering both urban and rural regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Explanation of Option 3 (Incorrect)**__

 __
 
• The statement in Option 3 incorrectly states that the scheme incentivizes buyers of fuel-efficient vehicles **only in urban areas.**
 
• However, the programme is applicable nationwide, and there is no urban-only restriction on incentives.
 
 
 
• **Importance of VVMP**__
 
 
• The VVMP is critical for addressing India’s growing problem of **air pollution,** especially in cities where vehicular emissions are a significant contributor.
 
• The programme also contributes to the **recycling** of materials such as steel and aluminum from scrapped vehicles, promoting a circular economy.
 
• This initiative aligns with global efforts to combat **climate change** and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

question: Which of the following is a key focus area of the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Multi-modal connectivity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan** is a transformative initiative by the Government of India aimed at improving **infrastructure planning and implementation.**
 
• The focus is on **multi-modal connectivity**, which integrates various modes of transport—such as roadways, railways, waterways, and airways—to ensure seamless movement of goods and people.
 
• This plan aims to reduce **logistics costs**, enhance supply chain efficiency, and boost **economic growth.**
 
• It leverages **geospatial technology** and digital tools to create a unified platform for better coordination among ministries and state governments.
 
• The initiative also seeks to address issues like **delayed infrastructure projects** and overlapping efforts by different departments.
 
• By ensuring synchronized development, the plan contributes to improving the **global competitiveness of Indian industries.**
 
• The target sectors include **transportation, energy, manufacturing, and urban development.**
 
• The PM Gati Shakti framework aligns with India's **vision of becoming a $5 trillion economy** by enhancing connectivity and infrastructure development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rural electrification**__

 __
 
• **Rural electrification** is a critical initiative to provide electricity access to rural households and villages.
 
• India has implemented programs such as **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana** to improve electricity distribution in rural areas.
 
• While important for development, it is not the focus area of the **PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan**.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural subsidies**__
 __
 
• **Agricultural subsidies** are financial aids provided by governments to support farmers and agriculture-related activities.
 
• These subsidies aim to reduce input costs and enhance productivity in farming.
 
• However, they are not directly related to **multi-modal connectivity**, which is the key focus of the PM Gati Shakti initiative.
 
 
 
• **Urban development**__
 
 
• **Urban development** focuses on improving infrastructure, housing, and services within cities and towns.
 
• Although urban development is a significant area, the **PM Gati Shakti** plan has a broader scope that includes multi-modal connectivity across both urban and rural areas.

question: What is the aim of Ayushman Bharat scheme?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Health insurance for the poor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ayushman Bharat** is a flagship health insurance scheme launched by the Government of India under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **free health insurance coverage of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year** for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
 
• It targets **vulnerable and economically weaker sections** of society, specifically 10.74 crore poor and deprived rural families and identified occupational categories of urban workers.
 
• The program is officially known as the **Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)**.
 
• The scheme is fully financed by the Government of India and is considered the **world's largest government-funded health assurance program.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Benefits:**

 
 
• It covers hospitalization expenses for almost all secondary and tertiary medical conditions.
 
• AB-PMJAY includes pre- and post-hospitalization expenses, diagnostic tests, and medicines.
 
• Over 1,400 procedures are covered under the scheme across public and private empanelled hospitals.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility:**
 
 
• Eligibility is determined based on the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data.
 
• There is no restriction on family size, age, or gender under this scheme.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The National Health Authority (NHA) is the apex body responsible for implementing the scheme.
 
• Beneficiaries receive an e-card that allows them to access cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• As of 2023, the scheme has positively impacted millions of families by ensuring financial protection against high medical costs.
 
• It is a critical step towards achieving the goal of universal health coverage in India.

question: Which of the following schemes provides annual income support to farmers directly into their bank accounts?

The correct answer is __**PM-KISAN**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **PM-KISAN** stands for **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi**, a flagship scheme of the Indian government.
 
• Under this scheme, the government provides **income support of Rs. 6,000 per year** to all eligible small and marginal farmers.
 
• The amount is directly transferred into the **bank accounts of beneficiaries** in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 each.
 
• It was launched on **24th February 2019** by PM Narendra Modi in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The scheme aims to ensure **financial stability and reduce the economic distress** faced by farmers, particularly those owning cultivable land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eligibility for PM-KISAN:**

 
 
• All landholding farmer families with cultivable landholding in their names are eligible.
 
• However, institutional landholders, taxpayers, and professionals like doctors, engineers, and government employees are excluded.
 
 
 
• **Funding and Implementation:**
 
 
• The scheme is **fully funded by the central government** and is implemented across India, including Union Territories.
 
• State governments are responsible for identifying and verifying beneficiaries.
 
 
 
• **Benefits:**
 
 
• Direct cash transfer to farmers helps in reducing dependency on informal credit and strengthens rural financial infrastructure.
 
• The scheme supports improved agricultural productivity and income stability.
 
 
 
• **Technology Integration:**
 
 
• The scheme utilizes technology and the Aadhaar database for beneficiary identification and fund transfer.
 
• This ensures **transparency and minimizes duplication** in disbursal.

question: Which of the following is the central objective of Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 scheme?

options.text: Strengthening early childhood care and nutrition delivery systems

solution:
The correct answer is __**Strengthening early childhood care and nutrition delivery systems**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0** scheme aims to strengthen **early childhood care, nutrition delivery, and development**.
 
• It integrates the **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), Poshan Abhiyaan, and Scheme for Adolescent Girls** for a comprehensive approach to nutrition and care.
 
• The scheme focuses on **malnutrition eradication** by providing supplementary nutrition to children (0-6 years), pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• **Modernization of Anganwadi centers** is a key component, ensuring better infrastructure and services for early childhood care.
 
• The initiative emphasizes **community participation** and behavioral change to address nutrition challenges at the grassroots level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS):**

 
 
• Launched in 1975, it is one of the world’s largest programs aimed at providing food, preschool education, and primary healthcare to children under 6 years and their mothers.
 
• It includes immunization, health check-ups, and referral services.
 
 
 
• **Poshan Abhiyaan:**
 
 
• Also known as the National Nutrition Mission, it was launched in March 2018 to address malnutrition through a life-cycle approach.
 
• It aims to reduce stunting, undernutrition, anemia, and low birth weight among children.
 
 
 
• **Anganwadi Centres:**
 
 
• These are village-level child care centers established under ICDS to deliver nutrition, education, and health services.
 
• Modernization efforts under Saksham Anganwadi include smart learning modules, better sanitation, and hygienic food preparation.
 
 
 
• **Malnutrition in India:**
 
 
• According to the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), stunting affects 35.5% of children under 5 years in India.
 
• The scheme aims to address root causes such as inadequate dietary intake and poor maternal nutrition.

question: Which Ministry implemented the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)?
solution:
The correct answer is the Ministry of Rural Development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aajeevika - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) was launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development** (MoRD), **Government of India** i**n June 2011.**
 
• NRLM aims to alleviate rural poverty and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for the rural poor.
 
• NRLM set out with an agenda to cover **7 Crore** rural poor households, across **600 districts, 6000 blocks, 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats and 6 lakh villages** in the country through self-managed **Self Help Groups (SHGs) **and federated institutions and support them for livelihoods collectives in a period of **8-10 years**.
 
• The scheme is an improved version of the earlier **Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY).**
 
• The program is supported partially by the **World Bank**.
 
• In November **2015**, the program was renamed **Deendayal Antayodaya Yojana (DAY-NRLM).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Sub-schemes under NRLM-

 
• **Aajeevika Grameen Express Yojana (AGEY)**

 
 
• This scheme was initiated in 2017.
 
• It aims at providing alternative sources of livelihood to members of SHGs under the parent scheme by enabling them to offer public transport services in backward rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP)**
 
 
• The main objective of this sub-scheme is to empower women in agriculture by making systematic investments to enhance their participation and productivity.
 
• The program also seeks to create and sustain agriculture-based livelihoods concerning women in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP)**
 
 
• The objective of this sub-scheme is to promote startups in rural areas.
 
• SVEP envisions the generation of sustainable self-employment opportunities for rural poor youth, facilitating them to engage effectively with the market and help generate wealth locally.
 
 
 
• **National Rural Livelihoods Project (NRLP)**
 
 
• The NRLP is designed to create ‘proof of concept’ and build capacities at the central and state levels, to have a facilitating environment for all states and UTs to transit to the NRLM.

question: Which of the following states emerged as a champion state under the Van Dhan Vikas Yojana in 2021?

__
 
• Manipur emerged as a champion state under the Van Dhan Vikas Yojana in 2021 due to its effective implementation of the scheme.
 
• The state set up numerous Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) to empower tribal communities by promoting value addition to forest products.
 
• Manipur's success was driven by its focus on capacity building, skill development, and market linkages for tribal entrepreneurs.
 
• The state has a significant tribal population that benefited from the initiatives aimed at improving their socio-economic status.

• The scheme aims to improve the livelihood of tribal communities by establishing VDVKs for value addition, branding, and marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP).
 
• Tribal communities are encouraged to collect, process, and sell forest products to enhance their income.
 
• The scheme also focuses on skill upgradation and capacity building among tribal members to create sustainable livelihoods.
 
 
 
• **Minor Forest Produce (MFP)**
 
 
• MFP includes all non-timber forest products such as bamboo, tamarind, honey, and medicinal plants.
 
• These products are crucial for the subsistence and economy of tribal communities.
 
• The collection and sale of MFPs provide significant income to tribal families, especially in forest-rich regions.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED)**

• Its primary objective is to promote the socio-economic development of tribal communities through marketing development activities.
 
• TRIFED assists in the creation of market linkages for tribal products, ensuring fair trade and better income for tribal producers.

question:
73 Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN) system?

1. ULPIN assigns a unique ID to every land parcel in India.

2. ULPIN is a 14-digit identification number.

3. ULPIN helps track land ownership and resolve disputes.

4. ULPIN is only for urban areas and not rural land.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1) 1, 2, and 3 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN)** provides a 14-digit alphanumeric ID to uniquely identify every land parcel in India.
 
• ULPIN is designed to improve transparency in land ownership and facilitate seamless integration of land records across states.
 
• The system helps in the resolution of disputes related to land ownership and ensures proper tracking of land transactions.
 
• ULPIN is applicable to both **rural and urban land parcels**, contrary to the incorrect statement that it is only for urban areas.
 
• It is a step towards the digitization of land records under the **Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP):**

 
 
• Launched in 2008, DILRMP aims to digitize and modernize land records to enhance efficiency, transparency, and dispute resolution.
 
• It involves the integration of property registration with land records and cadastral maps.
 
 
 
• **ULPIN Implementation:**
 
 
• ULPIN is being rolled out in a phased manner across Indian states and union territories.
 
• It is expected to be a single source of information for any land parcel, accessible through a centralized database.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of ULPIN:**
 
 
• Reduction in land disputes through accurate identification and ownership tracking.
 
• Improved ease of doing business as it simplifies land-related transactions.
 
• Better targeting and implementation of government schemes linked to land.
 
 
 
• **Land Reforms in India:**
 
 
• Land reforms aim to address issues like land ownership inequality, tenancy regulation, and consolidation of fragmented land holdings.
 
• Digitization initiatives like ULPIN play a key role in modernizing and streamlining land governance.

question: Which principle of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ensures that entities collecting personal data must obtain explicit consent from individuals?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Notice and Choice Framework**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Notice and Choice Framework** is a principle of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, ensuring that personal data collection entities must obtain explicit consent from individuals before collecting their data.
 
• The framework mandates that individuals must be provided with clear and concise notices regarding the purpose of data collection and their rights under the law.
 
• Under this principle, data fiduciaries are legally obligated to ensure that users fully understand how their data will be used before granting consent.
 
• Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, and revocable at any time to uphold the framework's integrity.
 
• This principle is crucial in empowering data principals (individuals) with control over their personal data in alignment with global data protection practices such as the GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023**

 
 
• This act focuses on protecting personal data while ensuring the responsible use of data by fiduciaries.
 
• It adopts a principles-based approach, including aspects such as purpose limitation, data minimization, and accountability.
 
• The act introduces penalties for data breaches and non-compliance to ensure adherence to its provisions.
 
 
 
• **Purpose Limitation**
 
 
• Entities can only process personal data for specific, clear, and lawful purposes communicated to the data principal at the time of collection.
 
• This ensures that data is not misused for purposes beyond what was agreed upon.
 
 
 
• **Data Fiduciary**
 
 
• A data fiduciary is any entity (individual, company, or organization) that determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.
 
• They are required to act responsibly and transparently while handling personal data.
 
 
 
• **Data Principal**
 
 
• The data principal refers to the individual whose personal data is being collected, stored, or processed.
 
• They have rights such as the right to access, correct, and erase their personal data under the act.
 
 
 
• **Global Context**
 
 
• The Notice and Choice Framework in India aligns with global data protection standards such as the GDPR (EU) and CCPA (California), emphasizing informed and explicit consent.
 
• This ensures that Indian data protection laws are in harmony with international practices.

**Given below are two statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read and mark the correct options:

Assertion (A):**

The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, promotes e-filing and virtual trials to expedite the justice delivery system.

**Reason (R):**

The integration of technology aims to reduce case pendency and enhance accessibility to justice.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, is part of the reforms aimed at modernizing the criminal justice delivery system in India.
 
• The Sanhita promotes e-filing of cases and virtual trials to facilitate faster and more efficient legal proceedings.
 
• Virtual trials aim to reduce logistical challenges and expedite the resolution of pending cases in the courts.
 
• Technological integration under BNSS is designed to enhance accessibility to justice, especially for remote and marginalized communities.
 
• The focus is on leveraging technology to address case backlogs and improve overall transparency in the justice system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **E-filing:** Refers to the electronic submission of legal documents, enabling litigants and lawyers to file cases online without physical visits to the court.
 
• **Virtual Trials:** These are court proceedings conducted via video conferencing or other digital platforms, ensuring continuity of justice even during emergencies like pandemics.
 
• **Case Pendency:** India’s judicial system faces a significant backlog of cases, with millions of cases pending across various courts, making swift reforms necessary.
 
• **Accessibility to Justice:** Leveraging technology makes the justice system more inclusive, reducing barriers for people in rural areas or those with limited resources.
 
• **Judicial Reforms:** BNSS, 2023, is part of a series of legislative updates aimed at modernizing colonial-era laws, such as replacing the Indian Penal Code (IPC), Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), and Evidence Act.

question: Shobhana Ranade's legacy as a Gandhian is most closely aligned with which contemporary governance initiative?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shobhana Ranade was a dedicated Gandhian known for her commitment to social welfare and community development, resonating with the principles of cleanliness, sanitation, and grassroots empowerment.
 
• Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 2, 2014, emphasizes cleanliness and sanitation, aligning closely with Gandhian ideals of self-reliance and hygiene.
 
• The mission aims to eliminate open defecation and improve waste management in both rural and urban areas, addressing foundational societal issues that Gandhian philosophy advocates resolving.
 
• Shobhana Ranade’s legacy of community-driven initiatives mirrors the participatory approach of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, where citizens are actively engaged in improving their surroundings.
 
• The campaign is a tribute to Mahatma Gandhi's vision of a clean and self-sufficient India, making it highly relevant to Gandhian principles and Ranade's lifelong work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan:**

 
 
• It is a nationwide cleanliness campaign initiated by the Government of India with the goal of achieving universal sanitation coverage.
 
• The mission has two sub-components: Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) for rural areas and Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) for cities and towns.
 
• By 2019, India was declared open-defecation free (ODF), a milestone achieved under this campaign.
 
 
 
• **Gandhian Philosophy on Cleanliness:**
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi often emphasized the importance of sanitation, stating, "Sanitation is more important than independence."
 
• He believed cleanliness was essential for individual dignity and societal progress.
 
• Gandhian principles advocate community participation and local solutions to improve hygiene and living standards.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan:**
 
 
• Construction of household toilets with subsidies provided to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families.
 
• Promotion of awareness campaigns to encourage behavioral changes regarding hygiene practices.
 
• Improved waste management systems to ensure proper disposal and recycling.
 
 
 
• **Role of Civil Society:**
 
 
• Civil society organizations, like the ones Shobhana Ranade has been associated with, play a pivotal role in supporting Swachh Bharat initiatives.
 
• Community-led efforts ensure sustainable and effective implementation of cleanliness drives.
